pub.passage: Anniversaries matter to me. Ten years after my first novel appeared, I wanted a dinner on the harbor, speeches, a printed card with both our names. Eulalio, who had carried my sentences into English through three books, wanted nothing. We argued on the stairwell of my lodging on the Cornish coast, I on the landing, he two steps below, the skylight rattling in the sea wind. I reminded him that reviewers had praised the music of the English pages, and that he had asked for his name to be printed small on the title page, then smaller. He said that was rather the point. His part, he told me, had always been a lamp in the next room: enough to read by, never meant to be looked at. I wanted to argue that lamps can be thanked. Instead I asked him to write the card himself, in whatever size he liked. Overhead, a gull walked the slate roof, its claws scraping at every step.

pub.passage: Rain drums on the galvanized roof, and the lamp smells of coconut oil and scorched wick. Each night Roshane sits across from you and copies your pages into his ledger, the French on the left, your English on the right, his pen scratching long after you have gone to bed. You had expected him to arrive with objections; his own novels sold better than yours in Paris. When you ask why he has not gone back down to Port of Spain, Linton, he says the road below the cocoa estate is washed out. Perhaps it is. Yet the boy who brought his mule up the hill led it home on Tuesday, a full day before the first rain. And the publisher's letter, the one asking for forty pages to be cut, is no longer on the shelf where you left it. On Sunday morning you find his finished ledger beside your inkwell, every chapter intact, its spine tied with your own blue ribbon.

pub.passage: Urban planners examining the history of Curitiba, Brazil's bus rapid transit (BRT) system have noted an unusual design choice: the system's tubular, cylindrical boarding stations, in which passengers pay fares and wait before buses arrive, rather than paying on board. Historical records show that when the BRT system was first proposed in the early 1970s, the city's municipal budget could not accommodate the cost of building an underground subway network, yet planners still wanted a system that could move as many passengers per hour as a subway. Engineers found that the primary source of delay in conventional bus systems was not travel time between stops but the time spent boarding, since drivers had to wait for each passenger to pay and find a seat one at a time. The tubular stations were designed so that fare collection and platform-level boarding occur before the bus arrives, allowing passengers to enter through multiple wide doors simultaneously, much like on a subway train. Ridership data collected after the stations opened showed that average boarding time per bus fell from roughly forty-five seconds to under twenty seconds, even though the buses themselves were not redesigned and the distance between stops remained unchanged. Taken together, this evidence suggests that the tubular stations were designed to ______.

pub.passage:
Text 1
Marine biologists studying octopus cognition have proposed that these animals possess a form of intelligence comparable to that of many vertebrates, despite octopuses having a nervous system structured almost nothing like a mammal's. Two-thirds of an octopus's neurons are distributed throughout its arms rather than centralized in a brain, yet octopuses solve puzzle boxes, recognize individual human faces, and use tools such as coconut shells for shelter. Because these behaviors require flexible problem-solving rather than fixed instinctive responses, researchers argue that intelligence can evolve along radically different neural architectures and should not be measured by how closely an animal's brain resembles our own.

Text 2
While octopuses undeniably display impressive behavioral flexibility, some cognitive scientists caution against equating this flexibility with intelligence in the sense usually reserved for vertebrates. An octopus's arms can each act with a degree of autonomy, solving local problems like gripping or exploring without input from the central brain at all. This decentralization means that what looks like unified, deliberate problem-solving may actually be the aggregate of many semi-independent local reactions. Attributing a single, coherent intelligence to the whole animal, these researchers suggest, may overstate the case and obscure how differently octopus cognition is actually organized compared to centralized vertebrate brains.

pub.passage: We never reached the far wall that summer, though Dario spoke of it each morning as if distance were only another word to learn. He sat on the rim of the salt pool in Havana, trousers rolled, and named things in the language of his village: tile, gull, the green rust on the ladder. Bartolo repeated each word and swam a length before the next. On Thursday she stopped short of the far wall, held the rope, and came back saying she had only wanted to rest. Dario nodded and gave her the word for rest, then a second, older word that he said meant resting before one has finished. She practiced it without asking why. Later, reciting the colors, he paused at the word for the rust, and let her supply it, which she did loudly, as though he had been testing her. On the walk home she carried his towel over her shoulder, still damp at one corner where the rope had dripped on it.

pub.answer_rationale: "Launching" is a participial phrase that logically modifies the entire preceding clause (the discovery), correctly indicating the result of that discovery without introducing a second subject.
pub.evidence_span: astronomers eventually realized that these signals came not from any terrestrial source but from cataclysmic events far beyond the solar system, ______ the field of gamma-ray burst astronomy.
pub.explanation: 빈칸 앞 절 전체가 새로운 학문 분야를 만들어냈다는 결과를 나타내야 하므로 정동사 없는 분사구 "launching"이 적절하다. "and this launching"은 등위접속사 뒤에 정동사가 없고, "they launched"는 콤마로 독립절을 이어 붙이며 대명사가 불분명하고, "which had launched"는 시제가 맞지 않고 "the solar system"을 수식하는 것으로 오독된다. 정답은 C.
pub.explanation_en: The clause before the blank as a whole needs to be shown as having resulted in a new field of study, so the participial phrase "launching" appropriately modifies the entire preceding clause. "And this launching" has no finite verb after a coordinating conjunction; "they launched" splices two independent clauses with a comma and has an unclear pronoun; "which had launched" has a mismatched tense and can be misread as modifying "the solar system." Therefore, C is correct.
options: and this launching
they launched
launching
which had launched

Later, when the card she had written in advance in both their names is read aloud, it becomes clear that the earlier "mistake" was actually meant to avoid being repaid. Therefore, B, which states the main idea through the relationship between the two events, is the answer. A summarizes only the first event, C only the later one, and D reverses the causality by treating the mix-up as the cause of the card, ignoring the clue that the card was prepared in advance.
options: A nephew's attempt to repay an old loan goes awry at a crowded wedding.

A shared card at a wedding shows that the aunt and nephew have grown close.
An aunt's confusion at the wedding leads her to write a card in both names.
pub.passage: Tromso in June never gets dark, and the wedding hall had its curtains open to a sky that refused to end the evening. I had come with an envelope in my jacket: the eight thousand kroner my aunt Wilhelmina had lent me eleven years earlier, when I was nineteen and stranded in Bergen without a ticket home. I found her near the cake table and pressed it into her hand. She looked at the envelope, thanked me for being so generous to the bride, and dropped it into the white box of cards by the door before I could explain. I stood there with my mouth open. Her old wristwatch, I noticed, had stopped at twenty past four, and she did not wind it all night. Hours later, during the speeches, the bride read aloud a card that had been tucked into my envelope, a card I had not written, thanking Devon and Wilhelmina together for their gift. Across the room my aunt raised her glass toward me and turned back to her conversation.

pub.explanation:
정답 B: Venkataraman의 결론은 '전압과 유속을 함께 조절하면 섬유를 가늘게 할 수 있다'는 것이지만, 이 결론은 전기장이 강해질수록 제트가 그만큼 더 늘어난다는 가정에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 일정 문턱을 넘으면 전압을 높여도 늘어나는 단계가 길어지지 않고 제트가 불안정해진다고 보여 주므로, 바로 이 가정을 겨냥한다.
A: 결론 자체를 가리킨다. Text 2는 결론을 간접적으로 약하게 만들지만, 그 근거는 결론이 기대는 가정을 깨뜨리는 데 있다. 또한 Text 2는 유속을 낮추는 쪽은 인정하므로, 결론 전체를 반박한다고 보기 어렵다.
C: 실험 조건이라는 부수적 세부이다. Text 2는 용액 종류나 온도를 전혀 언급하지 않는다.
D: Text 2는 유속을 적당히 줄이면 대체로 섬유가 가늘어진다고 말하므로, 오히려 이 점에 동의한다.
pub.explanation_en:
B is correct. Venkataraman's conclusion rests on an assumption: that a stronger field always stretches the jet more. Text 2 shows that above a threshold, raising the voltage does not lengthen the stretching phase. Instead, the jet whips and splits into several jets, so this assumption is exactly what Text 2 undermines.
A states the conclusion itself. Text 2 weakens the conclusion only indirectly, by attacking the assumption beneath it. It also accepts the point about flow rate, so it doesn't reject the conclusion outright.
C is an incidental detail of the experiments. Text 2 never mentions the solution type or the temperature.
D is something Text 2 actually agrees with: it says a modest reduction in flow rate generally gives finer fibers.
options: The claim that fiber diameter can be reliably minimized by adjusting voltage and flow rate together
The idea that each increase in field strength produces a corresponding increase in how far the jet is drawn out
The decision to conduct the tests with a single polyvinyl alcohol solution kept at room temperature
The view that delivering less solution per second to the needle tends to yield finer fibers
pub.passage:
Text 1
In electrospinning, a high voltage draws a charged polymer solution from a needle into a thin jet that stretches and dries into nanofibers. Materials engineer Priya Venkataraman argues that fiber diameter can be reliably minimized by tuning just two dials: raising voltage while lowering flow rate. Her reasoning is that a stronger electric field pulls harder on the jet, and that this added stretching, applied to less fluid per second, must translate directly into thinner fibers. Her lab's tests used a single polyvinyl alcohol solution at room temperature.

Text 2
A team led by Tomás Ferreira measured jet behavior directly with high-speed imaging. Like other groups, they found that a modest reduction in flow rate generally yields finer fibers. But beyond a moderate threshold, increasing voltage did not lengthen the stretching phase; instead, the jet began whipping erratically and ejecting from several points on the droplet at once, producing fibers with widely scattered and often larger diameters. The added field strength, the team concluded, changes how the jet forms rather than simply how much it is drawn out.

advisory.note: 정답 B는 Text 2가 직접 반박하는 가정(전기장 세기에 비례해 제트가 더 늘어난다는 것)이다. A는 결론이며, Text 2가 '전압+유속을 함께 조절'한다는 결론의 유속 부분에는 동의하므로 결론 전체를 반박한다고 보기 어렵다. 다만 A도 부분적으로 매력적이어서 변별력은 충분하지만 약간의 모호성 위험이 있다. D는 Text 2가 동의하는 부분, C는 Text 2와 무관하다.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 결론(전압↑·유속↓로 섬유 직경 최소화)과 근거(전기장이 강할수록 제트가 더 늘어남 + 유속 감소)가 명확히 구분되고, 실험 조건(단일 PVA 용액·실온)은 부수 정보로 배치됨. Text 2는 유속 감소 효과에는 동의(D=동의 오답)하고 문턱 이상 전압에서는 늘어남 단계가 길어지지 않고 제트 형성 방식이 바뀐다고 하여 B의 가정과만 정면 충돌함. 정답 B는 결론이 아닌 가정이며 해설도 수치·논리 모순 없음. A는 결론 자체를 가리키는 함정으로 '함께 조절'이라는 방향 비명시 표현 덕에 Text 2가 절반(유속)은 인정하므로 '가장' 겨냥하는 요소로는 B가 우세하나, 'reliably minimized'가 Text 2에 의해 실질적으로 약화되는 점에서 A의 흡인력이 다소 강한 편임(결정적 결함은 아님). 전기방사에서 고전압 시 whipping 불안정·다중 제트 발생은 실제 문헌과 부합. 두 텍스트 입장을 종합하고 Text 2의 반응을 추론하며 결론/가정/조건의 강도를 가려야 하므로 hard 적합.

pub.question: Based on the texts, which element of Venkataraman's argument in Text 1 would Ferreira's team (Text 2) most likely challenge?

pub.answer_rationale: C는 while이 이끄는 종속절 안에 정동사 lacked와 moved를 완전하게 갖추어 문법적으로 완결된 대조절을 만든다.
pub.evidence_span: the compass sense appeared only in turtles older than five years, ______ juveniles tracked in the same study drifted passively with currents
pub.explanation: 빈칸 앞뒤는 대조되는 두 절을 연결해야 하는 구조로, 접속사 while이 이끄는 절 안에는 완전한 정동사(주어+정동사)가 있어야 문법적으로 완성된 문장이 된다. B는 "while the younger animals ... lacked ... and moved ..."로, while절 안에 정동사 lacked와 moved가 병렬적으로 완결되어 있어 문법적으로 올바르며, 성체와 대비되는 유생의 행동을 논리적으로 제시한다. A는 접속사 and 뒤에 분사 relying만 있어 정동사가 없는 비문(dangling/incomplete clause)이며, 게다가 시각적 랜드마크라는 지문에 없는 정보를 도입한다. C는 while절 안에 lacking과 moving이라는 분사만 있고 정동사가 없어 문법적으로 불완전한 종속절이 된다. D는 so로 시작해 앞 문장의 "5세 이상에서만 나타났다"는 조건과 논리적으로 모순되는 내용을 도입한다. 따라서 정답은 B이다.
pub.explanation_en: The blank must join two contrasting clauses, and a clause introduced by the conjunction "while" needs a complete finite verb (subject plus finite verb) to be a grammatically complete sentence. B reads "while the younger animals ... lacked ... and moved ...," so the finite verbs "lacked" and "moved" are completed in parallel inside the while-clause, which makes it grammatically correct and logically presents the juveniles' behavior in contrast to the adults. A has only the participle "relying" after the conjunction "and," with no finite verb, making an incomplete (dangling) clause, and it also introduces information not in the passage, visual landmarks. C has only the participles "lacking" and "moving" in the while-clause, with no finite verb, creating a grammatically incomplete subordinate clause. D begins with "so" and introduces content that logically contradicts the previous sentence's condition that the behavior appeared only at age 5 and older. Therefore, the answer is B.
options: and the adult turtles, unlike the juveniles, relied entirely on visual landmarks near the coastline to navigate
while the younger animals in her sample lacked this navigational ability and moved according to current patterns alone
while the younger animals in her sample lacking this navigational ability and moving according to current patterns alone
so that the younger animals in her sample, lacking this navigational ability, moved according to current patterns alone
pub.passage: Marine biologist Sylvia Alarcón spent a decade tracking the migratory routes of leatherback sea turtles across the Pacific. Her data revealed that the turtles do not simply drift with ocean currents, as earlier researchers had assumed, but instead adjust their swimming direction in response to subtle magnetic field variations. This finding suggested that the turtles possess an internal compass sensitive enough to detect geomagnetic gradients far weaker than scientists had previously believed detectable by any marine animal. Alarcón's conclusion, however, rested on a critical qualification: the compass sense appeared only in turtles older than five years, ______.

pub.explanation_en: The first paragraph lays out a limitation: metamaterial acoustic cloaks work only within narrow frequency bands. The second paragraph explains that because of this, researchers now design cloaks that hide objects from the specific frequencies that matter in a given setting, so B is correct. A correctly mentions the negative refractive index, but it claims success at all frequencies, which is the opposite of what the text says. C uses the light origin and the submarine and factory examples, but the text never compares how well the cloaks work for those two uses. D uses the detail that the units are smaller than the waves, but nothing in the text suggests engineers abandoned acoustic cloaking.
options: Because metamaterials can produce a negative refractive index, engineers have succeeded in building acoustic cloaks that conceal objects from sound at all frequencies.
Because metamaterial cloaks perform well only over limited frequency ranges, engineers are increasingly tailoring them to block particular sounds relevant to practical uses.
Because acoustic cloaks were adapted from designs for light, engineers have found that they are more effective at hiding submarines than at reducing factory noise.
Because the resonating units in metamaterials are smaller than sound waves, engineers have abandoned acoustic cloaking in favor of cloaks that manipulate light.
pub.passage:
Engineers designing acoustic cloaks often borrow an idea first developed for light: metamaterials, structures built from repeating units smaller than the waves they manipulate, can be arranged to give a material properties no natural substance has, including a negative refractive index that bends waves the "wrong" way. By grading these properties carefully, a shell of metamaterial can steer incoming sound around an object and release it on the far side as if nothing had been in the way. Early laboratory demonstrations were striking, but they worked only within a narrow band of frequencies, because the tiny resonating units that produce the unusual behavior respond strongly to some pitches and hardly at all to others.

Researchers at several universities have therefore shifted their focus. Rather than pursuing a perfect cloak, many now design shells that hide objects from the specific frequencies that matter in a given setting, such as the sonar pulses used to locate submarines or the low hum of machinery in a factory. pub.explanation_en: Correct choice B presents together that the underdrawings were apprentice-style yet the final brushwork did not match the master's technique, and that the compositions and colors still followed the master's typical style. This precisely supports the execution-based view that stylistic consistency (composition and color) alone cannot show whether the master actually painted a work and that separate evidence of execution, namely brushwork, is needed. A is a trap: it pairs apprentice underdrawings with brushwork that matches the master, a combination in the opposite direction not in the text, and it can seem to support the stylistic view (matching composition and color is enough). C pairs master-style underdrawings with mismatched brushwork, a combination not in the text, and it undermines the reliability of the execution-based standard by shaking the correlation between underdrawing and brushwork, so it does not support that view. D presents only that composition and color match and does not mention brushwork (evidence of execution), so it actually supports the opposing view that stylistic consistency is enough.

pub.passage: Art historians examining the workshop practices of Renaissance-era painters have long questioned how much of a celebrated master's output was actually painted by the master himself rather than by assistants working under his supervision. One view holds that attribution to a given master should be based primarily on stylistic consistency—that is, a painting should be credited to the master if its brushwork, color palette, and composition closely match the master's known solo works, regardless of who physically applied the paint, since the master's design and final approval were what defined the work as "his." A competing view holds that true authorship requires evidence of the master's own hand in the actual execution, not merely his design or supervision, so a painting produced largely by assistants should not be attributed to the master even if it closely resembles his style. Conservators examining underdrawings and pigment layers of several paintings long attributed to a well-known Florentine workshop found that in works where the underlying sketch showed the confident, fluid lines characteristic of the master's documented solo drawings, the final paint layers also showed brushstroke patterns matching his known technique. By contrast, in paintings where the underdrawing showed the more tentative, corrected lines typical of apprentice practice, the final paint layers showed brushwork inconsistent with the master's documented technique, even though the overall composition and color choices closely followed his typical designs.

pub.passage:
Text 1
In the following excerpt from a novel, Masako, the daughter of a fisherman in an Edo-period coastal village, practices net-weaving. A marriage to a merchant in the castle town has already been arranged for her, though her father does not know she has accepted it.
Her father guided her fingers through the knot again, his calloused thumb pressing hers against the twine. "Tighter," he said. "A loose knot lets the whole catch slip away." Masako pulled until the cord bit her skin. She told herself she was learning only to please him, that the skill would be useless behind a merchant's counter. Yet when the finished row lay taut and even across her lap, she found she could not stop looking at it.

Text 2
A literary critic comments on the novel.
Some readers take Masako's net-weaving scenes as proof that she secretly wants to stay in the village, as if the novel were quietly arguing against her marriage. This reading overlooks how firmly the author keeps Masako's choice intact: she never wavers in her plan to leave. What the weaving scenes reveal is not a hidden wish to remain but the cost of departure—Masako can value what her father gives her and still give it up. The novel's tension lies in that coexistence, not in any reversal.

pub.answer_rationale: 'and thereby' with no punctuation correctly joins two verb phrases sharing one subject, since 'thereby' modifies 'shortens' rather than marking an independent clause boundary.
pub.evidence_span: speeds embryonic development ______ shortens the extraordinarily long incubation period
pub.explanation: 이 문장은 'warmer water'가 주어인 하나의 절 안에서 'speeds embryonic development'와 'thereby shortens the incubation period'라는 두 개의 동사구가 접속사 'and'로 연결된 구조다. 'thereby'는 뒤의 동사 'shortens'를 수식하는 부사일 뿐 독립절을 이끌지 않으므로 앞뒤에 문장부호가 필요 없다. B는 'and,' 뒤에만 쉼표를 두어 짝이 없는 쉼표가 되고, C는 'thereby' 뒤에만 쉼표를 두어 역시 짝이 없는 쉼표가 되며, D는 세미콜론으로 동사구를 독립절처럼 분리해 세미콜론의 절 경계 규칙을 어긴다. 따라서 아무 문장부호 없이 'and thereby'로 잇는 A가 정답이다.
pub.explanation_en: This sentence has two verb phrases, "speeds embryonic development" and "thereby shortens the incubation period," joined by "and" inside a single clause whose subject is "warmer water." "Thereby" is an adverb that modifies the following verb "shortens" and does not introduce an independent clause, so no punctuation is needed on either side of it. B puts a comma only after "and," which leaves an unpaired comma. C puts a comma only after "thereby," which is likewise unpaired. D uses a semicolon to separate a verb phrase as if it were an independent clause, which breaks the clause-boundary rule for semicolons. So A, which joins the phrases as "and thereby" with no punctuation, is the answer.
options: and thereby
and, thereby
and thereby,
and; thereby

difficultyReasons: 콤마+분사구문과 콤마+which 관계절의 차이를 구별해야 함(1단계)
동격 명사구 구조('a solution that offered')를 인식해야 정답을 고를 수 있음(2단계)
세미콜론 오용은 비교적 쉽게 배제 가능하나 A와 B는 정답과 형태적으로 유사해 변별이 필요함

distractors.matches: 'a solution that offered...'라는 의미와 유사한 정보를 전달함
distractors.plausibleBecause: 콤마+which는 비제한적 관계절을 도입하는 흔한 패턴이라 문법적으로 그럴듯해 보인다
distractors.whyWrong: 'elevated tracks, which offered a solution'은 elevated tracks 자체가 solution이라는 명사구 동격 구조(elevated tracks, a solution that offered...)를 관계절로 바꿔 의미가 어색해지고, 'offered a solution' 뒤에 다시 'a solution'이 오는 구조와 충돌하여 비문법적이거나 어색한 문장이 됨

distractors.matches: 분사구문 형태로 부가 설명을 붙이는 표준적 방식과 유사
distractors.plausibleBecause: 분사구 offering이 분사구문으로 문장을 자연스럽게 이어주는 것처럼 보임
distractors.whyWrong: 콤마 없이 'tracks offering a solution'이 되면 elevated tracks를 수식하는 현재분사구로 읽혀 'a solution'이 명사 보어로 붙는 원래 의도(동격: elevated tracks, a solution that...)와 달리 track 자체를 수식하는 형태가 되어, 뒤에 동격 명사구 'a solution'이 독립적으로 붙을 자리를 만들지 못함(콤마 없이 두 개의 독립 요소를 연결할 수 없음)

distractors.matches: 세미콜론 뒤에 분사구가 오는 형태가 격식있는 문장처럼 보임
distractors.plausibleBecause: 세미콜론이 두 개의 독립절을 연결하는 것으로 보여 문법적으로 정교해 보임
distractors.whyWrong: 세미콜론은 독립절과 독립절을 연결해야 하는데 뒤에 오는 'offering a solution...'은 독립절이 아니라 분사구이므로 세미콜론 사용이 문법적으로 부적절함

issues: 선택지 A(', which offered')는 실제로 문법적으로 완전히 자연스러운 비제한적 관계절 구조입니다. 'elevated tracks, which offered a solution that promised...'는 표준 영어 문법상 문제가 없으며, 'a solution'은 'offered'의 목적어로 자연스럽게 기능합니다. 해설에서 '이중 서술이 되어 어색하다'는 근거는 명확한 문법적 결함이 아니라 주관적 판단에 가깝습니다.
따라서 A와 D 모두 문법적으로 허용 가능한 구조일 수 있어, 정답이 D 하나로 유일하게 결정된다는 근거가 약합니다. 실제 SAT 스타일 문제에서는 이런 애매성을 피하기 위해 선택지 간 의미나 문법적 차이를 더 명확히 해야 합니다.

pub.explanation_en: The answer is D. The opening shows two people worn out by night shifts, bickering in short remarks, with a narrator proudly counting the dishes Genevieve rejected, so the tone is irritable. Later, in the scene where the two mothers clumsily cook each other's dishes and Genevieve, who already knows the list, mouths the number, the narrator comes to laugh sheepishly at her own fixation. B misreads the scene of handling the list as resentment, C has no basis for sorrow, and A mistakes the opening tone for cheerful anticipation.
options: From cheerful anticipation to nervous unease about how the two mothers will get along
From cool detachment to lingering resentment over the many dishes Genevieve rejected
From tense rivalry to quiet sorrow about the weeks the two women lost to arguing
From weary irritation to sheepish humor about the narrator's own grievance
pub.passage: We had argued for weeks about the table. I wanted the terrace laid the Galician way for my mother's visit, with octopus on wooden plates and bread torn by hand; Genevieve insisted on the long French lunch her grandmother used to serve, course after careful course. Both of us worked nights at the hospital, and we fought the way tired people fight, in clipped sentences over cold coffee at seven in the morning. I kept a list of every dish she rejected, and I was proud of how long it had grown. On the morning itself, both mothers arrived early. I found them in the kitchen, mine rolling crêpe batter far too thick and hers slicing octopus with a bread knife, each doing the other's dish badly and neither apologizing. I touched the list in my pocket. Seventeen items, I recalled, numbered in my neatest hand. We set out both kinds of plates, and Genevieve, catching my eye across the terrace, mouthed the number seventeen, which meant she had found it on the dresser days ago. Below us the vines dripped from the night's rain.

pub.explanation_en: The boot's split sole is glued shut every week, but a few days later it quietly splits open again. Meanwhile, the duo's audience is shrinking and they never talk about it; Sergio covers missed high notes with guitar flourishes, and Nicolas pretends not to hear. Connecting these two threads, the boot symbolizes the two men's habit of covering over their decline instead of facing it, so B is the answer. A misreads it as pride in appearance, C shifts the focus to the cobbler, and D is too general.
options: Sergio's pride in keeping up a neat appearance before the audience in the plaza
The duo's habit of covering over their decline instead of facing it openly
The cobbler's quiet loyalty to the regular customers who visit his stall
The general hardships of earning a living as street musicians in a big city
pub.passage: Years later, Nicolas would remember the boots more clearly than the songs. Every Saturday that last autumn, before their set in the plaza, Sergio left his left boot at a shoe repair stall near the cathedral in Seville, where an old cobbler glued the split sole back together without comment. The duo was drawing fewer listeners each week, though neither of them said so. Nicolas noticed that Sergio had begun to miss the high note in their closing song and to cover it with a flourish on the guitar; Nicolas, in turn, pretended not to hear. Each Saturday the cobbler held the boot up to the light, pressed the seam with his thumb, and handed it back. Each week the glue held for a few days, and then the sole began, quietly, to open again. One evening Nicolas saw Sergio wince as he stepped onto a curb, the boot gaping at the toe, and still say nothing. After the stall closed, the cobbler swept leather scraps into the gutter, where pigeons inspected them and moved on.

pub.answer_rationale: 동사 "requires"는 목적어로 동명사를 취하므로, 뒤에 이어지는 세 개의 how절을 목적어로 연결하는 "examining"만이 동사 형태 규칙에 맞고 구조적으로 자연스럽다.
pub.evidence_span: requires ______ how mechanization increased output, how railways distributed that output efficiently, and how urban labor markets supplied the workers
pub.explanation: "requires" 뒤에는 동명사가 목적어로 와야 하며 "examining"이 뒤의 세 how절을 목적어로 취한다. "to have examined", "one who examines", "examine"은 requires의 목적어 자리에 올 수 없다.
pub.explanation_en: "Requires" takes a gerund as its object, and "examining" governs the three following how-clauses. "To have examined" (perfect infinitive), "one who examines" (a person, not an action), and "examine" (a bare verb) cannot serve as the object of "requires" here.
options: to have examined
one who examines
examining
examine

distractors.plausibleBecause: examination이라는 명사와 that절을 통해 뒤따르는 내용을 자연스럽게 연결하는 것처럼 보임

pub.explanation: 지문은 단일 기포 실험으로 섬광을 정밀하게 측정할 수 있게 되었지만, 빛의 원인에 대해서는 여전히 합의가 없다는 점을 중심으로 하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 섬광 시간을 언급하지만, 섬광은 예상보다 '짧았다'고 했으므로 방향이 반대다. B는 플라스마 가설을 언급하지만, 그것은 여러 가설 중 하나일 뿐 실험으로 확인된 것이 아니다. C는 기포 구름 연구를 포기했다거나 더 밝았다는 내용을 담고 있는데, 이는 지문에 나오지 않는다.
pub.explanation_en: The text's focus is that a single-bubble setup made precise measurement of the flashes possible, but scientists still disagree about what causes the light, so D is correct. A mentions flash duration, but the text says the flashes were shorter than expected, not longer. B names the plasma idea, but the text presents it as only one of several competing explanations, not a confirmed one. C claims that researchers abandoned bubble-cloud studies and that the flashes were brighter, and the text says neither.
options: Trapping a single bubble showed that sonoluminescence flashes last far longer than earlier studies of bubble clouds had suggested.
Gaitan's single-bubble experiment confirmed that sonoluminescence results from gas heated into a glowing plasma during collapse.
Researchers abandoned the study of bubble clouds after Gaitan found that a single bubble produces brighter and more regular flashes.
Although isolating one bubble let researchers measure sonoluminescence precisely, the cause of its light remains unsettled.
pub.passage: When a liquid is blasted with intense sound waves, tiny gas bubbles can form, swell, and then collapse violently, a process called acoustic cavitation. In 1990, physicist Felipe Gaitan showed that a single bubble trapped in a flask of water by a standing sound wave could be made to collapse over and over, giving off a faint flash of blue-white light with each cycle. This effect, called sonoluminescence, had first been noticed decades earlier in clouds of bubbles, but isolating one bubble let researchers time the flashes precisely. They found that each flash lasts less than a billionth of a second, far shorter than many had expected. Yet even with this precision, researchers still disagree about what produces the light. Some argue that the collapsing bubble heats its gas enough to form a glowing plasma, while others propose that the light comes from chemical reactions or from electric charges separating at the bubble wall, and no single model yet accounts for all the measurements.

advisory.note: D는 지문의 '정밀 측정이 가능해졌다'는 내용과 '빛의 원인은 아직 정해지지 않았다'는 내용을 모두 담고 있다. A(섬광 시간이 지문과 반대 방향)와 B(여러 가설 중 하나를 확정된 것처럼 진술)는 지문 일부에 근거가 있어 비교해야 배제된다. C는 근거가 약해 쉽게 배제되지만 그럴듯하게 읽힌다. Gaitan(1990)의 단일 기포 실험과 섬광 지속 시간이 1나노초 미만이라는 내용은 사실과 맞다.

hardJudge.note: D는 지문 전체 구조(정밀 측정 가능 → 그러나 원인 미합의)를 정확히 요약. A는 '짧다'를 '길다'로 뒤집은 세부 왜곡, B는 여러 가설 중 하나를 확정된 결론으로 과장, C는 지문에 없는 내용(기포 구름 연구 포기, 더 밝은 섬광). 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답과 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 서술 정확. Gaitan 1990 단일 기포 소노루미네선스, 1ns 미만 섬광, 플라스마/화학반응/전하분리 가설 등 사실 관계 무리 없음. 오답 A·B가 부분적 근거를 가져 비교가 필요하므로 medium 적합.

pub.explanation: Text 1은 기계화가 소규모 가족 농장 도태의 핵심 원인이라고 주장한다. Text 2는 은행 기록을 근거로, 많은 소농이 기계가 아예 없어서가 아니라 대출을 거절당해서 실패했고, 담보력이 큰 대농장은 유리한 금융 조건을 확보했다는 점을 들어 신용 접근성 차이가 농장 생존을 더 잘 설명한다고 반박한다. 따라서 정답은 A번이다.
pub.explanation_en: Text 1 claims that mechanization was the central cause of the decline of small family farms. Text 2 uses bank records to argue that many small farmers failed not because they lacked machines but because they were denied loans, while large farms with greater collateral secured favorable financing terms, so differences in access to credit better explain farm survival. Therefore, the answer is A.
options: The author would argue that unequal access to credit, not machinery ownership alone, better explains which farms survived and which were forced to sell.
The author would agree completely, citing bank records as further proof that machinery purchases alone determined which farms survived consolidation.

The author would contend that mechanization only mattered for farms that lacked any banking relationships, since Text 2 shows that well-financed farms could ignore machinery investment entirely and still outproduce their mechanized rivals.
The author would contend that credit access mattered only for the largest farms, and that among small and mid-sized farms, mechanization remained the decisive factor in survival.
pub.passage:
Text 1

Economic historians studying the collapse of small family farms in the early twentieth century often point to mechanization as the central cause. As tractors and mechanical harvesters became affordable, farms that could invest in this equipment achieved dramatically higher yields per worker, allowing them to undercut smaller neighbors on price. Within a generation, thousands of family farms that could not afford machinery were forced to sell their land to larger operations, consolidating agricultural production into far fewer, much larger farms than had existed before.

Text 2

Mechanization certainly reshaped agriculture, but focusing on machinery alone obscures the role that credit access played in determining which farms survived. Bank records from the period show that many small farms failed not because they lacked machinery outright, but because they were denied the loans needed to purchase it, while larger operations with more collateral secured favorable financing terms. Farms with equally modest yields but better banking relationships often survived the consolidation wave, while some mechanized but heavily indebted farms still failed when a single bad harvest made loan payments impossible to meet.

This makes A correct. Any comma placed between the adjectives or between the second adjective and "and," as in B, C, and D, incorrectly breaks a single modifying phrase into fragments. pub.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

pub.explanation:
정답 A: Text 1의 결론(소설이 아버지를 단죄함)은 할머니의 반어적 말이 아들을 '꾸짖는다'는 전제에 기대고 있다. Text 2는 할머니가 앞 장에서 자신을 두고 같은 말을 하며 웃었고 아들도 함께 웃었다는 점을 들어, 그 말이 자기 자신을 비꼬는 가족 농담이라고 본다. 즉 Text 2는 바로 이 전제를 공격한다.
B(결론 자체): Text 2는 'Whatever the novel finally decides about the father'라고 하여, 결론을 직접 부정하지 않고 판단을 보류한다. 문제 삼는 것은 이 대사가 결론의 근거가 될 수 있느냐는 점뿐이다.
C(부수적 세부): 새벽 어둠과 밤샘 끓이기에 관한 묘사는 Text 2가 전혀 다루지 않는다.
D(동의하는 부분): Text 2의 마지막 문장은 할머니가 Duc에게 육수 기술을 전수한다는 점에 분명히 동의한다.
pub.explanation_en:
Choice A is correct. Text 1's conclusion, that the novel condemns the father, depends on the idea that the grandmother's ironic line "plainly rebukes her son." Text 2 goes after exactly this idea. In an earlier chapter, she says nearly the same words about her own shortcuts and laughs, and her son laughs with her. So the line is a self-mocking family joke, not scorn.
Choice B is the conclusion itself. Text 2 does not reject it. It says "whatever the novel finally decides about the father" and argues only that this line can't support that judgment.
Choice C is a minor detail from Text 1 that Text 2 never mentions.
Choice D is something Text 2 agrees with. Its final sentence says the scene clearly shows the grandmother passing her technique on to Duc.
options: The assumption that the grandmother's ironic remark expresses scorn toward Duc's father
The assumption that the novel ultimately condemns Duc's father for giving up his inheritance
The assumption that the scene's opening in darkness stresses the long overnight simmer
The assumption that the scene shows the grandmother teaching Duc how to make the broth
pub.passage:
Text 1
In the dawn scene of Linh Tran's novel The Long Simmer, set in a Hanoi street-food alley, Duc's grandmother teaches him to char ginger and skim the beef-bone broth. The scene opens in the dark, with the pot already steaming from its overnight simmer. When Duc's father stirs bouillon powder into a second pot, she remarks, "Of course—bones are so slow, and customers never notice." Because this mock approval plainly rebukes her son, the scene sets the old woman's tradition against the father's shortcuts, and the novel finally condemns him as a man who has given up his inheritance.

Text 2
Readers who hear only scorn in the grandmother's line overlook an earlier chapter. There, recalling the rationing years, she says almost the same words about the powder she herself once stirred into her broth, and she laughs as she says them. Her son laughs too. The phrase is a family joke, used to poke fun at oneself, and it shows Duc that every cook is tempted by shortcuts. Whatever the novel finally decides about the father, this line cannot show it. Still, the scene clearly shows the grandmother passing her broth technique on to Duc.

advisory.note: 핵심 함정은 B다. Text 2는 결론에 대한 판단을 보류하면서("Whatever the novel finally decides") 결론의 근거만 공격한다. 이처럼 근거 공격과 결론 부정을 구분해야 하므로 medium보다 한 단계 높은 사고가 필요하다. 다만 Text 2가 "hear only scorn"이라고 공격 대상을 거의 그대로 밝히고 있어, 정답 A는 비교적 직접적으로 찾을 수 있다. 그래서 hard 수준으로는 경계선에 있다. D는 Text 2가 동의하는 부분을 오답으로 둔 것으로, 레시피 4번을 충족한다.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 전제(반어가 아들을 꾸짖음)와 결론(소설이 아버지를 단죄)을 'Because…' 구조로 명확히 구분하고, Text 2는 앞 장의 자기비하 농담 근거로 전제만 공격하며 결론은 'Whatever the novel finally decides'로 보류하고 전수 장면(D)에는 동의한다. B는 결론 자체를 공격 대상으로 오인하게 하는 강도 조절 함정, D는 동의 부분, C는 미언급 세부로 기능이 분명하다. 가상 소설이라 저작권·사실 문제 없음. 정답 A 타당.

pub.question: Based on the texts, which element of the argument in Text 1 would the author of Text 2 most likely challenge?

pub.answer_rationale: Ostrander's cycle (fee → revenue → better transit → less driving) assumes reinvestment happens after pricing begins; Holloway's insistence that expansion come "before it is implemented, not after" shows he views that sequence as harming residents of underserved neighborhoods in the interim, since they "have little choice but to pay the fee or lose access to jobs downtown."
pub.evidence_span: He contends that any pricing scheme must be paired with substantial transit expansion in underserved areas before it is implemented, not after, or it risks simply taxing those who have the fewest alternatives.
pub.evidence_target: Text 2's Holloway would counter Text 1's Ostrander by arguing that her reinvestment cycle still forces underserved commuters to pay the fee immediately, well before any transit improvements it funds could reach them.
pub.explanation: Holloway's central objection is one of timing and sequence: he insists that transit expansion must occur before pricing is implemented, because Ostrander's cycle assumes future reinvestment will eventually help underserved riders, but those riders would already be paying the fee with no immediate alternative. This directly targets the gap between Ostrander's proposed long-term cycle and the immediate burden it places on commuters lacking transit access.
pub.explanation_en: Holloway's central objection is about timing and sequence. He insists that transit expansion must happen before congestion pricing is implemented. Ostrander's cycle assumes that future reinvestment will eventually help underserved riders, but those riders would already be paying the fee with no immediate alternative. Choice A captures this: the plan could burden commuters in underserved areas before the promised transit improvements ever arrive. This directly targets the gap between Ostrander's proposed long-term cycle and the immediate burden it places on commuters who lack transit access.
options: He would point out that this plan could burden commuters in underserved areas before promised transit improvements ever arrive.
He would agree entirely, adding that this reinvestment cycle eliminates any concern about which commuters can afford the fee.

He would contend that reinvesting the revenue is an inadequate solution on its own, since the transit improvements it funds would take years to materialize while commuters need viable alternatives immediately.
He would maintain that the plan is flawed because transit expansion should follow pricing revenue rather than come at the same time as it, allowing funds to accumulate first.
pub.passage:
Text 1

Urban planner Miriam Ostrander maintains that congestion pricing—charging drivers a fee to enter a city's downtown during peak hours—is the most effective tool for reducing gridlock. Ostrander points to case studies showing that when driving becomes more expensive, commuters shift to public transit, cycling, or off-peak travel almost immediately. She argues that the revenue generated can be reinvested into buses and trains, creating a self-reinforcing cycle: fewer cars, better transit, and further reductions in driving. For Ostrander, the price signal is what makes commuters reconsider habits that decades of public awareness campaigns failed to change.

Text 2

Transportation economist Devon Holloway argues that congestion pricing, while effective at reducing traffic volume, disproportionately burdens lower-income commuters who cannot easily switch to alternative transportation, especially in cities where transit coverage is uneven. Holloway notes that many outer neighborhoods lack reliable bus or rail service, so residents there have little choice but to pay the fee or lose access to jobs downtown. He contends that any pricing scheme must be paired with substantial transit expansion in underserved areas before it is implemented, not after, or it risks simply taxing those who have the fewest alternatives.

시간 순서(선 확충-후 시행 vs 후 확충)를 정확히 구분해야 정답을 고를 수 있음
선택지 C, D는 Holloway의 실제 주장과 표면적으로 유사한 요소를 포함하여 정답과 혼동 가능성이 있음

distractors.plausibleBecause: Holloway는 재투자 자체는 긍정적으로 언급하므로 일부 동의하는 듯 보일 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: Holloway는 '전적으로 동의'하지 않으며, 오히려 저소득층 부담 우려를 핵심 논지로 삼음. 'eliminates any concern'은 그의 주장과 정반대임

distractors.plausibleBecause: Text2의 'before it is implemented, not after' 구절을 반대로 해석하여 '자금 축적 후 확충'으로 오해할 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: Holloway는 확충이 가격 부과보다 먼저 이루어져야 한다고 명시했는데, 이 선택지는 정반대로 '확충이 나중에 이루어져야 한다'고 말함 - 인과관계 및 시간관계를 뒤집은 오답

issues: 선택지 C도 Holloway의 입장과 상당히 부합하는 매력적인 오답으로 보임: Holloway는 '재투자만으로는 불충분하다'는 취지의 주장을 하므로, C와 B 사이의 변별이 다소 모호할 수 있음. 다만 지문에서 Holloway는 명시적으로 'before it is implemented, not after'라고 하여 시점(timing) 문제를 강조하므로 B가 더 직접적으로 부합하긴 함.
D는 지문 내용과 반대되는 주장(가격 부과 후 수익 축적)을 담고 있어 명백한 오답으로 문제 없음.

pub.explanation: 앞부분에서 Joon의 농담에 Sunja가 눈물이 날 만큼 웃는 장면은 편안한 농담의 분위기를 보여 준다. 사진이 나온 뒤 Sunja는 거의 찬 잔을 다시 채우고, 잡채를 크게 권하고, 신부 드레스를 두 번이나 칭찬하는데 이는 화제를 돌리려는 억지 명랑함이다. 냅킨으로 사진을 덮는 행동도 같은 의도를 뒷받침하므로 D가 정답이다. A는 Sunja가 회상에 잠기는 장면이 없고, C는 그녀가 슬픔을 드러내지 않고 오히려 감추므로 틀리며, B는 사진 이후의 변화를 놓친다.
pub.explanation_en: In the first part, Sunja laughs until she tears up at Joon's jokes, showing a relaxed, joking mood. After the photograph appears, Sunja refills a nearly full glass, urges more japchae on people, and compliments the bride's dress twice, which is forced cheerfulness meant to change the subject. Covering the photograph with a napkin supports the same intent, so the answer is D. A fails because there is no scene of Sunja sinking into memories, C fails because she hides her grief rather than showing it, and B misses the change after the photograph.
options: From playful teasing between relatives to wistful nostalgia as Sunja recalls the man in the photograph
From irritation at the noisy crowd to warm amusement as Joon jokes about a clumsy cousin
From festive merriment to open grief as Sunja is reminded of a loss she has long concealed
From relaxed banter to an effortful cheerfulness that seems meant to steer attention elsewhere
pub.passage: When the buffet doors opened, the wedding hall in Busan dissolved into a hundred conversations, and Sunja let the noise carry her to a corner table. Joon, her grandson, slid in beside her, tugging at a collar his mother had ironed too stiffly, and teased her about the cousin who had tripped on the aisle runner. Sunja swatted his wrist and laughed until her eyes watered. Then he drew a creased photograph from his jacket: a young woman in a borrowed hanbok beside a man no one in the family had ever named. "Who is he, Halmeoni?" Sunja glanced at it, smiled, and said it was only a neighbor, a long time ago. She refilled Joon's cup, though it was nearly full, and asked loudly whether he had tried the japchae. Twice more she praised the bride's dress. When he slid the photograph back toward her, she placed her napkin over it, smoothing the cloth flat with both hands, and turned to wave at a cousin across the room.

pub.explanation: 길드가 구근 상태나 수량에 변화가 없는데도 계약 이행을 거부하도록 촉구했다는 것은 가격 폭락이 구매자 신뢰 붕괴 때문이라는 주장을 가장 직접적으로 뒷받침합니다. 나머지 선택지는 구근의 품질 저하, 공급 증가, 희소성 변화를 가정하는데, 이는 주장과 반대되거나 지문에서 공급과 재배 조건에 변화가 없었다고 한 내용과 모순됩니다.
pub.explanation_en: Only the guild letters urging refusal of contracts while the bulbs were unchanged show that the crash came from collapsing confidence rather than from supply or quality. The other options point to bulb condition, increased supply, or scarcity, which are changes in the bulbs' scarcity or value and so would undercut the claim or are contradicted by the passage's statement that no supply or condition change was recorded.
options: Several Haarlem auctioneers began reporting that Semper Augustus bulbs had arrived in poor condition, even though contract prices for the variety had held steady until February.
Several regional growers began planting far larger quantities of Semper Augustus bulbs, which flooded the market and pushed contract prices down in the weeks before the failed auction.
Several regional guilds began circulating letters urging members to buy additional tulip contracts at the lower prices, even though the bulbs themselves were scarcer than in earlier seasons.
Several regional guilds began circulating letters urging members to refuse to honor existing tulip contracts entirely, even though the bulbs themselves were unaffected in condition or quantity.
pub.passage: An economic historian studying the collapse of the Dutch tulip market in 1637 argued that the crash resulted primarily from a sudden failure of buyer confidence rather than from any change in tulip bulbs' actual scarcity or agricultural value. To support this claim, the historian traced contract prices for a specific tulip variety, Semper Augustus, across several weeks. The price records showed that contracts for delivery of the bulbs held steady at extremely high values right up until a single afternoon in February, when a routine auction in Haarlem failed to attract any bidders willing to pay even a fraction of the previous asking price. No new bulbs had been planted, harvested, or destroyed in the days surrounding this event, and no change in the growing conditions or bulb supply was recorded. The historian also noted that, within days of the failed auction, several regional guilds began circulating letters urging members to stop honoring existing tulip delivery contracts altogether, regardless of the bulbs' condition or quantity.

pub.explanation: 지문은 맨티스 새우가 많은 광수용체를 가지고 있음에도 색을 정밀하게 구분하는 능력은 오히려 떨어진다는 반전된 실험 결과를 제시한 뒤, 최근 연구에 따르면 이 시각계가 정밀한 색 구분이 아니라 빠른 색 인식에 특화된 것이라는 결론으로 마무리된다. 이는 지문 전체를 아우르는 핵심 주장이므로 B가 정답이다. A는 광수용체가 많다는 세부 사실은 맞지만 '포식자 회피를 위해 진화했다'는 인과 관계는 본문에 없는 확대 해석이다. C는 색 구분 실험 결과라는 세부 사실만 다루고, 그로부터 도출된 핵심 결론(빠른 인식 시스템)을 놓친 채 '덜 발달했다'는 지문에 없는 판단으로 비약한다. pub.explanation_en: The text presents a surprising experimental result: although mantis shrimp have many photoreceptors, they are actually worse at precisely telling colors apart. It then concludes that recent research suggests this visual system is specialized for rapid color recognition rather than fine color discrimination. This is the central claim of the whole text, so the answer is B. A is true about the large number of photoreceptors, but the causal claim that they evolved 'to avoid predators' is an overreach not found in the text. C covers only the detail about the color-discrimination experiments; it misses the key conclusion (a rapid-recognition system) and leaps to the claim that the system is 'less advanced,' which the text never makes. D is wrong because it states the opposite of the text, which says the mantis shrimp's method differs from the human method.
options: Mantis shrimp evolved sixteen types of photoreceptors specifically to help them avoid predators while hunting on coral reefs.
Although mantis shrimp have many more photoreceptor types than humans, their unusual visual system appears built for rapid color recognition rather than for distinguishing subtle color differences.
Because mantis shrimp perform poorly on behavioral tests of color discrimination, scientists have concluded that their visual system is less advanced than that of bees or humans.
Mantis shrimp process visual information by blending signals from multiple photoreceptors in the brain, similar to the method used in human color vision.
pub.passage: The mantis shrimp, a marine crustacean found in tropical and subtropical waters, possesses one of the most complex visual systems in the animal kingdom, yet the exact purpose of this complexity has puzzled scientists for decades. Unlike humans, who perceive color using three types of photoreceptors, mantis shrimp have between twelve and sixteen types, and their eyes can independently rotate to track prey while scanning for predators. Researchers initially assumed this abundance of photoreceptors allowed the shrimp to distinguish an extraordinary range of colors, but behavioral tests revealed the opposite: mantis shrimp are surprisingly poor at telling similar hues apart compared to humans and bees. More recent studies suggest that instead of blending color signals in the brain the way human vision does, the shrimp's eyes may process each photoreceptor's input separately and rapidly, allowing near-instant color identification without complex neural computation—a system suited less for fine discrimination than for extremely fast recognition in the fast-moving reef environments where the shrimp hunts.

pub.answer_rationale: Text 2는 요금 정책의 속도나 효과 자체를 반박하기보다, 그로 인한 형평성 문제를 지적함으로써 Text 1의 주장을 제한적으로 인정하면서도 비판한다.

pub.evidence_target: Text 2는 혼잡 통행료의 빠른 효과 자체를 부정하지는 않지만, 그 속도가 대중교통 접근성이 부족한 저소득층 통근자에게 불공평한 부담을 지운다는 점을 들어 정책의 형평성을 문제 삼는다.
pub.explanation: Text 2는 혼잡 통행료가 교통량 감소에 즉각적 효과를 낼 수 있다는 점을 명시적으로 부정하지 않는다. 대신, 그 효과가 대중교통 대안이 부족한 저소득층 통근자에게 불균형한 부담을 지운다는 형평성 문제를 제기하며, 대중교통 투자를 먼저 해야 한다고 주장한다. 즉, Text 1의 '빠르고 측정 가능한 결과'라는 주장에 대해 속도는 인정하되 그 대가로 형평성이 희생된다는 조건을 덧붙이는 반응을 보일 것이다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A는 Text 1의 주장(사회기반시설 사업이 새로운 운전자를 끌어들일 수 있다는)을 Text 2의 입장인 것처럼 뒤바꾼 것이다. C는 Text 2가 실제로 부정하지 않는 부분을 부정한 것으로 만든 왜곡이다. D는 Text 2의 주장과 정반대로, 저소득층이 오히려 부담을 받는다는 내용을 이익을 받는다는 것으로 화자의 입장을 잘못 귀속시킨 것이다.
pub.explanation_en: Text 2 never explicitly denies that congestion pricing can reduce traffic right away. Instead, it raises an equity concern: the effect places a disproportionate burden on lower-income commuters who lack transit alternatives, and it argues that investment in public transit should come first. So in response to Text 1's claim of 'faster and more measurable results,' the author of Text 2 would acknowledge the speed but add that fairness is sacrificed as the price. The answer is B. A swaps in Text 1's claim (that infrastructure projects can attract new drivers) as though it were Text 2's position. C turns something Text 2 does not deny into a denial, which distorts the text. D is the opposite of Text 2's argument: lower-income commuters are burdened, not benefited, so it misattributes the author's position.
options: By insisting that infrastructure projects always attract more new drivers than congestion pricing does
By agreeing that congestion pricing works quickly but arguing that its speed comes at the cost of fairness for commuters without transit access
By denying that congestion fees have any measurable effect on traffic volume in cities that have adopted them
By claiming that lower-income commuters actually benefit most directly from downtown congestion fees
pub.passage:
Text 1
Urban planners advocating for congestion pricing argue that charging drivers a fee to enter crowded downtown areas during peak hours is the most effective way to reduce gridlock. Cities that have implemented such fees report meaningful drops in traffic volume, along with increased revenue that can be reinvested in public transit. Because the fee directly targets the behavior causing congestion—driving into the city center at busy times—proponents claim it produces faster and more measurable results than infrastructure projects, which can take years to complete and may simply attract new drivers once finished.

Text 2
Critics of congestion pricing point out that the policy places a disproportionate burden on lower-income commuters who cannot afford the daily fee but also lack convenient access to public transit alternatives. These critics argue that without first expanding affordable transit options in underserved neighborhoods, congestion pricing effectively restricts who can drive downtown based on income rather than genuinely solving the underlying transportation problem. They favor phasing in transit investment before introducing any fee.

pub.explanation: 어머니는 쓸면서 결혼 준비 이야기를 하고 딸의 새 집 바닥을 언급하므로 청소가 결혼을 피하는 수단이 아니다. 끝에 밀레나가 같은 방식으로 빗자루를 이어받고 어머니가 쓰레받기를 드는 장면은 역할이 바뀌는 가운데 습관이 이어짐을 보여 준다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 바닥 이야기를 벗어나고 싶은 일로 오해했고, B는 카탈로그가 펼쳐진 채 방치된 점만 근거로 삼았으며, D는 마를론의 농담을 규칙으로 과장했다.
pub.explanation_en: The mother talks about the wedding preparations while sweeping and mentions the floor of her daughter's new home, so the cleaning is not a way of avoiding the wedding. At the end, Milena takes over the broom in the same way and her mother holds the dustpan, which shows a habit continuing as their roles shift. So C is the answer. A misreads the floor talk as something she wants to escape, B relies only on the catalog being left open and unattended, and D exaggerates Marlon's joke into a rule.
options: a tiresome chore that Milena intends to leave behind once she is married.
the mother's quiet resistance to discussing her daughter's coming wedding.
a shared habit carrying their bond forward as their roles shift.
the strict standards Marlon expects his employees to follow in the shop.
pub.passage: Milena held the dustpan while her mother swept, as she had every Saturday since she was nine. Marlon's barbershop on Brīvības Street closed at six, and her mother, who had cut hair there for twenty years, never let anyone else sweep the floor. Tonight they were meant to choose wedding napkins; the catalog lay open on a barber chair, untouched. The broom moved in its old pattern, under the mirrors, around the coat rack, toward the door. Her mother talked about guest lists and seating while she swept, and Milena answered without looking up. Once her mother paused and said that Milena's new flat had wooden floors, the kind that showed every hair. Marlon, counting the till, laughed and said she would need a better broom. Near the end, her mother's arms slowed. Milena set down the pan, took the broom, and finished the last corner in the same strokes, left to right. Her mother picked up the dustpan without a word. Outside, a tram rang its bell twice at the corner.

pub.explanation: 유리병에는 지도에서 사라진 마을 이름이 붙어 있고, Dvora는 그 씨앗들이 코트 주머니에 담겨 옮겨졌지만 지금도 봄마다 싹을 틔운다고 말한다. 아버지가 농장을 떠나 도시로 옮겨야 하는 상황에서 그녀는 빈 병에 아버지 농장 이름을 적는다. 두 단서를 이으면 병은 옮겨지더라도 고향의 무언가가 살아남을 수 있다는 희망을 상징하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 지문에 없는 판매 이야기이고, B는 인물 관계로 초점을 옮겼으며, D는 상실만 강조해 씨앗이 다시 자란다는 점을 놓쳤다.
pub.explanation_en: The glass jars are labeled with the names of villages that have vanished from the map, and Dvora says the seeds were carried in coat pockets and still sprout every spring. With her father having to leave the farm and move to the city, she writes her father's farm name on an empty jar. Connecting the two clues, the jars symbolize the hope that something of a home can survive being carried somewhere new, so C is the answer. A is a selling story not found in the text, B shifts the focus to a relationship between characters, and D stresses only loss and misses that the seeds grow again.
options: The cooperative's success in selling its grain to many of the nearby villages
Dvora's distrust of the new teacher who has recently joined the cooperative
The hope that something of a home can survive being carried somewhere new
The loss of farmland that has been swallowed up by the growing city nearby
pub.passage: By the third week of term, Dvora still sat at the farthest table in the seed-saving cooperative in Haifa, sorting lentils without a word to me. I was the new teacher, and she had made it plain that she considered me temporary. Her father, I learned from the director, was to be moved from his farm in the hills to a small room in the city, and he had refused to go. One afternoon she showed me a cabinet of glass jars, each labeled in faded ink with the name of a village that no longer appeared on any map. These were carried here in coat pockets, she said. Some of them still come up every spring. I watched her lift a jar of dark wheat and turn it slowly, as if weighing it. The next morning, she asked me for an empty jar and a label, and she wrote the name of her father's farm on it in careful letters. Rain fell on the tin roof all that day, and the director kept the stove burning in the back room.

pub.explanation: 초반에 사디아는 의자를 세는 하산을 성직자에 빗대고 하품 타이밍을 맞추는 등 가볍게 비꼬는 재미로 바라본다. 이후 하산이 화를 내지 않고 잠든 아이를 지켜보는 모습, 아버지가 해고된 사연을 털어놓는 장면이 이어지며 어조는 이해와 연민이 담긴 차분한 성찰로 바뀐다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 '천둥에 대비했다'는 예상만 보고 실제로 분노가 오지 않았다는 점을 놓쳤고, C와 D는 결혼식의 기쁨이나 하산의 엄격함에 대한 감탄으로 변화의 방향을 잘못 읽었다.
pub.explanation_en: At first, Sadia looks at Hasan lightly and wryly, comparing him to a priest as he counts the chairs and timing her yawns. Then Hasan does not get angry but watches a sleeping child, and her father's story of being fired follows, so the tone shifts to a calm, reflective one full of understanding and sympathy. The answer is A. B notices only the expectation of 'bracing for thunder' and misses that anger never actually comes, while C and D misread the direction of the change as joy at the wedding or admiration for Hasan's strictness.
options: It shifts from wry amusement at Hasan's ritual to a gentle, reflective sympathy.
It shifts from wry amusement at Hasan's ritual to nervous dread of his temper.
It shifts from quiet boredom with the work to exuberant joy at the crowded feast.
It shifts from mocking impatience with Hasan to admiration for his strict precision.
pub.passage: Hasan counted chairs. At every wedding we staffed in Thessaloniki that summer of 1872, he circled the hall twice before the guests came, tapping each chair back like a priest blessing pews, and I, newly hired, learned to time my yawns to the movement of his lips. That evening the count collapsed within minutes: cousins perched on window ledges, the musicians spilled down the stairs, and an aunt sat squarely on his tally board. I braced for thunder. None came. Hasan stood among the dancers with his hands loose at his sides, watching a boy asleep across two laps. Much later, as we folded linens, he mentioned that his father had once lost a post over a single guest left standing, and that he had counted chairs every night since, though no one had ever asked him to. Then he set his tally slate on my stack of napkins. Keep it or break it, Sadia, he said, and went to help the cooks. Out on the street, a cart wheel ground slowly over the wet stones.

pub.answer_rationale: 정답은 여러 세대에 걸친 이동(4~5세대)과 생식 지연(diapause)으로 마지막 세대가 오래 사는 이유를 결합해, 그 결과 경로 자체가 '유전'되는 것이지 한 마리가 배우는 게 아니라는 핵심 논리를 완성한다.

pub.evidence_target: notes 2번(4~5세대에 걸친 이동)과 3번(슈퍼 세대의 생식 지연) 및 6번(경로가 유전됨)
pub.explanation: 학생의 목표는 '어느 한 마리도 왕복 전체를 완주하지 않는데도 이동이 놀라운 이유'를 설명하는 것이다. A는 여러 세대(4~5세대)에 걸쳐 이동이 이루어진다는 점과, 마지막 슈퍼 세대가 생식을 늦춰 8개월간 살면서 봄에 북상을 시작한다는 점을 결합하여, 그 결과 경로 자체가 개별 나비의 학습이 아니라 세대를 통해 '유전'된다는 핵심 논리를 완성한다. B는 방향 감지 메커니즘(태양 나침반, 자기장)만 다뤄 목표와 무관하다. C는 세대 교체와 diapause를 언급하지만 '경로가 유전된다'는 핵심 결론을 빠뜨려 목표를 완전히 달성하지 못한다. D는 단순히 이동 거리가 멀다는 점만 강조해 세대 교체나 유전 개념을 전혀 다루지 않는다.
pub.explanation_en: The student's goal is to explain why the migration is remarkable even though no single butterfly completes the whole round trip. A combines two points: the migration is completed over several generations (4 to 5), and the final super generation delays reproduction, living for 8 months and beginning the northward trip in spring. It then completes the key logic that, as a result, the route itself is 'inherited' across generations rather than learned by any individual butterfly. B covers only the direction-sensing mechanisms (sun compass, magnetic field) and is irrelevant to the goal. C mentions the generational turnover and diapause but omits the key conclusion that 'the route is inherited,' so it does not fully achieve the goal. D stresses only that the distance traveled is long and does not address generational turnover or inheritance at all.
options: Because the migration is completed across several short-lived generations and a long-lived super generation that delays reproduction, the route itself is passed down rather than learned by any one butterfly.
Monarch butterflies rely on a time-compensated sun compass and possibly a magnetic backup cue, which together allow them to navigate thousands of miles even on cloudy days.
Although the migration requires four to five generations to complete, the reproductive diapause of the final super generation lets it live up to eight months and travel north in spring.
The monarch butterfly travels up to 3,000 miles from Canada and the northern United States to central Mexico, a distance that would be difficult for any single insect to cover alone.
pub.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- The Monarch butterfly (Danaus plexippus) migrates up to 3,000 miles each fall from Canada and the northern United States to overwintering sites in central Mexico.
- No single butterfly completes the round trip; the migration spans four to five generations, with each generation living only a few weeks except the final "super generation," which can live up to eight months.
- The super generation delays reproduction until spring, a state called reproductive diapause, which allows it to survive the winter and begin the journey north.
- Scientists have found that monarchs use a time-compensated sun compass, adjusting their flight direction based on the sun's position and an internal circadian clock.
- Cloudy days do not stop migration entirely, suggesting monarchs may also sense the Earth's magnetic field as a backup orientation cue.
- Because no individual monarch has ever made the full round trip, researchers describe the migratory route itself as being "inherited" across generations rather than learned by any single butterfly.

difficultyReasons: 정답과 오답 B가 세대 교체·diapause라는 동일한 핵심 정보를 공유해 두 문장의 차이를 세밀하게 구분해야 함(사실 나열 vs 결론까지 연결)
질문이 요구하는 것은 단순 사실 재진술이 아니라 '왜 remarkable한가'에 대한 인과적 결론까지 포함하는 문장이라는 점을 파악해야 함
여러 메모(세대 수, diapause, 유전된 경로)를 종합해 하나의 논리적 흐름으로 재구성해야 하는 3단계 이상의 추론이 필요함
오답 A와 D도 지문에 실제 있는 정보를 사용하지만 질문의 초점(왜 remarkable한가: 세대 전달)과 다른 측면(방향 감지, 거리)을 다뤄 표면적으로는 관련 있어 보임

pub.answer_rationale: "In doing so" correctly forms a participial transitional phrase that connects the potters' action to its result without introducing a contradictory or unnecessary coordinating word.
pub.evidence_span: ______, these potters preserved a regional craft tradition that industrial ceramics manufacturers had largely abandoned
pub.explanation: 이 문장은 빈칸 뒤에 ", these potters preserved ..."라는 완전한 독립절이 이어지므로, 빈칸에는 이 절 앞에 놓이는 삽입 수식어구가 와야 한다. "In doing so"는 앞 문장의 행위를 받는 완결된 수식어구로 뒤 독립절과 콤마로 자연스럽게 이어진다. "In doing so, and"와 "In doing so, or"는 등위접속사가 콤마 뒤에 매달려 연결할 대상이 없고, "In doing so, which"는 관계대명사가 이끄는 절이 완성되지 않아 모두 비문이다. 따라서 정답은 B이다.
pub.explanation_en: After the blank comes a complete independent clause, ", these potters preserved ...," so the blank must hold an introductory phrase placed before that clause. "In doing so" is a complete introductory phrase that picks up the action of the previous sentence and connects to the clause with a comma. "In doing so, and" and "In doing so, or" leave a coordinating conjunction hanging with nothing to join, and "In doing so, which" starts a relative clause that is never completed, so all three are ungrammatical. So the answer is B.
options: In doing so, and
In doing so
In doing so, which
In doing so, or
pub.passage: In the 1930s, several Appalachian potters revived a nearly forgotten technique known as salt glazing, in which salt thrown into a hot kiln vaporizes and coats each piece with a glassy, mottled surface. ______, these potters preserved a regional craft tradition that industrial ceramics manufacturers had largely abandoned.

difficultyReasons: 단순히 전환어(however)나 양보 접속사(despite)가 문맥에 맞는지 한 단계만 판단하면 됨
인과/설명 관계와 대조/양보 관계를 구분하는 것이 핵심이나 지문 내용이 명확하여 판단이 어렵지 않음
오답 중 하나(or)는 명백히 문법적으로 부적절하여 쉽게 제거 가능
문장 하나의 논리 흐름만 보면 되고 여러 자료를 종합할 필요 없음

distractors.matches: 두 문장이 대조 관계가 아니라 인과/설명 관계인데, 표면적으로 앞뒤 문장 사이에 전환어를 넣어도 될 것 같다고 느낄 수 있음
distractors.plausibleBecause: 'In doing so'는 문법적으로 맞고, 학생이 접속부사 'however'를 추가로 넣으면 더 자연스럽다고 착각할 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 문맥상 두 절은 대조 관계가 아니라 '그렇게 함으로써(도공들이 이 기법을 되살림으로써) 전통을 보존했다'는 순접/설명 관계이므로 'however'를 넣으면 논리적으로 모순됨

distractors.matches: 산업 도자기 제조업체들이 이 기법을 버렸다는 내용과 연결지어 '그럼에도 불구하고'라는 의미로 오인할 수 있음
distractors.plausibleBecause: 'Despite'는 양보의 의미로, 얼핏 보면 전통 보존이 어떤 어려움에도 불구하고 이루어진 것처럼 보일 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 이 문장은 도공들이 소금 유약 기법을 되살린 행위 자체가 전통 보존의 수단이므로, 'despite doing so'는 인과관계를 양보관계로 왜곡하여 의미가 통하지 않음

distractors.matches: 문장 구조상 접속사가 필요한 자리라는 점에서 형식적으로는 비슷해 보임
distractors.plausibleBecause: 'or'는 선택지를 나열할 때 쓰이므로 목록처럼 보이는 문장에서 그럴듯해 보일 수 있음

pub.explanation: 직선 $y = kx + 4$를 타원 방정식에 대입하면 $\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{(kx+4)^2}{16} = 1$이 된다. 양변에 400을 곱해 정리하면 $16x^2 + 25(kx+4)^2 = 400$, 즉 $16x^2 + 25k^2x^2 + 200kx + 400 = 400$이 되고, 이는 $(16+25k^2)x^2 + 200kx = 0$으로 정리된다. 이 식은 $x[(16+25k^2)x + 200k] = 0$으로 인수분해되므로 $x=0$이거나 $x = \frac{-200k}{16+25k^2}$이다. 접선(교점이 정확히 하나)이 되려면 이 두 근이 같아야 하므로 $\frac{-200k}{16+25k^2} = 0$, 즉 $k=0$이어야 한다. $k=0$일 때 직선은 $y=4$이고, 이는 타원의 위쪽 꼭짓점 $(0,4)$에서 정확히 한 번 접한다(상반부 조건 $y\ge0$ 안에서). 오답들은 접선의 기울기를 구하는 일반 공식(장반경·단반경 비율)을 그 자체로 착각하거나, 판별식을 0으로 놓는 대신 이차항 계수나 상수항 조건만 일부 만족하는 값들이다.
pub.explanation_en: Substitute the line $y = kx + 4$ into the ellipse equation to get $\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{(kx+4)^2}{16} = 1$. Multiplying both sides by 400 and simplifying gives $16x^2 + 25(kx+4)^2 = 400$, that is, $16x^2 + 25k^2x^2 + 200kx + 400 = 400$, which simplifies to $(16+25k^2)x^2 + 200kx = 0$. This factors as $x[(16+25k^2)x + 200k] = 0$, so $x=0$ or $x = \frac{-200k}{16+25k^2}$. For the line to be tangent (exactly one intersection point), these two roots must be equal, so $\frac{-200k}{16+25k^2} = 0$, that is, $k=0$. When $k=0$, the line is $y=4$, which touches the ellipse exactly once at the top vertex $(0,4)$ (within the upper-half condition $y\ge0$). The wrong answers mistake the general formula for the slope of a tangent line (the ratio of the semi-major to semi-minor axis) for the answer itself, or are values that satisfy only part of the condition on the quadratic coefficient or the constant term instead of setting the discriminant to 0.
pub.passage: An architect is designing an elliptical archway. In a coordinate system where $x$ and $y$ are measured in feet, the outline of the archway's opening satisfies the equation $\frac{x^2}{25} + \frac{y^2}{16} = 1$ for $y \ge 0$, representing the upper half of an ellipse. A horizontal support beam is to be installed along the line $y = kx + 4$, where $k$ is a constant, and the beam must touch the archway's curved edge at exactly one point.

issues: 해설의 대수적 전개는 정확하지만, 문제 설계 자체에 결함이 있음: 직선 y=kx+4는 항상 y절편이 (0,4)이며 이는 타원의 상반부 꼭짓점과 정확히 일치한다. 따라서 어떤 k값을 대입해도 x=0, y=4는 항상 교점이 되고, 판별식 계산 결과 이차방정식의 근이 x=0과 x=-200k/(16+25k^2)로 나온다. k≠0인 경우에도 두 번째 근이 x=0이 아니면 그 x값에서 실제로 상반부(y≥0) 타원 위에 있는지 확인해야 하는데, 해설은 이를 '두 근이 같아야 접선'이라는 논리로 단순화했다. 그러나 이는 오해의 소지가 있다: 두 근이 다르더라도 두 번째 근이 정의역(y≥0) 밖에 있으면 실질적으로 교점이 하나뿐일 수 있다. 예를 들어 k=4/5나 k=5/4를 대입했을 때 두 번째 근에서의 y값이 음수라면(즉 하반부에 해당) 상반부 곡선과는 오직 (0,4)에서만 만나므로 그 값들도 '정확히 한 점에서 접한다'는 조건을 만족시킬 수 있다. 실제로 확인해보면 k=4/5일 때 두 번째 교점의 x값과 y값을 계산하면 y가 4보다 작아지며 여전히 y≥0 범위 내에 있을 가능성이 있어, 선택지 B도 조건을 만족할 수 있는지 검토가 필요하다. 즉 '두 근이 같아야 한다'는 조건(완전한 접선, 판별식=0)과 '상반부에서 교점이 정확히 하나'라는 조건이 동치가 아닐 수 있으므로, 해설의 논리가 문제의 실제 요구사항과 정확히 일치하지 않을 가능성이 있다. 이 점을 재검토해야 한다.
선택지 B(4/5)가 장반경-단반경 비율(b/a = 4/5)과 정확히 일치하는데, 이는 타원의 특수한 대칭성과 관련이 있어 단순히 '오답 함정'으로 치부하기에는 지나치게 의미심장한 값으로, 실제로 y=(4/5)x+4가 상반부와 정확히 한 점에서 만나는지 별도 검증이 필요하다.

pub.explanation_en: At first, the underlined sentence reads like background description of the father's tidy habits. But later the father names a village he had never mentioned and unfolds the map corner he had folded over, pointing to a dot on a riverbank unrelated to Shanghai. Once these two scenes overlap, the corner folded to the north is reread as foreshadowing of longing for his hometown, so D is the answer. A is a reading based on the underlined sentence alone, B is a misreading that ties it to the post office scene right after, and C generalizes the habit into a character trait and cannot explain the later clues.
options: It establishes the father's clerical habits as background for the errand at the post office.
It introduces a tidy habit that the clerk's careful weighing of the parcel then echoes.
It shows the general care with which the father treats the objects that he owns.
It hints at a longing for a distant place that the father's later gestures reveal.
pub.passage: "Father, the postmaster says the river road is shorter," I told him, spreading the map across the counter. Taeyang did not look at it. __He had folded the corner of every map he owned toward the north, a habit I took for the neatness of a clerk.__ Outside, a cart of melons rolled past the little post office, and the clerk inside weighed our parcel twice, frowning at the scale as though it had insulted him. I paid the fee from my own purse, counting the coins in English under my breath, which made the clerk smile. We had come to send a parcel to my aunt, though Father had written nothing on the label but a name. When the clerk asked where it should go, Father answered with the name of a village I had never once heard him say aloud. He took the map from me, opened its folded corner, and pressed his thumbnail against a small dot beside a river that does not run anywhere near Shanghai. Then he handed the map back to me and asked whether the river road was paved.

When Tane offers to hand over the chisel, Moana falls silent and then breaks that rule by telling a childhood memory about the groove beside the blade. Therefore, the answer is C: it sets up a vow of silence and then breaks it to share a memory. A is wrong because the son never gives up the chisel, and B and D do not match the focus of the text.
options: It describes a family quarrel over a chisel and then shows the son giving it up to end the dispute.
It lists the rules of a business and then explains why the father enforces them so strictly.
It establishes a father's private vow of silence and then shows him breaking it to share a memory.

pub.passage: Three rules hung on the laundromat wall in Moana's handwriting: no dyeing, no sleeping, no leaving wet clothes past closing. He had added a fourth in his head the day the will was read, a rule for himself: do not mention the chisel. His father had left the carving chisel, the one with the whalebone handle, not to Moana but to Moana's son, Tane, who was nineteen and wanted to fix engines. Now Tane sat on a dryer, turning the chisel over, while the machines thumped. "You want it," Tane said. "Take it." Moana said that was not how it worked. Tane said that was exactly how it worked, that he could hand it over in one second. Moana folded a towel twice and did not answer. Then he asked, almost against his will, whether Tane had ever noticed the small notch near the blade. Tane had not. Moana took the chisel, showed him where his own thumb had slipped at age eight, and handed it back. "Your grandfather wanted someone to ask about that," he said. Outside, a bus hissed at the stop, and the last dryer clicked off.

But after the sentence saying the drawing vanished once the route changed, and the ending scene on Saturday in which Moana is with the child holding a real red kite, it becomes clear that the drawing was a token of a promise made to the child. It also interlocks ironically with the opening saying that 'promises are cheap,' so the answer is C. A reads only the surface function, B ties it to the apology in the next scene and misreads it, and D borrows the saying's wording to generalize but does not fit the ending scene.
options: It adds a homely detail that describes the interior of the bus the narrator rides.
It introduces a lighthearted note that prepares for Moana's apology for the missed stop.
It introduces an object that points toward a pledge Moana eventually keeps for a child.

pub.passage: Promises are cheap on a tram line. That was my mother's saying, and I repeated it the winter I rode Moana's bus each morning to the weaving cooperative on Ponsonby Road. __Moana kept a child's drawing of a red kite pinned above the fare box, its corners curling from the heat of the engine.__ At the cooperative we were finishing a flax mat for a wedding, and I spent most days arguing with the other women about a border pattern none of us would agree to tighten. One morning Moana missed my stop and drove two streets past it before he noticed, apologizing so many times that I laughed at him. In late August his route changed, and a new driver took the bus. The drawing was gone from above the fare box. That Saturday, walking home, I saw Moana on the hill above the harbor, holding the string of a red kite while a small girl in a borrowed coat ran beneath it, shouting at the wind.

options: From grief over a mother's death to relief that the letters contain no painful secrets

pub.passage: We took the letters to the bridge because the apartment was already full of boxes. Mathis, my sister, read the first one aloud in a mock-theatrical voice, and I applauded each of our mother's complaints about the price of leeks, the neighbor's dog, the rain over the Saone. "Etienne, listen to this one," she would say, and bow before reading. For half an hour it felt like a performance staged for two. Then she opened a letter dated the spring before she was born, and her voice dropped. Our mother had written that she was afraid of staying in Lyon forever, afraid she would never see the sea again. Mathis folded the page along its old crease. I thought of her plane ticket, tucked into the passport in her coat, and of how she had mentioned it to me as if mentioning the weather. Below us the river carried a single plastic bottle past the pillars, turning it slowly, never letting it sink.

pub.passage: Why did Hedwig wind the clocks backward? Kalani, the landlord's son, had noticed it on three rent days running: while her father counted coins at the bench of the little Havana shop, she moved along the wall of clocks and turned each key the wrong way, gently, until it resisted, and then let it go. He took it for a girl's idle mischief and said nothing, since his own father disliked complaints. On the fourth rent day his father asked to see the shop's account book. Hedwig's father went pale and reached for the drawer, but Hedwig was quicker; she set the book on the counter herself, opened to a page in her own neat hand, and stepped back to the clocks. Kalani, reading over his father's shoulder, saw that every entry was dated a week before the coins had truly come in. His father nodded and closed the book. Hedwig turned one more key the wrong way and looked at Kalani, and he held her gaze without a word.

pub.explanation: 어머니는 사진을 홍수 때 잃어버렸다고 생각했고 30년 만에 연 상자에서 그날 아침 우연히 발견했다. 사진에는 화자가 몰랐던 어머니의 첫 결혼이라는 과거가 담겨 있으며, 화자는 그 열쇠를 원하는지 망설인다. 따라서 잠긴 상자가 해변에 밀려왔다는 비유는 묻혀 있던 과거가 예기치 않게 떠올랐다는 뜻이므로 D가 정답이다. C는 그럴듯하지만 어머니가 일부러 숨겨 온 것이 아니라 잃어버렸다고 여긴 사진이므로 맞지 않고, A는 세관이라는 소재만, B는 어머니가 사진을 버리려 한다는 근거 없는 해석이다.
pub.explanation_en: The mother thought she had lost the photograph in a flood and found it by chance the morning she opened the chest after 30 years. The photograph holds a past the narrator did not know about, her mother's first marriage, and the narrator hesitates over whether she wants the key. Therefore, the metaphor of a locked chest washed ashore means that a buried past has unexpectedly resurfaced, so the answer is D. C is plausible, but it does not fit because the mother did not deliberately hide the photograph; she believed it was lost. A relies only on the customs detail, and B is an unsupported interpretation that the mother wants to throw the photograph away.
options: is a valuable keepsake that the customs officer must inspect
is a burden the mother has finally chosen to cast away
hides a secret the mother has carefully guarded for decades
holds a buried past that has resurfaced without warning
pub.passage: Anything to declare? asked Lorenzo, the customs officer, as my mother and I reached the little checkpoint on the Cornish coast, where an old tale says brides once paid their toll in shells. My mother had nothing but a photograph she had found that morning in a box of my grandmother's linens, a box she had not opened in thirty years. It showed her own wedding, the groom's half torn away. I had thought it lost in the flood of '89, she said, and I wanted Callum to see it before we choose the chapel. Lorenzo studied it and waved us through. On the cliff path she told me that the torn-away man had drowned off this coast before I was born, and that the man I call father had married her the next spring. The photograph was a locked chest washed ashore, and I could not decide whether I wanted the key. Gulls hung above the checkpoint roof, motionless against the wind.
