pub.explanation:
정답 D: Text 1의 논증은 '단속(나무 소각·순찰)이 재배를 네덜란드 영토에 묶어 두었다'는 가정에 기대고 있으며, 그래서 단속이 약해지자 독점이 끝났다고 결론짓는다. Text 2는 밀반출된 묘목 대부분이 죽었고, 육두구는 토양·그늘·습도 조건이 까다로우며 암수 구별에도 수년이 걸려 수십 년간 재배에 실패했다고 보고한다. 즉 다른 지역에서 재배되지 못한 주된 이유는 단속이 아니라 원예적인 어려움일 수 있다는 것이므로, 바로 이 가정을 약화한다.
A(오답): Text 1의 결론에 해당한다. Text 2는 독점이 결국 끝났다는 사실 자체를 부정하지 않고, 이유를 설명하는 방식에만 문제를 제기한다.
B(오답): 부수적인 세부 사항이다. Text 2는 반다 제도의 수비대에 대해 아무 언급도 하지 않는다.
C(오답): Text 2가 오히려 전제로 받아들이는 내용이다. 묘목이 반출되었다는 사실은 인정하고, 반출된 묘목이 대부분 죽었다는 점만 덧붙인다.
pub.explanation_en:
Correct answer, D: Text 1's argument depends on an assumption: Dutch enforcement (burning trees and running patrols) was what kept spice growing limited to Dutch-held islands. That is why Text 1 concludes the monopoly ended once enforcement weakened. Text 2 reports that most smuggled seedlings died. Nutmeg needs particular soils, shade, and humidity, and growers had to wait years to tell male trees from female ones, so attempts failed for decades. This points to the difficulty of growing the plants, not policing, as the real barrier, which weakens exactly that assumption.
A is wrong: This is Text 1's conclusion. Text 2 never denies that the monopoly eventually ended. It only questions why.
B is wrong: This is a side detail. Text 2 says nothing about the garrisons on Banda.
C is wrong: Text 2 actually accepts this point. It agrees the seedlings were taken out and then explains that most of them died.
options: The claim that the VOC's control of the spice trade could not be sustained indefinitely once the late eighteenth century arrived
The claim that garrisons were stationed on the Banda Islands to protect the nutmeg groves
The claim that agents working for Poivre managed to carry spice seedlings out of Dutch-held territory
The claim that Dutch policing was the main obstacle that kept the spices from being grown in other places
pub.passage:
Text 1
For roughly a century and a half, the Dutch East India Company (VOC) kept cloves and nutmeg scarce and expensive in European markets. Company fleets made regular "extirpation" voyages to burn unauthorized clove trees on outlying islands, and garrisons on the Banda Islands guarded the nutmeg groves. Historian Pieter Lindqvist argues that this enforcement was what confined spice cultivation to Dutch-held islands. So when the company's naval patrols thinned in the 1760s and agents of the French administrator Pierre Poivre slipped seedlings out of the region, the monopoly's days were numbered.

Text 2
Botanist Amara Siregar's review of colonial garden records from Mauritius complicates the story of the smuggled seedlings. Most of the trees that Poivre's agents carried out died within months. Nutmeg in particular proved hard to grow: it needs specific soils, shade, and steady humidity, and it requires both male and female trees, which cannot be told apart until they flower years later. Profitable plantations outside the Moluccas appeared only after decades of repeated failed attempts.

advisory.note: Text 1의 결론('독점의 날이 얼마 남지 않았다')과 근거(단속이 재배를 묶어 두었다는 Lindqvist의 주장)가 분명히 나뉘어 있다. Text 2는 원예적 어려움을 들어 이 근거 가정을 겨냥하지만, Text 1을 직접 언급하지는 않는다. 그래서 반응을 추론해야 한다. A는 결론에 해당하고, C는 Text 2가 인정하는 사실을 담은 오답이다. A가 매력적인 오답으로 작동하려면 결론과 가정을 구분해야 한다. 다만 D의 핵심 단서가 Text 1에 거의 그대로 나와 있어서('this enforcement was what confined...') 난이도는 hard 하한선에 가깝다.

hardJudge.note: Text 1은 결론(독점의 종말)과 근거(단속이 재배를 묶어 둠, Lindqvist)가 명확히 구분됨. Text 2는 밀반출 사실(C)을 전제로 받아들이고, 독점이 결국 끝났다는 결론(A)도 부정하지 않으며, 수비대(B)는 언급하지 않음. 오직 '단속이 주된 장벽'이라는 가정만 원예적 난점으로 약화 → D 정답 타당. 실존 인물 Poivre의 밀반출 시기는 엄밀히 1769–1772년이지만 '1760년대'는 허용 범위의 근사로 판단, 가공 학자명 사용은 문제 없음. 결론과 가정을 구분하고 Text 2 관점에서 Text 1의 논증 요소를 평가해야 하므로 hard 적합.

pub.answer_rationale: 밑줄 문장은 Morgan의 신호 설계가 부분적으로만 해결한 문제(불규칙한 정지·출발)를 신호 연동(progression)이 더 지속적으로 해결했다는 핵심 주장을 제시하며, 뒤이어 이 혁신의 의의를 설명하는 결론으로 이어진다.
pub.evidence_span: The more lasting solution, however, came from coordinating signal timing across entire streets so that a driver traveling at a steady speed could pass through a series of green lights without stopping.
pub.explanation: 밑줄 문장 앞에서는 경찰관의 수동 조작 방식의 문제점과 Morgan의 신호 설계가 이를 부분적으로만 해결했음을 설명한다. 밑줄 문장은 'however'로 시작하며 신호 연동이라는 더 지속적인 해결책을 제시하는 핵심 주장 역할을 하며, 뒤따르는 문장에서 이 혁신의 의의를 결론짓는다. 따라서 정답은 C번이다.
pub.explanation_en: Before the underlined sentence, the text explains the problems with police officers operating signals manually and says that Morgan's signal design addressed them only partially. The underlined sentence begins with "however" and presents the key claim, a more lasting solution in signal coordination, and the following sentence concludes with the significance of this innovation. So the answer is C.
options: To emphasize that signal progression, rather than Morgan's design alone, deserved credit for coordinating traffic across a corridor
To describe the specific mechanical components used in Garrett Morgan's original patented signal
To identify the development that resolved a limitation left unaddressed by an earlier improvement
To illustrate how the problem of inconsistent manual signal timing typically affected drivers at a single intersection
pub.passage: During the 1920s, city planners in several American cities began installing traffic signals at intersections to manage the growing number of automobiles sharing the road with pedestrians, streetcars, and horse-drawn carts. Early signals were often manually operated by police officers stationed in booths, a system that proved inconsistent because officers in different intersections along the same street frequently changed the lights at different times, causing drivers to stop and start unpredictably. Engineer Garrett Morgan's patented signal design, which introduced a distinct caution position between stop and go, addressed part of this problem by giving drivers time to slow down before a full stop. __The more lasting solution, however, came from coordinating signal timing across entire streets so that a driver traveling at a steady speed could pass through a series of green lights without stopping.__ This innovation, known as signal progression, transformed traffic engineering from a matter of managing individual intersections into a matter of managing the flow of traffic across whole corridors.

difficultyReasons: 밑줄 문장이 앞 문장(Morgan의 부분적 해결)과 뒤 문장(신호 연동의 결과)을 모두 참조해야 정확한 기능을 파악할 수 있어 추론 단계가 2단계 이상 필요함
'however'라는 대조 연결어와 'more lasting solution'이라는 표현이 무엇과 대조되는지(완전한 반박이 아니라 남은 한계 해결) 정확히 구분해야 함
오답 B는 정답과 유사하게 signal progression의 중요성을 언급하지만 '공로 논쟁'이라는 다른 프레임으로 왜곡되어 있어 표면적으로 그럴듯함
오답 D는 밑줄 문장이 아니라 그 앞 문장의 내용과 혼동하게 만들어 문장 간 경계를 명확히 구분해야 함

distractors.matches: 밑줄 문장이 'the more lasting solution, however'라며 Morgan의 해결책과 대조되는 구조를 취한 점
distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문 마지막 문장에서 signal progression이 교통 흐름 관리 방식을 바꿨다는 내용이 나오므로, 밑줄 문장이 Morgan의 공로를 깎아내리려는 의도라고 착각할 수 있다
distractors.whyWrong: 지문은 Morgan의 설계가 문제의 일부(part of this problem)만 해결했고 signal progression이 남은 문제(전체 도로 흐름)를 해결했다고 서술할 뿐, 공로를 누가 가져가야 하는지에 대한 논쟁이나 재평가를 다루지 않는다. 즉 '누구의 공로인가'라는 프레임 자체가 지문에 없다

distractors.matches: Garrett Morgan의 특허 신호(caution position)에 대한 언급
distractors.plausibleBecause: Morgan의 특허 신호 장치가 언급되어 있어 그 장치에 대한 구체적 설명이 나올 것이라 예상할 수 있다
distractors.whyWrong: 밑줄 문장은 Morgan의 장치가 아니라 signal progression이라는 전혀 다른 해결책과 그 효과(연속 녹색불 통과)를 설명하며, 기계적 구성요소에 대한 서술이 전혀 없다

distractors.matches: 수동 신호 조작의 불일치 문제(단일 교차로 단위)가 앞 문장에 등장
distractors.plausibleBecause: 바로 앞 문장에서 경찰관들이 서로 다른 시간에 신호를 바꿔 운전자들이 예측 불가능하게 멈추고 출발했다는 문제가 서술되어 있어, 밑줄 문장이 이 문제를 부연 설명한다고 오인할 수 있다
distractors.whyWrong: 밑줄 문장은 문제 상황을 묘사하는 것이 아니라 그 문제(및 Morgan의 부분적 해결책이 남긴 한계)를 해결한 새로운 방안(신호 연동)을 제시하는 문장이며, 단일 교차로가 아니라 '전체 도로(entire streets)'에 걸친 해법을 설명한다

pub.explanation: 지문은 매주 커피를 두고 가는 습관을 먼저 보여 주고, 중간에 화자가 학생 아버지의 치료비를 대신 냈다는 사실을 밝힌다. 이어 학생이 더 많은 수업을 청하자 화자는 웃지 않고 커피를 다시 바라보는데, 이는 커피와 요청이 갚지 못한 빚에 대한 학생 나름의 보답임을 깨닫는 장면이다. 따라서 D가 전개 순서를 정확히 담는다. A의 다툼, B의 후회와 수업 중단, C의 공개 칭찬은 지문에 나오지 않는다.
pub.explanation_en: The text first shows the habit of leaving coffee every week, and in the middle the narrator reveals that she paid for the student's father's medical bills. When the student then asks for more lessons, the narrator does not smile but looks at the coffee again, a scene in which she realizes that the coffee and the request are the student's own way of repaying a debt he could not pay back. So D accurately captures the sequence of development. The quarrel in A, the regret and ending of the lessons in B, and the open praise in C do not appear in the text.
options: A weekly lesson is described, and then a quarrel about payment arises that the housekeeper settles.
The narrator recalls a past kindness, regrets having offered it, and then resolves to end the lessons.
A student's eagerness for harder work is portrayed, and then the narrator decides to praise him openly.
A routine gesture is introduced, a past favor is disclosed, and a later request recasts the gesture.
pub.passage: When Anacleto came up to the terrace on Thursdays, he brought his grammar and, without fail, a small paper of coffee, which he set on the wall beside my inkstand as though it had arrived there by itself. I never thanked him, and he never waited to be thanked. We read our verbs while the bay below us went from grey to silver. Some months before, I had paid the physician who attended his father, and neither of us had spoken of it since; I believed the matter forgotten, as I had wished it to be. This Thursday, however, he recited the conditional mood without a single error and then asked, quite formally, whether I might set him harder lessons, longer ones, as many as I pleased. Rosalinda, my housekeeper, laughed from the doorway at such appetite. I did not laugh. I looked at the coffee on the wall, and then at his careful hands, which had already opened the grammar to a page we had not reached.

pub.explanation: 지문은 홍수로 아포니의 오빠가 죽었다는 사실을 언급한 직후 '둘 다 그를 말하지 않았다'고 쓰고, 물소리가 커질 때마다 아포니가 매를 가리키며 화제를 돌리고 화자가 보이지 않는 매를 바라보며 따라 주는 장면을 덧붙인다. 이 두 단서를 연결하면 '한 목초지의 가장자리를 맴돌며 이야기했다'는 표현은 두 사람이 함께 고통스러운 한 주제를 의도적으로 피했다는 뜻이므로 정답은 C이다. A는 잡담을 했다는 표면만 보고 회피의 대상이 있다는 점을 놓쳤다. B는 아포니가 이미 오빠의 죽음을 알고 있으므로 맞지 않고, D는 목초지를 문자 그대로 읽은 오답이다.
pub.explanation_en: Right after mentioning that Aponi's brother died in the flood, the text says "neither of us spoke of him," and adds that whenever the sound of the water grew louder, Aponi pointed at the hawk to change the subject, and the narrator went along by looking at the unseen hawk. Connecting these two clues, the phrase "grazed our talk around the edges of one pasture" means that the two deliberately avoided one painful subject together, so the answer is C. A looks only at the surface, that they made small talk, and misses that there is a subject being avoided. B is wrong because Aponi already knows of her brother's death, and D reads the pasture literally.
options: a habit of filling the awkwardness of a long separation with small talk.
Omar's quiet effort to shield Aponi from news she had not yet heard.
a shared, deliberate steering of conversation away from one painful subject.
a lingering dispute over the grazing land each family claimed near the bridge.
pub.passage: Tell me about the trading post first, Aponi said, before I had even set down my bundle. So I told her. We stood on the stone bridge below the mesa in the spring of 1879, a year after my family had gone east, and I described my father's ledgers and the schoolmaster's squeaking boots until she laughed. Once, when we were nine, her brother had dared us both to walk the parapet; the summer before I left, the flood had taken him from beneath these same arches. Neither of us mentioned him. For two days we grazed our talk around the edges of one pasture, wandering wide to horses, to weather, to the price of wool. Whenever the water grew loud below us, she would point out a hawk, and I would look where she pointed, though I saw no hawk. On the third evening she pressed a smooth river stone into my palm without explaining it, and I carried it east in my coat. Shadows of the arches lay long across the dry wash, and somewhere up the slope a dog was bringing the sheep down.

pub.explanation: 지문은 외부인에게는 지구력을 보여주는 공연처럼 보이는 세마 의식이 실제 수행자에게는 각 요소에 의미가 부여된 기도였다고 대조한 뒤, 망토·손바닥·회전 방향의 상징과 내면 암송 훈련으로 이를 뒷받침하므로 A가 정답이다. B는 관계를 뒤집었다. 지문은 수행자들이 신체적 기량보다 기도로서의 가치를 더 중시했다고 말한다. C는 천일 하루의 훈련이라는 세부는 맞지만, 지문은 그 훈련의 대부분이 균형이 아니라 내면 암송에 관한 것이었다고 밝힌다. D는 행성과 순례자의 회전을 언급하지만 이는 여러 상징 중 하나일 뿐이어서 모든 동작의 주된 목적으로 볼 수 없다.
pub.explanation_en: The text contrasts how the sema looks to outsiders, a feat of endurance, with how the dervishes understood it, a structured prayer in which every element had a meaning. It backs this up with the cloak, the palms, the rotation, and the inner recitation, so A is correct. B reverses the relationship: the text says the dervishes valued the spinning less as a physical feat than as prayer. C gets the long training period right, but the text says most of that training concerned inner recitation, not balance. D takes one symbol, the planets and pilgrims, and wrongly treats it as the main purpose of every gesture.
options: Although the Mevlevi ceremony may look like a test of physical stamina, its practitioners regarded the turning as a symbolically ordered act of devotion.
Although the Mevlevi ceremony began as a form of prayer, Ottoman-era dervishes came to value it mainly for the physical skill it displayed.
Although Mevlevi novices trained for a long period, most of their preparation focused on avoiding the dizziness caused by prolonged spinning.
Although the Mevlevi ceremony drew on Rumi's poetry, its gestures were designed chiefly to imitate the movements of planets and pilgrims.
pub.passage: To outside observers, the sema ceremony of the Mevlevi order, founded in thirteenth-century Konya by followers of the poet Rumi, often appears to be a performance of endurance: dancers in tall felt hats and white skirts turn for long stretches without apparent dizziness. Yet for the Ottoman-era dervishes who practiced it, the spinning was valued less as a physical feat than as a structured form of prayer. Each element of the ritual carried assigned meaning. The black cloak removed at the start represented the grave and worldly attachment; the right palm, turned upward, received divine grace, while the left, turned downward, passed that grace to the earth. Even the counterclockwise rotation around the heart was understood as aligning the body with the circling of planets and of pilgrims around the Kaaba. Novices trained for a thousand and one days before joining the ceremony, and much of that training concerned not balance but the inner recitation that was meant to accompany every turn.

At the sanatorium above the lake outside Bergen, I was the nurse who sat up with the patients who could not sleep, and Thorvald was the most stubborn of them. He would not lie down until I wheeled him to the end of the dock, where he watched the water as if a boat were due. On the fourth night he told me about his brother, a quarrel over their father's boathouse, and a letter he had written the week after and carried in his coat ever since. His brother had died the following spring. I said that someone in the family might still read the letter, and he shook his head. An apology, he said, was a door that opens from one side only. After that he spoke less and slept more. When he asked me, Sigrid, to burn the envelope in the ward stove, I did, and I noticed that he no longer looked out at the water.

Everyone at the show knew her blooms were the best, and everyone saw her withdraw her entry an hour before judging, leaving mine to win. I had brought the ribbon to return it. pub.passage: When Paloma handed me the ring of keys that morning, she bowed as if presenting a crown, and I laughed so hard I nearly dropped them. The salt-water pool behind the Dayton rec center had been hers for thirty summers; I was nineteen, her apprentice, and the aquatic park across town had just offered me twice her wage. I mentioned it while we skimmed leaves. Paloma asked whether they would give me a whistle with my name engraved on it, and maybe a manager younger than my sneakers. We traded jabs down the length of the deep end. Then, testing the water, she held the vial up to the light longer than she needed to. Her father's crew had poured these walls, she said. Every child on Fifth Street had learned to float in the shallow end, me included, and the drain still stuck each November in a way no manual explained. She did not ask me to stay. She only showed me, slowly, where to kick the grate. I set down the net. Across the water, light lay flat on the tiles, and a dragonfly kept touching the surface and lifting away.

pub.passage: Albuquerque in October smells of roasting chiles, and the seed-saving cooperative behind my church smells of paper envelopes and dust. I was labeling squash seed there when Nova walked in, eleven years after she had stopped coming to Mass, and asked whether we still needed volunteers. Yona, who runs the cooperative and has opinions about everyone, raised her eyebrows at me over the scale. I asked Nova nothing beyond whether she knew beans from squash. She said she had grown up sorting both. I have heard a great many confessions, and I have come to distrust the long ones; the shortest are often followed, much later, by the true account. So I let the afternoon pass in envelopes. Nova sorted the speckled bean seed from the plain faster than I could, pausing only once, over a packet labeled in her late grandmother's slanted script, which she set aside without comment. I did not ask about it. By evening the long table was covered in small brown packets, and I found that she had labeled each of hers in a hand very much like the one on the packet she had set aside.

pub.explanation:
지문은 영구 융합 전략이 '암수의 만남이 극히 드문 경우에만' 의미가 있다고 말하고, 독립적으로 사는 종은 개체군 밀도가 더 높아 수컷이 다른 암컷을 다시 만날 가능성이 있다는 연구 결과를 제시한다. 이 두 정보를 종합하면, 융합 전략은 개체군 밀도가 낮아 수컷이 이후 다른 암컷을 다시 만날 가능성이 극히 낮은 상황에서 진화했다고 추론할 수 있다. 
B는 이 관계를 정확히 포착한다.
A는 '개체군 밀도가 종마다 다르다'는 사실 자체만 언급할 뿐, 그 차이가 재만남 가능성과 연결되어 융합 전략을 설명한다는 핵심 인과관계를 빠뜨려 범위가 지나치게 좁다(WRONG_SCOPE).
C는 지문에 없는 '정자 공급'이라는 무관한 세부사항을 끌어온다(IRRELEVANT_DETAIL).
D는 심해 생물 전반의 번식 행동이라는, 지문이 다루는 앵귀상어 종 간 비교를 넘어선 지나치게 넓은 일반화다(OVERREACH).
pub.explanation_en:
The text says the permanent-fusion strategy makes sense only when meetings between the sexes are extremely rare, and it presents research finding that species living independently have higher population densities, so males may meet other females again. Combining these two pieces of information, we can infer that the fusion strategy evolved under low population density, where a male is extremely unlikely to meet another female later. B captures this relationship exactly.
A only mentions the fact that population density varies by species and omits the key causal link that the difference relates to the chance of meeting again and explains the fusion strategy, so its scope is too narrow (WRONG_SCOPE).
C pulls in an irrelevant detail, the sperm supply, that is not in the text (IRRELEVANT_DETAIL).
D is an overly broad generalization about the reproductive behavior of deep-sea organisms as a whole, going beyond the comparison between anglerfish species that the text deals with (OVERREACH).
options: the fact that population densities vary considerably among different species of deep-sea anglerfish
the extremely low likelihood that a male will locate more than one female across the sparsely populated deep sea
the fact that male anglerfish, once fused, provide the female with a steady supply of sperm for repeated fertilization over many years
the tendency of deep-sea species in general to evolve unusual reproductive behaviors over time
pub.passage: Marine biologists studying the deep-sea anglerfish have long puzzled over how males, which are dramatically smaller than females, manage to find mates in the vast darkness of the ocean depths. Some species solve this problem through a permanent physical fusion: upon locating a female, the male bites into her body and gradually merges with her tissue, eventually sharing her bloodstream and losing his own digestive organs. This extreme strategy makes sense only if encounters between the sexes are exceedingly rare events. Researchers have found that in species where males retain independent digestive systems and free-swimming ability throughout adulthood, population densities tend to be considerably higher than in species exhibiting permanent fusion. In these higher-density species, a male that separates from one female after mating retains a reasonable chance of encountering another receptive female later on, since individuals of both sexes are more frequently within range of one another. This pattern suggests that the evolution of permanent sexual parasitism among anglerfish is closely tied to ______.

pub.passage:
Text 1

Recent excavations of Bronze Age settlements in the eastern Mediterranean have uncovered large communal grain silos located at the center of villages rather than within individual households. Archaeologists studying these sites argue that this arrangement reflects a cooperative economic system in which grain surplus was pooled and redistributed by community leaders, reducing the risk that any single family would starve during a poor harvest. The consistent placement of these silos in public areas, often near ceremonial structures, further suggests that communal storage was tied to shared religious authority rather than private wealth accumulation.

Text 2

The interpretation of centrally located grain silos as evidence of egalitarian, cooperative economies deserves scrutiny. In several excavated villages, the silos nearest the ceremonial structures contained noticeably larger stores of grain than smaller silos scattered elsewhere, and skeletal remains from elite burials in the same period show better nutrition than those from ordinary households. This pattern is more consistent with a system in which local leaders controlled and unevenly distributed the communal surplus, using access to stored grain as a source of political power rather than a mechanism for protecting the whole community from famine.

pub.passage: Rain beaded on the manuscript pages Jiayi had carried to the stone bridge, and she shielded them with her sleeve while Haoran read. He had translated four of her novels and liked to say that he read her endings first, the way some people taste the sauce before the noodles. Tonight he lingered over the opening chapters, laughing aloud at a scene in a fish market and quoting a line about a stubborn aunt back to her twice. Jiayi teased him for performing, and he bowed to the lanterns as if they were an audience. When he reached the last pages, he read them quickly, squared the stack, and began to tell her about a noodle shop that had opened behind the temple. She waited for the joke about the sauce. He offered her the pages instead, holding them by the corners so the rain would not spot the final chapter, the one she had rewritten six times. Traffic hissed over the wet stones. Jiayi tucked the manuscript under her coat and asked, in an even voice, whether the shop stayed open late.

pub.passage: Bao did not like surprises. As captain of the river freighter, he had found Wira curled among the rice sacks two days out, and now, docked below the terraced hills outside Hanoi, he had brought the boy home to eat because there was nowhere else to put him. Bao's mother set out bowls and chopsticks with the precision she gave to every meal. Wira, from an island far to the south, hesitated, then began eating with his right hand as his family always had. Bao waited for the small frown he had known since childhood. Instead his mother watched a moment, set down her chopsticks, and tore a piece of rice cake with her fingers. Bao felt the meal tilt on its hinge. Later Wira picked up the chopsticks and fumbled a dumpling into his lap, and Bao's mother laughed, a sound Bao had not heard at that table in years. Mist gathered over the terraces, erasing the lower paddies one by one.

pub.passage: Who goes to the cinema in Tromso in May, when the sun refuses to set and no one needs the dark? Anders asked himself this as he bought a ticket from a girl reading a magazine. Inside, the theater held eleven people, and one of them was Anneke, who had not come to Mass in three years. She waved with easy warmth, and Anders, who had rehearsed several gentle reproaches over the years, found he wanted none of them. They traded complaints about the stale popcorn and the price of parking. Then Anneke's daughter leaned across her mother's lap. "Why don't we go to church anymore? You said Father Anders moved away." Anneke laughed a little too quickly and said children mix everything up. Anders laughed as well, and agreed that he did travel a great deal. He began folding his ticket stub into smaller and smaller squares. When the lights finally dimmed, he found himself studying the advertisements with unusual care.

빈칸 앞 문장은 도덕적 담론이 지속되어 화가와 후원자들이 물질과 영성 사이의 긴장을 의식하게 되었다는 '원인'을 제시하고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 이로부터 그림들이 문화적 불안을 반영한다는 '결과'를 도출한다. 따라서 인과 관계를 나타내는 'As a result,'(B)가 정답이다.

'For example,'(A)은 뒤 문장이 앞 내용의 구체적 사례여야 하는데, 뒤 문장은 예시가 아니라 앞의 원인으로부터 도출된 결론이므로 예시 관계로 보면 틀리다.

'In fact,'(C)는 앞 문장의 내용을 더 강한 표현으로 재확인·강조할 때 쓰이는데, 뒤 문장은 앞 문장과 같은 내용을 강조하는 것이 아니라 그로부터 새로운 결과를 이끌어내는 것이므로 강조 관계로 보면 인과 관계를 놓치게 된다.

'However,'(D)는 앞 문장과 반대되거나 대조되는 내용이 와야 하는데, 뒤 문장은 앞 내용과 상충하지 않고 그것을 원인으로 자연스럽게 이어지는 결과이므로 대조 관계로 보면 틀리다.
pub.explanation_en:
The sentence before the blank presents a cause: the ongoing moral discourse made painters and patrons aware of the tension between materiality and spirituality. The sentence after the blank draws a result from it: the paintings reflect cultural anxiety. Therefore, "As a result," (B), which signals cause and effect, is correct.

"For example," (A) would require the next sentence to be a specific instance of the previous idea, but the next sentence is a conclusion drawn from the earlier cause, not an example, so reading it as an example relationship is wrong.

"In fact," (C) is used to reaffirm or emphasize the previous sentence in stronger terms, but the next sentence does not emphasize the same content; it draws a new result from it, so treating it as emphasis misses the cause-and-effect relationship.

"However," (D) requires content that contrasts with or opposes the previous sentence, but the next sentence does not conflict with the earlier content; it follows naturally from it as a result, so reading it as a contrast is wrong.
options: For example,
As a result,
In fact,
However,
pub.passage: Art historians studying the Dutch Golden Age have generally attributed the rapid rise of still-life painting in the seventeenth century to the growing wealth of merchant-class patrons who wanted decorative, secular art for their homes rather than religious commissions for churches. This economic explanation accounts for the sheer volume of still-life production, but it struggles to explain a more specific puzzle: why so many of these paintings incorporated hidden symbols of mortality, such as wilting flowers, half-peeled fruit, or extinguished candles, tucked among otherwise celebratory displays of abundance. A closer look at sermons and moral literature circulating in Dutch cities during this period reveals that vanitas themes, warning against the vanity of earthly pleasures, were a dominant strain of public religious discourse even as church commissions declined. Because this moral discourse continued to shape how ordinary citizens thought about wealth and mortality, painters and patrons alike remained conscious of the tension between material display and spiritual warning. ______ the paintings may reflect not simply new patrons' tastes but a broader cultural anxiety about material wealth that persisted independently of formal religious institutions.

distractors.plausibleBecause: 빈칸 뒤 문장이 앞 내용을 강조하거나 재확인하는 것처럼 읽힐 수 있어 '사실'이라는 강조 표현이 어울려 보일 수 있다
distractors.whyWrong: In fact는 앞 내용을 더 강하게 확증하는 뉘앙스인데, 뒤 문장은 새로운 결론(해석의 확장/재해석)을 이끄는 것이므로 단순 강조가 아니라 논리적 귀결(따라서)의 관계임

pub.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

pub.explanation:
정답 B: Farouk의 기준은 '여러 독립적 증거 유형이 동시에 한 경로를 지지할 때만' 신뢰할 수 있다는 것이다. Reyes는 도자기·문헌을 검토하지 않고 동전만으로 확정했으므로, 적합도가 아무리 높아도 Farouk 기준으로는 성급하다(그녀는 단일 증거에 대한 밀접한 일치가 매장·발굴 위치의 편향일 수 있다고 경고함).
A: Text 2 저자(Reyes)의 기준, 즉 동전 증거의 밀도·일관성으로 평가한 것이다. Farouk에게 단일 증거의 양은 핵심이 아니다.
C: 두 기준의 혼합이다. 신중함은 Farouk처럼 보이지만, 보완책을 '동전을 더 모으는 것'으로 제시해 독립적 증거 유형의 교차 확인이라는 Farouk의 기준을 놓친다.
D: 일반 상식적 회의론이다. Farouk는 동전 증거 자체를 무가치하다고 보지 않으며, 동전은 여러 증거 중 하나로 인정된다. 또한 Reyes의 동전은 명확한 연대 순서를 보인다.
pub.explanation_en:
Answer B: Farouk's standard is that a route can be trusted only when several independent types of evidence support it at the same time. Reyes did not examine pottery or written sources and settled on a route from coins alone, so no matter how close the fit is, it is premature by Farouk's standard (she warns that a close match based on a single type of evidence may reflect bias in where hoards were buried or excavated).
A: This evaluates the claim by Text 2's author (Reyes)'s standard, namely the density and consistency of the coin evidence. For Farouk, the quantity of single-type evidence is not the key point.
C: This is a mixture of the two standards. The caution looks like Farouk's, but proposing to gather more coins as the remedy misses her standard of cross-checking across independent types of evidence.
D: This is generic commonsense skepticism. Farouk does not consider coin evidence worthless in itself; she accepts coins as one piece of evidence among several. Also, Reyes's coins show a clear dating sequence.
options: She would regard the conclusion as well founded, since the size of the hoard database and the orderly east-to-west dating make it unlikely that the pattern arose by chance.
She would view the conclusion as premature, because the route's close fit rests on a single type of evidence that has not yet been checked against other independent sources.
She would consider the route plausible but would argue that Reyes should describe it as probable rather than certain until the database is expanded with additional coin finds.
She would reject the conclusion outright, because coin hoards are generally too rare and poorly dated to reveal anything reliable about ancient trade.
pub.passage:
Text 1
Historians of medieval trade routes often reconstruct caravan paths from scattered finds of coins. The historian Leila Farouk argues that such reconstructions deserve confidence only when a single path explains finds from several independent kinds of evidence at once—coins, but also pottery styles, place-names, and written itineraries. A route that fits one kind of evidence very closely but has no support from the others, she warns, may simply reflect where coins happened to be buried or dug up.

Text 2
Using a newly compiled database of more than four hundred coin hoards, archaeologist Tomas Reyes has mapped a previously unrecognized northern caravan route across the steppe. The hoards line up along the proposed path with remarkable precision, and their dates form a clear sequence from east to west. Although no pottery or documents from the region have yet been examined, Reyes concludes that the coin evidence alone is so dense and so consistent that the route should now be considered firmly established.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 Farouk의 다중 독립 증거 기준을 그대로 적용한 결과다. A는 Reyes의 기준, B는 두 관점을 섞은 혼합형 함정(동전만 더 모으라는 보완책), D는 강도를 넘어선 과잉 거부다. 다만 Text 2에 '도자기·문헌 미검토'가 명시되어 있어 추론 거리는 짧다. 그래서 hard 중에서도 쉬운 편이다.

hardJudge.note: Text 1 explicitly states Farouk's criterion (multiple independent evidence types must converge; close fit to one type alone may reflect burial/discovery bias). Text 2 gives Reyes's conclusion resting on coins alone with pottery/documents unexamined, so it is directly judgeable. C follows uniquely from Farouk's standard. A applies Reyes's own density/consistency standard; B mixes Farouk-like caution with Reyes's single-evidence remedy (more coins); D overstates to blanket rejection Farouk never endorses. Explanation is accurate and consistent. Fictional scholars/data; no copyright concern. Standard SAT paired-passage format and length.

pub.question: Based on the texts, how would Farouk (Text 1) most likely evaluate Reyes's conclusion in Text 2?

pub.answer_rationale: Text 2는 유화의 기술적 이점을 완전히 부정하지 않으면서도 그것을 '부차적 정당화'로 격하시키고 후원자 수요를 주된 원인으로 제시하므로, Text 1의 기술 중심 인과 주장에 대해 원인의 우선순위를 뒤바꾸는 방식으로 반응한다.
pub.evidence_span: workshops adopted oil paint largely because patron demand for a new kind of artwork made the medium economically necessary, with its technical qualities serving as a secondary justification rather than the primary cause
pub.evidence_target: Text 2는 Text 1이 강조하는 유화의 기술적 장점을 부수적 요인으로 격하시키고, 후원자의 경제적·사회적 수요를 유화 채택의 주된 원인으로 제시하여 Text 1의 인과 설명을 뒤바꾼다.
pub.explanation: Text 1은 유화가 천천히 마르는 성질 덕분에 색을 부드럽게 혼합할 수 있어 화가들이 기술적 이유로 유화를 채택했다고 주장한다. Text 2는 부유한 상인 후원자들이 휴대 가능한 패널 회화를 주문하게 되면서 유화의 내구성과 적합성이 상업적으로 매력적이었고, 이러한 후원자 수요가 유화 채택의 주된 원인이며 기술적 장점은 부차적 정당화에 불과했다고 주장한다. 따라서 Text 2의 저자는 Text 1의 '기술적 이점이 주된 원인'이라는 주장에 대해, 실제 주된 원인은 후원자 수요이고 기술적 이점은 이차적이었다고 반박할 것이므로 정답은 C이다. A는 Text 2가 주장하지 않은 '템페라가 기술적으로 우월했다'는 내용으로 지문에 없는 주장이다(IRRELEVANT_COMBINATION). B는 Text 1의 입장(기술이 유일한 원인)을 Text 2에 잘못 귀속시키면서 동시에 Text 2가 실제로 강조하는 후원자의 영향력을 부정하여 지문 내용을 뒤집는다(MISATTRIBUTED_STANCE). D는 Text 2가 언급하지 않은 프레스코의 완전한 소멸이라는 과장된 주장으로 한 지문의 세부만을 왜곡한 것이다(SINGLE_TEXT_ONLY).
pub.explanation_en: Text 1 claims that oil paint's slow drying allowed colors to be blended smoothly, so painters adopted oil for technical reasons. Text 2 claims that as wealthy merchant patrons began to commission portable panel paintings, oil's durability and suitability made it commercially attractive, that this patron demand was the main cause of oil's adoption, and that the technical advantages were only a secondary justification. Therefore, the author of Text 2 would respond to Text 1's claim that technical advantages were the main cause by arguing that the real main cause was patron demand and that the technical advantages were secondary, so the answer is C. A claims that tempera was technically superior, which Text 2 never argues and which is not in the passage (IRRELEVANT_COMBINATION). B attributes Text 1's position (technology as the only cause) to Text 2 while denying the patrons' influence that Text 2 actually emphasizes, reversing the content of the passage (MISATTRIBUTED_STANCE). D is an exaggerated claim about the complete disappearance of frescoes that Text 2 does not mention, distorting only one detail of a single text (SINGLE_TEXT_ONLY).
options: By insisting that tempera remained technically superior to oil paint throughout the fifteenth century

By conceding that oil's technical qualities contributed to its appeal, but maintaining that patrons' desire for durable panel paintings mattered only after workshops had already begun favoring oil for its blending advantages
By arguing that patron demand for portable panel paintings, not oil's blending capabilities, was the primary force behind its adoption, with technical benefits playing a secondary role

By pointing out that Text 1 overlooks how patrons' preference for durable, portable panel paintings—not oil's slow-drying blending properties—explains why frescoes gradually became less common in workshops that shifted to oil
pub.passage:
Text 1

Art historians who study the shift from tempera to oil paint in fifteenth-century European workshops often emphasize technical advantages as the driving cause of the transition. Oil paint dries more slowly than tempera, allowing artists to blend colors gradually on the canvas and achieve subtle gradations of light and shadow that tempera's quick-drying surface made difficult. These historians argue that once painters recognized oil's capacity for richer modeling of form, workshops across Italy and northern Europe adopted the new medium primarily because it expanded what was technically achievable on canvas.

Text 2

Other historians studying the same transition argue that economic and social pressures, not technical capability alone, drove the shift to oil paint. They note that wealthy merchant patrons increasingly commissioned portable panel paintings for private homes rather than large frescoes for public spaces, and oil paint's durability and suitability for such panels made it commercially attractive independent of its blending properties. These historians contend that workshops adopted oil paint largely because patron demand for a new kind of artwork made the medium economically necessary, with its technical qualities serving as a secondary justification rather than the primary cause.

pub.explanation_en: The conditions are $8x + 15y \le 240$ and $x \ge 5$. Checking the point $(6, 10)$: $x = 6 \ge 5$ is satisfied, and $8(6) + 15(10) = 48 + 150 = 198 \le 240$ is also satisfied. pub.passage: A museum curator is planning an exhibit space and wants to display paintings and sculptures together. Each painting requires 8 square feet of wall space, and each sculpture requires 15 square feet of floor space. The exhibit has at most 240 square feet of combined space available for these two types of art. The curator also wants to display at least 5 paintings. Let $x$ represent the number of paintings and $y$ represent the number of sculptures. The graph shows the boundary lines $x = 5$ and $8x + 15y = 240$, with the solution to the system of inequalities shown as the set of points satisfying both $x \ge 5$ and $8x + 15y \le 240$.

pub.explanation_en: The text's central point is that abrupt collapse of ice-rich permafrost (thermokarst) boosts methane release and strengthens a feedback loop, so models that assume only gradual thaw likely understate permafrost's contribution to warming. That makes D correct. A gets the detail about oxygen-poor ponds producing methane right, but the text never says methane emissions exceed carbon dioxide emissions or that methane is the main driver of Arctic warming. B cites the "less than a fifth" figure but reaches the opposite conclusion, since the text says abrupt thaw could roughly double the projected impact. C claims a point of no return has been passed, which the text explicitly says is not the researchers' conclusion.
options: Because thermokarst ponds lack oxygen, microbes in permafrost regions now emit more methane than carbon dioxide, making methane the main driver of Arctic warming.
Because abrupt thaw affects less than a fifth of the permafrost region, its contribution to Arctic warming is likely to remain minor compared with that of gradual thaw.
Because permafrost has begun collapsing abruptly, the Arctic has likely passed a point beyond which further warming cannot be prevented.
Because sudden ground collapse can intensify a self-reinforcing cycle of thaw and warming, models assuming only slow thaw probably underestimate permafrost's climate effect.
pub.passage:
For decades, climate models treated Arctic permafrost largely as a passive store of carbon, frozen soil that would thaw gradually and release its methane and carbon dioxide at a slow, predictable pace. Field research led by ecologist Merritt Turetsky has complicated that picture. Her team found that in ice-rich permafrost, thawing does not simply proceed downward a few centimeters each year; instead, melting ground ice can cause the land surface to collapse abruptly, forming slumps and ponds known as thermokarst. These waterlogged depressions create oxygen-poor conditions in which microbes produce methane, a greenhouse gas far more potent than carbon dioxide over short periods.

Because the warming caused by this methane can in turn thaw more permafrost, abrupt thaw strengthens a feedback loop that models built around gradual thaw tend to underestimate. Turetsky and her colleagues estimate that although abrupt thaw is likely to affect less than a fifth of the permafrost region, it could roughly double the climate impact projected from gradual thaw alone. Their conclusion is not that the Arctic has already passed a point of no return, but that projections ignoring sudden ground collapse may substantially understate how much permafrost will contribute to future warming.

'reflecting the conviction of'는 현재분사로 앞 절 전체를 수식하며 'its founders'와 결합해 '설립자들의 신념'이라는 의미를 정확히 전달한다. 'which reflecting the conviction of'는 관계대명사 뒤에 정동사 없이 분사만 와서 비문이다. 'a practice that reflect the conviction of'는 관계절 동사가 단수 선행사 'a practice'와 수가 맞지 않는다(reflects여야 함). 'reflecting the convictions they held for'는 복수 'convictions'를 써서 설립자들이 여러 개별 신념을 가졌다는 잘못된 의미를 만들고 뒤의 'that no single medium...' 절과도 연결되지 않는다. 따라서 정답은 A이다.
pub.explanation_en: The main clause "Students moved fluidly between workshops..." is already complete, so what follows must be a participial phrase explaining what this whole behavior reflects. "Reflecting the conviction of" is a present participle that modifies the whole preceding clause, and combined with "its founders" it conveys the founders' single shared belief. "Which reflecting the conviction of" places a participle after a relative pronoun with no finite verb, which is ungrammatical. "A practice that reflect the conviction of" has a relative-clause verb that does not agree with the singular antecedent "a practice" (it should be "reflects"). "Reflecting the convictions they held for" uses the plural "convictions," suggesting the founders held several separate beliefs, and it does not connect to the "that no single medium..." clause. Therefore, the answer is A.
options: reflecting the conviction of
which reflecting the conviction of
a practice that reflect the conviction of
reflecting the convictions they held for

pub.passage: The phrase "triangular trade" is often used to describe Atlantic commerce from the sixteenth to the nineteenth centuries: European manufactured goods shipped to West Africa, enslaved Africans carried across the Atlantic to the Americas, and sugar, tobacco, and cotton returned to Europe. The image is tidy, and it does capture how profits in one region depended on labor and markets in the others. Historians such as David Eltis, however, have argued that the triangle misrepresents how most voyages actually operated. Shipping records show that many vessels did not complete all three legs; ships that delivered captives to the Caribbean frequently sailed home with little cargo, while plantation goods crossed the ocean on separate, specialized ships. Moreover, a large share of the trade to Brazil ran directly between Brazilian and African ports, with tobacco and rum from Bahia exchanged for captives in Angola and the Bight of Benin, bypassing Europe entirely. For these historians, the system is better understood as a web of overlapping routes than as a single closed loop.

pub.answer_rationale: "Featuring" is a present participial phrase that correctly modifies "the revised routes" without needing its own subject or creating a second independent clause.
pub.evidence_span: The revised routes, ______ dedicated lanes and synchronized traffic signals, cut average commute times by nearly twenty percent within the first year.
pub.explanation: 이 문장에는 이미 주절의 동사 "cut"이 있으므로, 삽입된 구는 주어와 동사를 갖춘 완전한 절이 아니라 명사 "routes"를 수식하는 분사구여야 한다. "featuring"은 정동사 없이 "routes"를 자연스럽게 수식하는 현재분사구다. "which featured"는 관계절이지만 콤마 두 개 사이에서 앞의 "the revised routes"를 수식하려면 문법적으로는 가능해 보이나 문장 구조상 뒤의 "cut" 동사와 어울려 전체 문장이 두 개의 서술을 나란히 놓은 듯 어색해지고, "they featured"는 별도의 독립절을 콤마로 이어 붙여 콤마 스플라이스 오류를 만든다. "having been featured"는 수동 완료분사로 시제·태가 어색하며 논리적으로 노선이 스스로 특징을 갖는 것이 아니라 "갖추어진" 대상이 되어 의미가 왜곡된다. 따라서 정답은 A번이다.
pub.explanation_en: The sentence already has the main verb 'cut,' so the inserted phrase must be a participial phrase modifying the noun 'routes,' not a full clause with a subject and verb. 'Featuring' is a present participial phrase that naturally modifies 'routes' without a finite verb. 'Which featured' is a relative clause, and between two commas it may look grammatically possible for modifying 'the revised routes,' but combined with the later verb 'cut' it makes the sentence read awkwardly, like two predicates set side by side. 'They featured' joins a separate independent clause with a comma, creating a comma splice error. 'Having been featured' is a passive perfect participle whose tense and voice are awkward, and it distorts the meaning because the routes become things that were 'featured' rather than things that themselves have features. Therefore, the answer is A.
options: featuring
which featuring
they featured
having been featured
pub.passage: Urban planners in Bogotá redesigned the city's bus rapid transit corridors to reduce congestion during peak commuting hours. The revised routes, ______ dedicated lanes and synchronized traffic signals, cut average commute times by nearly twenty percent within the first year.

difficultyReasons: 콤마 뒤 삽입구의 문법적 기능(분사구 vs 관계절 vs 독립절)을 구분해야 함
comma splice 오류를 알아채려면 두 절이 독립절인지 판단하는 추론이 필요함
which와 featuring의 차이는 형태상 유사해 보여 한 단계 이상의 문법 지식이 필요함
having been featured의 시제 뉘앙스까지 고려해야 하므로 단순 암기로는 풀기 어려움

distractors.matches: routes 뒤에 삽입절로서 dedicated lanes와 synchronized signals를 설명하는 부분과 형태적으로 어울려 보임
distractors.plausibleBecause: which은 관계절을 이끄는 일반적 방법으로 앞 명사구(routes)를 수식하는 것처럼 보여 자연스러워 보인다
distractors.whyWrong: which는 계속적 용법 관계대명사로 사용 가능하지만, 이 문장은 이미 콤마로 분리된 삽입 수식구가 필요하며 which를 쓰면 두 개의 독립된 절 구조가 어색해지지 않지만 실제로는 콤마+which는 비제한적 관계절로 문법적으로 가능함에도 문장 전체 의미상 routes가 주어 The revised routes...cut... 구조에서 which절이 삽입되면 동사 cut의 주어가 명확치 않게 되어 어색함이 발생하여 오답으로 처리됨

distractors.matches: routes(복수 명사)와 they의 수 일치가 맞아떨어짐
distractors.plausibleBecause: they가 routes를 가리키는 대명사로 자연스럽게 이어지는 것처럼 보임
distractors.whyWrong: 콤마 뒤에 they featured를 쓰면 두 개의 독립절이 콤마로만 연결되어 콤마 스플라이스(comma splice) 오류가 발생함

distractors.plausibleBecause: 현재분사가 이미 정답으로 사용되므로 이 항목은 해당 없음

distractors.matches: 수동의 의미(featured가 수동으로 사용된 점)와 일부 맥락상 어울림
distractors.plausibleBecause: 완료형 분사가 원인이나 배경을 나타내는 것처�core 럼 보여 격식있는 문장에서 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.whyWrong: having been featured는 완료 수동분사로 '이미 특징지어진 상태였다'는 시간적 선행 의미를 나타내는데, 본문에서는 노선이 차선과 신호를 '갖추고 있다'는 동시적/현재 상태를 나타내야 하므로 시제 관계가 맞지 않고 문장도 어색해짐

issues: 'which featured'가 문법적으로 왜 부적절한지에 대한 해설 설명이 다소 모호함(실제로는 문법적으로 완전히 타당한 관계절이며, 의미상으로도 큰 문제가 없어 C와 경합할 수 있음). 해설에서 'A가 어색해지는 이유'를 더 명확한 문법적 근거(예: 콤마 사이의 비제한적 관계절이 실제로는 문법적으로 허용되는 표현이라 정답 C와의 변별력이 약함)로 보완할 필요가 있음.

pub.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

pub.answer_rationale: 분사구 "having reviewed over two hundred community submissions"는 콤마 뒤에 바로 오는 "the planning committee"를 논리적 주어로 삼아 자연스럽게 수식하므로 댕글링 모디파이어가 발생하지 않는다.
pub.evidence_span: After months of public hearings, ______, the planning committee ultimately approved a compromise
pub.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에는 ", the planning committee ultimately approved ..."라는 완전한 문장이 이어지므로 빈칸에는 이 문장 앞에 놓이는 삽입 수식어구가 들어가야 하고, 그 수식어구의 논리적 주어는 뒤의 주어 "the planning committee"여야 한다. "having reviewed over two hundred community submissions"는 완료분사구로 이 조건을 만족하며 문법적으로 완결된다. "which having reviewed..."는 관계대명사 뒤에 정동사 없이 분사만 와서 비문이다. "reviewing ... had"는 동사 형태가 뒤섞여 비문이다. 마지막 선택지는 "submissions and" 뒤에 곧바로 쉼표가 이어져 접속사 뒤에 연결할 대상이 없다. 따라서 정답은 B이다.
pub.explanation_en: After the blank comes a complete sentence, ", the planning committee ultimately approved ...," so the blank must hold an introductory modifier whose logical subject is "the planning committee." "Having reviewed over two hundred community submissions" is a perfect participial phrase that does this and is grammatically complete. "Which having reviewed..." puts a participle after a relative pronoun with no finite verb, which is ungrammatical. "Reviewing ... had" mixes verb forms and is ungrammatical. The last choice ends with "and" directly before the comma, so the conjunction connects nothing. So the answer is B.
options: which having reviewed over two hundred community submissions
having reviewed over two hundred community submissions
reviewing over two hundred community submissions had
having reviewed over two hundred community submissions and
pub.passage: Urban planners redesigning the light-rail network in Ho Chi Minh City faced a difficult choice: extend the existing lines into flood-prone districts or reroute them through denser commercial corridors. After months of public hearings, ______, the planning committee ultimately approved a compromise that combined both proposals.

difficultyReasons: 분사구문(having reviewed)과 관계절(which had reviewed)의 문법적 차이를 구분해야 함(1단계)
동사 형태가 깨진 오답(reviewing...had)을 제외하는 것은 쉬움
D는 문법적으로는 맞지만 불필요한 정보 추가로 간결성 위반임을 판단해야 하므로 약간의 판단력 필요(2단계)
전체적으로 구조 파악 후 간결성 비교까지 요구되어 medium 수준

distractors.matches: months of public hearings 뒤에 부가 정보를 덧붙이는 자리라는 점과 일치
distractors.plausibleBecause: 관계대명사 which로 앞 내용을 수식하는 방식은 흔한 문장 구조이며 의미상 '검토했던' 것을 나타내려는 의도로 보임
distractors.whyWrong: which 앞에 선행사가 없고(콤마 뒤에 이어지는 절인데 which가 가리킬 명사가 불분명), 문장 전체가 'After ~ hearings, [X], the committee approved...'의 구조에서 X 자리에 동사가 있는 완전한 절(which had reviewed...)이 들어가면 주절 앞에 종속절이 두 개 겹쳐 비문이 되거나 문법적으로 어색한 구조가 됨. having 분사구가 위원회를 수식하는 것이 자연스러움

distractors.matches: 검토했다는 의미적 내용은 지문과 일치
distractors.plausibleBecause: reviewing과 had를 결합해 진행/완료의 느낌을 주려는 시도로 보이나 문법적으로 어색함
distractors.whyWrong: 동사구 'reviewing ... had'는 문법적으로 성립하지 않는 비문이며 술어 구조가 깨져 있음

distractors.matches: having reviewed 구조가 정답과 완전히 동일하여 문법적으로는 맞음
distractors.plausibleBecause: having 분사구 자체는 정답과 동일한 올바른 문법 구조이며 추가 정보(주민 편지)가 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.whyWrong: 내용이 장황해지고 'carefully'라는 부사가 불필요하게 추가되어 간결성과 표준 영어 관습(간결하고 명확한 수식) 위반; 또한 원문에는 residents' letters에 대한 언급이 없어 지문에 없는 정보를 추가하는 것으로 SAT 문법 문제에서는 보통 더 간결한 표현이 선호됨

issues: D 선택지에 대한 해설이 다소 약함: 'residents' letters carefully'가 '어색하다'는 이유만으로 오답 처리하는 것은 문법적 근거라기보다 문체적 판단에 가까움. D도 분사구문 자체는 문법적으로 B와 동일한 구조(주어 일치)를 가지므로, 왜 명확히 틀렸는지(예: 부사 'carefully'의 위치 오류, 병렬 구조 파괴 등)에 대한 더 구체적인 문법적 근거가 필요함
선택지 D의 경우 단순히 내용이 길어지고 부가 정보가 추가된 것뿐이며 문법적으로 명백한 오류라 보기 어려워, 단일 정답으로서의 배타성이 다소 약할 수 있음

pub.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

pub.answer_rationale: Option A places 'Noether' right after the introductory participial phrase, so the phrase correctly modifies the person who did the 'spending years working,' and it joins the two independent clauses with the coordinating conjunction 'and,' which accurately reflects a simple sequential relationship rather than an overstated causal one.
pub.evidence_span: Having spent years working without pay or formal academic rank because of restrictions on women's employment at German universities, ______ her insight was eventually recognized
pub.explanation: 이 문장은 'Having spent years working without pay...'라는 분사구문으로 시작하는데, 분사구문의 의미상 주어는 콤마 뒤에 오는 문장의 주어와 같아야 한다. '급여 없이 오랜 세월 일한' 주체는 노에터 자신이므로 빈칸 뒤 주어는 'Noether'여야 한다. C는 'Noether persisted in her research despite these obstacles, and'로 시작해 분사구가 정확히 노에터를 수식하고, 등위접속사 'and'로 두 독립절을 자연스럽게 연결한다. A는 분사구가 'the obstacles'를, B는 'her persistence'를, D는 'Noether's persistence'를 수식하게 되어 '급여 없이 일한' 주체가 사람이 아닌 대상이 되는 현수 수식어 오류다. 따라서 정답은 C이다.
pub.explanation_en: The sentence begins with the participial phrase "Having spent years working without pay...," and such a phrase must modify the subject that comes right after it. The one who worked without pay has to be Noether herself, so "Noether" must be the subject after the blank. C begins "Noether persisted in her research despite these obstacles, and," so the phrase correctly modifies Noether, and "and" joins two independent clauses. In A the phrase modifies "the obstacles," in B "her persistence," and in D "Noether's persistence," so the one who "worked without pay" would be a thing instead of a person, which is a dangling modifier. So the answer is C.
options: the obstacles that had limited her research were overcome, and
her persistence in her research despite these obstacles, so
Noether persisted in her research despite these obstacles, and
Noether's persistence in her research, despite these obstacles, meant that
pub.passage: The mathematician Emmy Noether developed a theorem in 1915 connecting symmetries in physical systems to conservation laws, a result now central to modern theoretical physics. Having spent years working without pay or formal academic rank because of restrictions on women's employment at German universities, ______ her insight was eventually recognized as one of the most important theoretical results in the field.

difficultyReasons: 분사구문의 의미상 주어를 정확히 파악해야 하는 dangling modifier 문제로 추론 단계가 여러 개 필요함
오답 B와 D 모두 표면적으로 문법적으로 그럴듯해 보이며 정답과 상당 부분 어휘를 공유함(these obstacles, persistence 등)
오답 C는 인과관계의 미묘한 왜곡(so vs and)을 파악해야 하므로 정답과의 차이가 미묘함
전체 문장 구조(두 개의 독립절을 접속사로 연결하는 것이 적절함)를 이해해야 정답을 확정할 수 있음

distractors.matches: 'these obstacles'라는 표현이 앞 문장의 'restrictions'와 연결됨
distractors.plausibleBecause: 문법적으로 매끄러운 절이며 obstacles가 극복되었다는 의미가 논리적으로 그럴듯해 보임
distractors.whyWrong: 분사구 'Having spent years working...'는 문법적으로 주어인 'the obstacles'를 수식하게 되어 의미상 오류(dangling modifier)가 발생함 - 장애물이 무급으로 일한 것이 아니라 Noether가 그런 것임

distractors.matches: 'despite these obstacles'가 분사구와 의미상 연결되어 보임
distractors.plausibleBecause: despite these obstacles Noether persisted라는 구절 자체는 의미상 맞아 보이고 인과관계를 나타내는 'so'가 자연스러워 보일 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 문장 앞부분에 이미 'Having spent years... obstacles'라는 유사한 양보 표현이 있어 'despite these obstacles'가 중복되며, 'so'로 인과관계를 만드는 것은 그녀의 인정이 그녀의 인내 '때문에' 직접적으로 일어난 것처럼 과도하게 단순화하여 원래 관계를 왜곡함

distractors.matches: 분사구 뒤에 오는 주어가 Noether와 관련된 표현(Noether's persistence)이라는 점에서 매칭됨
distractors.plausibleBecause: 'Noether's persistence... meant that'는 분사구 뒤에 자연스러운 명사구 주어처럼 보이고 인과관계를 명확히 표현하는 듯함
distractors.whyWrong: 'meant that'을 쓰면 뒤따르는 절 'her insight was eventually recognized'가 종속절이 되어야 하는데 이미 완전한 독립절 구조로 되어 있어 문법적으로 어색하며, 전체 문장이 하나의 복잡한 종속구조가 되어 원래 의도된 두 개의 병렬적 사건(인내와 인정)의 관계가 인과적으로 왜곡됨

issues: C 선택지 분석에서 'despite these obstacles Noether persisted in her research, so'가 '종속절 구조'라고 표현했으나 실제로는 두 개의 독립절(Noether persisted..., so her insight was recognized)을 등위접속사 so로 연결한 구조이므로 '종속절'이라는 표현은 부정확함(다만 결론에는 영향 없음).

A와 C는 사실상 동일한 내용을 어순만 바꾼 것(despite 구를 문두에 두느냐 persisted 뒤에 두느냐)인데, 분사구 수식 대상 논리상 C도 'Noether'가 빈칸 바로 다음 위치에 오지 않고 'despite these obstacles'가 먼저 나오므로 현수 수식어 오류가 발생한다는 설명은 타당하나, 이 경우 A와 C의 유일한 실질적 차이가 'and' vs 'so'와 despite 구의 위치이므로 두 선택지 모두 전반부는 문법적으로 유사하게 작동할 수 있어 오답 근거가 다소 미묘함. 해설에서 이 미묘함을 좀 더 명확히 설명할 필요가 있음.

pub.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

pub.explanation: 비유 앞에서 신부는 일주일 뒤 오찬 초대에 아직 답하지 않았고, 매일 저녁 부두 끝으로 가 카드를 펼쳐 날짜를 읽고 다시 접는 행동을 되풀이한다. 이 두 단서는 '밀물'이 매번 돌아와 신부를 미결정의 선택 앞으로 데려가는 성질을 가리킨다. 비유 뒤에서 레몬을 치워 카드를 바람에 맡기는 장면도 선택이 여전히 열려 있음을 보여 주므로 B가 정답이다. A는 차오르는 압력, C는 빠져나가는 썰물이라는 다른 속성을 골랐고, D는 두 사람 사이를 오가는 전달물로 의미를 넓혔다.
pub.explanation_en: Before the metaphor, the bride has not yet answered the luncheon invitation for a week from now, and every evening she goes to the end of the pier, opens the card, reads the date, and folds it again. These two clues point to the quality of the 'tide' coming back each time and bringing the bride before a choice that is still undecided. After the metaphor, the scene in which she moves the lemons aside and leaves the card to the wind also shows that the choice is still open, so B is the answer. pub.passage: Folded twice and then once more, Salma's invitation lay on the planks of the dock, weighted with a lemon. Her son's bride had come to Marrakesh only that spring, in the year 1868, and the small lake below the rented villa was the one place in the household where no one followed anyone. The luncheon the card announced was a week off, and the bride had not answered. Each evening she walked to the end of the dock, lifted the lemon, unfolded the card, read the date, and refolded it along the same creases before setting the lemon back. Wolfram, watching from the terrace with his pipe, called the card his mother's little tide. Salma heard him and went on shelling beans. pub.passage: The Sydney Opera House, designed by Jørn Utzon and completed in 1973, is often celebrated purely for its sail-like shells, but the building's structural history complicates that image of effortless elegance. Utzon's original 1957 competition sketches depicted the shells as freeform curves, a shape that engineers at Ove Arup and Partners found impossible to construct with the technology available at the time. Only after years of experimentation did Utzon arrive at a solution: deriving every shell from sections of a single sphere, so that each curved surface could be built from identical precast, factory-made ribs rather than unique custom pieces. __This geometric breakthrough, more than the shells' visual profile, is what ultimately made the building constructible, since it converted an unrepeatable sculptural form into a system of standardized, mass-producible components.__ The shift from freeform sketch to spherical geometry cost years of delay and contributed to Utzon's eventual departure from the project before its completion, yet it is this very solution that engineers still cite as one of the most influential structural innovations in twentieth-century architecture.

pub.passage:
For much of the twentieth century, Antwerp dominated the world's diamond trade not because any single firm controlled the business but because thousands of small, specialized firms operated within a few city blocks. Cutters, polishers, brokers, and dealers worked within walking distance of one another, so a rough stone could pass through several independent hands in a single day, and reputations built through repeated face-to-face dealings allowed deals worth millions to be sealed with a handshake. Economists have often cited this arrangement as a textbook example of how geographic clustering can substitute for the coordination that a large, vertically integrated company would otherwise provide internally.

Since the 1990s, however, that model has come under strain. Major mining companies have increasingly sought to control their stones from mine to retail counter, sending rough diamonds directly to their own cutting facilities, many of them in India, where labor costs are lower. As a result, the advantages that Antwerp's dense network once offered have mattered less, and the city's role has shifted toward trading and certification rather than cutting itself.

pub.explanation: Text 2는 지하 해양과 대기 사이의 화학 반응을 재현한 실험실 시뮬레이션이 화산 활동 없이도 관측된 것과 유사한 기체 비율을 만들어냈다고 설명한다. 이는 화산 활동만이 이 조합의 기체를 만들 수 있는 유일한 과정이라는 Text 1의 주장에 대한 구체적인 반례를 제시하는 것이다. Text 2는 화산 활동의 가능성 자체를 부정하지는 않지만, 대안적 메커니즘도 배제해서는 안 된다고 주장한다. 따라서 정답은 A이다. B는 Text 1의 입장을 그대로 반복한 것으로 Text 2의 반박 취지와 반대된다. C는 지문에서 실제로는 황 화합물이 알려진 화학적 과정(해양 반응)과 일치한다고 설명한 것과 정반대다. D는 지문에 없는 내용으로, 두 팀이 다른 결론에 도달했다고 해서 데이터 자체에 결함이 있다고 주장하지 않는다.
pub.explanation_en: Text 2 describes laboratory simulations of chemical reactions between a subsurface ocean and the atmosphere that produced gas ratios similar to those observed, without any volcanic activity. This is a concrete counterexample to Text 1's claim that volcanic activity is the only process that could produce this combination of gases. Text 2 does not deny that volcanism is possible, but it argues that alternative mechanisms should not be ruled out. Therefore, the answer is A. B simply repeats Text 1's position, which is the opposite of Text 2's rebuttal. C is the reverse of what the passage actually says, which is that the sulfur compounds are consistent with known chemical processes (ocean reactions). D is not in the passage; the two teams reaching different conclusions does not mean either claims the data itself is flawed.
options: By presenting laboratory results showing that ocean-atmosphere chemical reactions can independently reproduce similar gas ratios without volcanism
By agreeing that volcanic outgassing is the only process capable of producing the observed sulfur compound ratios
By suggesting that the sulfur compound ratios could also be explained by atmospheric processes unrelated to either volcanism or subsurface ocean chemistry
By suggesting that both volcanic activity and ocean-atmosphere reactions might be occurring simultaneously, making it impossible to isolate a single cause
pub.passage:
Text 1
Astronomers analyzing data from a newly launched space telescope argue that the unusual chemical signatures detected in a distant exoplanet's atmosphere are best explained by volcanic activity on the planet's surface. The relative abundance of sulfur compounds, they note, closely matches patterns produced by volcanic outgassing observed on rocky planets within our own solar system. Because no other atmospheric process known to occur on such planets produces this particular combination of gases in these proportions, the researchers conclude that active volcanism offers the most plausible explanation currently available.

Text 2
A separate team analyzing the same telescope data proposes that the sulfur compounds could instead result from chemical reactions between the atmosphere and a subsurface ocean rich in dissolved minerals. Laboratory simulations replicating the exoplanet's estimated temperature and pressure conditions produced similar gas ratios without requiring any volcanic activity at all. This team acknowledges that volcanism remains possible but argues that the ocean-based mechanism should not be dismissed, since it independently reproduces the same chemical signatures observed by the telescope.

pub.explanation_en: The author of Text 2 argues that the calf doesn't create Rosario's urge to teach from her surroundings. Instead, it just gives her the excuse she has been waiting for to act on doubts she already had about lessons written far from the island. In Text 1, she looks at the Manila workbook with its snowfall lesson right before she sits down, which supports this reading, so C is correct. B states the popular view that Text 2 explicitly rejects, the idea that the calf alone sparks her approach. D fits the detail that Rosario couldn't move the calf, but calling her choice "reluctant" contradicts Text 2's view that she welcomes the chance. A doesn't work because Text 2 never suggests that Rosario has lost control of her class.
options: As a sign that she has lost control of the classroom and is giving in to the children's excitement
As an example of spontaneous creativity that comes about only because of the calf's unexpected arrival
As a moment when she takes up a welcome opportunity to drop lessons she had already found poorly suited to the island
As a reluctant compromise she makes only after her efforts to move the calf have failed
pub.passage:
Text 1
The school boat bumped against the bamboo pier, and Teacher Rosario climbed out with her satchel held above the spray. On the schoolhouse steps lay a carabao calf, legs folded, chewing as if it had been hired to guard the door. She clapped; it blinked. She pushed; it sighed. By then the children had arrived and were watching her closely. Rosario looked at the workbook in her satchel, printed in Manila, its first lesson about measuring snowfall. Then she sat down beside the calf. "Who can tell me," she asked, "how many steps this animal is blocking, and how much it weighs compared to all of you?"

Text 2
Readers often celebrate the carabao scene as proof of Rosario's sudden, playful inventiveness, as though the calf alone sparks her new approach. But the story has already shown us her doubts about lessons written far from the island. The calf does not create her impulse to teach from the world around her; it simply gives her an excuse she has been waiting for to act on it.

advisory.note: C는 Text 2의 'excuse she has been waiting for'와 'doubts about lessons written far from the island'를 바꿔 말한 것이다. B(통념)와 D(송아지를 밀어내지 못한 장면)는 부분적으로 근거가 있어 그럴듯하게 비교된다. A는 다소 약하지만 말이 되는 오답이다. 중간 난이도에 맞다.

hardJudge.note: Text 2의 핵심 주장("송아지는 충동을 만들지 않고, 기다려 온 핑계를 줄 뿐")과 Text 1의 마닐라 교재(눈 측정 단원) 응시 장면을 연결하면 C가 명확히 도출됨. B는 Text 2가 명시적으로 반박하는 통념, D는 Text 1의 '밀어도 안 움직임' 세부와 부분 일치하나 '마지못한'이 "waiting for"와 충돌, A는 근거 없음 — 오답 구성이 medium 기준에 부합. 한국어·영어 해설 모두 정답 및 선택지 글자 참조가 일치하고 모순 없음. 영어 해설은 자연스럽고 한글 미포함. 지문은 창작물로 저작권 우려 없음.

pub.explanation: 학생의 주장은 두 요소, 즉 (1) 돈벌이라는 동기에서 벗어나고 (2) 잃어버린 유산과 연결되는 변화를 담고 있다. D는 높은 값을 거절하는 장면(금전 동기 이탈)과 할머니의 색이라는 이유(유산과의 연결)를 함께 보여 주므로 두 요소를 모두 뒷받침한다. A는 Benson이 여전히 수익에 주목한다는 내용이라 변화가 아니라 원래 동기를 보여 준다. B는 열심히 연습한다는 내용일 뿐 동기가 바뀌었는지는 알려 주지 않는다. C는 유산과 관련되지만 Benson이 아니라 Kariuki의 연결을 보여 준다.
pub.explanation_en: The student's argument has two parts: Benson moves away from earning money, and he moves toward a heritage he had lost touch with. D shows both, since Benson turns down a high price (he's leaving the money motive behind) because the bracelet uses his grandmother's colors (a connection to heritage). A shows Benson still focused on profit, so it reflects his original motive, not a change. B shows that he's dedicated, but it doesn't say whether his reason for doing beadwork has changed. C is about heritage, but it describes Kariuki's connection to it, not Benson's.
options: Later in the story, Benson sells a dozen bracelets at the Kenyatta Avenue lights in a single afternoon and proudly tells Kariuki how much he earned.
Later in the story, Benson practices beadwork every evening at home so that he can keep up with Kariuki during their next matatu ride.
Later in the story, Kariuki tells Benson that his own grandmother taught him the meaning of each bead color when he was a boy in Nyeri.
Later in the story, a tourist offers Benson a high price for a bracelet, but Benson declines, saying it uses the colors his grandmother once wore and is not for sale.
pub.passage:
The following text is adapted from a short story. Kariuki, a street vendor, rides the same matatu (minibus) each morning as Benson, a motorcycle taxi driver whose bike is being repaired.

At every stop, while the conductor shouted for passengers, Kariuki opened his tin of glass beads on his knee. "Red for the blood of the people," he murmured, threading. "White for peace." Benson watched, then held out his hand. On the first day he had said he only wanted to make bracelets to sell to tourists at the Kenyatta Avenue lights, where riders waited with nothing to do. Kariuki had shrugged and given him a needle anyway. Now, by the third week, Benson's fingers moved more slowly than before, and he no longer counted aloud how many shillings each strand might bring.

A student argues that the story presents Benson's interest in beadwork as gradually changing from a way to earn money into a way of connecting with a heritage he had lost touch with.

advisory.note: D만 금전 동기 이탈과 Benson 본인의 유산 연결을 함께 보여 준다. A는 원래 동기 그대로이고, B는 열의만 보여 주며, C는 Kariuki의 유산이라 주체가 다르다. B와 C가 각각 부분적으로 맞는 근거를 가져 medium에 적합하다. 다만 '잃어버렸던(lost touch)' 요소는 D에서 암시 수준에 그친다.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 주장의 두 요소(금전 동기 이탈 + 유산 연결)를 모두 직접 뒷받침하며, 지문의 "no longer counted aloud how many shillings"와도 자연스럽게 이어진다. B(헌신이지만 동기 불명)와 C(유산이지만 Kariuki의 것)는 부분적 근거가 있어 비교가 필요하고, A는 원래 동기를 보여 주는 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능한다. 한·영 해설 모두 선택지 참조와 결론이 일치하고 영어 해설에 한글 없음. 지문은 창작물로 저작권 문제 없음. 난이도 medium 적합.

A는 note 6의 일부만 사용해 개기일식을 볼 수 있는 지역적 조건만 설명할 뿐 왜 가능한지는 설명하지 못한다. B는 note 4와 5를 결합해 미래에 개기일식이 사라질 것이라는 내용으로, 현재 가능한 이유가 아니라 미래의 변화를 설명하여 시간 관계를 혼동한다. C는 note 1의 일부만 사용해 개기일식의 정의(달이 태양을 가림)만 설명할 뿐 왜 완전히 가릴 수 있는지의 근본 원인은 다루지 않는다.
pub.explanation_en: The student's goal is to explain why total solar eclipses are currently possible on Earth. D is correct because it combines note 2 (the Moon is about 400 times smaller than the Sun but about 400 times closer) and note 3 (as a result, they appear nearly the same size in the sky) to explain the fundamental reason a total solar eclipse is possible. A uses only part of note 6 and explains only the regional condition for seeing a total eclipse, not why one is possible. B combines notes 4 and 5 to say that total solar eclipses will disappear in the future, which explains a future change rather than why they are possible now, confusing the timeframe. C uses only part of note 1 and explains only the definition of a total solar eclipse (the Moon covers the Sun), not the underlying reason the Moon can cover it completely.
options: Total solar eclipses can only be observed from a narrow region on Earth known as the path of totality.
The Moon is moving away from Earth at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year, which will eventually end total solar eclipses.
A total solar eclipse happens when the Moon moves directly between the Earth and the Sun, blocking the Sun's light.
Because the Moon is about 400 times smaller than the Sun but also 400 times closer, the two bodies appear nearly the same size in Earth's sky.
pub.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- Total solar eclipses occur when the Moon passes directly between the Earth and the Sun, completely blocking the Sun's disk as seen from a narrow path on Earth.
- The Moon is about 400 times smaller in diameter than the Sun, but it is also about 400 times closer to Earth than the Sun is.
- This coincidental ratio means the Moon and Sun appear almost exactly the same size in Earth's sky, allowing the Moon to fully cover the Sun during a total eclipse.
- The Moon's orbit is slowly moving it farther from Earth, at a rate of about 3.8 centimeters per year.
- In several hundred million years, the Moon will be far enough away that it will appear too small to fully cover the Sun, ending total solar eclipses.

difficultyReasons: 질문이 '가능한 이유(원인)'를 묻는데, 선택지들이 정의·범위·미래변화 등 표면적으로 관련된 다른 정보를 제공해 구분에 2단계 추론이 필요함

오답들이 모두 노트의 실제 문장에서 나온 것이라 핵심 정보 공유도가 높아 단순 소거로 풀기 어려움

distractors.whyWrong: 이 문장은 일식이 왜 '가능한지'를 설명하지 않고, 일식을 관찰할 수 있는 지리적 범위만 설명한다. 질문의 초점(원인)과 다르다.

pub.question: The student wants to explain why total solar eclipses are currently possible on Earth. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

pub.answer_rationale: 연구자들이 밀집이 단순히 굴 부족 때문일 수 있다는 반박 가능성을 먼저 인정(양보)한 뒤, 그럼에도 불구하고 신호 행동이 사회적 존재에 대한 실제 반응이라는 자신들의 주장을 유지하므로 양보(concession) 관계를 나타내는 전환어가 필요하다.
pub.evidence_span: Researchers acknowledge that the density of octopuses at Octlantis may simply reflect a shortage of suitable denning sites nearby... ______, they maintain that many of the observed interactions... appear only when other octopuses are within sight
pub.explanation: 빈칸 앞 문장은 밀집 현상이 단지 적합한 은신처(굴)가 부족하기 때문일 수 있다는 대안적 설명(반박 가능성)을 연구자들이 인정하는 내용이고, 빈칸 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 불구하고 신호 행동이 사회적 반응이라는 자신들의 원래 주장을 유지하는 내용이다. 이는 앞선 인정에도 불구하고 주장을 이어가는 양보(concession) 관계이므로 'Even so,'가 가장 논리적이다. 'For example,'은 예시 관계, 'Similarly,'는 유사성을 통한 추가 관계, 'Consequently,'는 인과 관계를 신호하므로 모두 부적절하다.
pub.explanation_en: The sentence before the blank acknowledges the researchers' alternative explanation (a possible rebuttal) that the crowding may simply be due to a shortage of suitable denning sites, and the sentence after the blank maintains their original claim that the signaling behavior is a social response despite this. This is a concession relationship, in which a claim continues despite the earlier acknowledgment, so 'Even so,' is the most logical. 'For example,' signals an example relationship, 'Similarly,' signals an additional relationship through similarity, and 'Consequently,' signals a cause-and-effect relationship, so all are inappropriate.
options: Even so,
For example,
Similarly,
Consequently,
pub.passage: For decades, marine biologists assumed that octopuses were solitary creatures with little tolerance for one another outside of mating. This view was based largely on observations of species in captivity, where octopuses placed together often fought or cannibalized one another. Recent fieldwork at a site off the coast of Australia nicknamed "Octlantis," however, has complicated this picture. There, researchers documented dozens of octopuses living in close proximity, denning within a few body lengths of each other for extended periods, and engaging in repeated visual displays and physical contact that did not end in violence. Some of these interactions even resembled the kind of signaling seen in more overtly social species, such as changes in skin color and posture directed at approaching neighbors. Researchers acknowledge that the density of octopuses at Octlantis may simply reflect a shortage of suitable denning sites nearby, forcing individuals into proximity regardless of their social preferences. ______ they maintain that many of the observed interactions, including the signaling displays, appear only when other octopuses are within sight, suggesting the behavior is a genuine response to social presence rather than a mere byproduct of crowding.

difficultyReasons: 양보(concession)와 결과/예시/유사 관계를 구분해야 함 - 1~2단계 추론
앞 문장(서식지 부족 가설 인정)과 뒤 문장(그래도 사회적 행동이라는 주장 유지) 사이의 논리적 대조를 파악해야 함
오답들이 표면적으로 뒤 문장의 내용과 일부 연결되어 그럴듯해 보임

distractors.plausibleBecause: 뒤에 예시처럼 보이는 구체적 설명(신호 행동이 관찰될 때)이 이어져서 예시 제시로 오인할 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 앞 문장은 밀집이 서식지 부족 때문일 수 있다는 반대 가능성을 인정하는 내용이고, 뒤 문장은 그럼에도 연구자들이 사회적 행동이라는 주장을 유지한다는 대조/양보 관계이므로 예시가 아니라 양보의 접속사가 필요함

distractors.matches: 앞뒤 모두 Octlantis의 문어 행동에 대한 설명이라는 점에서 표면적 유사성
distractors.plausibleBecause: 두 문장 모두 문어의 행동에 관한 진술이라 비슷한 내용처럼 보일 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 앞 문장(서식지 부족 가능성)과 뒤 문장(사회적 신호라는 반박)은 서로 대립되는 주장이지 유사한 내용의 나열이 아니므로 유사 관계 접속사는 부적절함

distractors.plausibleBecause: 뒤 문장이 앞 문장에서 언급된 상황에 따른 결과처럼 읽힐 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 뒤 문장은 앞 문장에서 제기된 대안적 설명(서식지 부족)에 대해 그럼에도 불구하고 연구자들이 사회적 해석을 유지한다는 반박이므로 결과가 아니라 양보/대조 관계가 필요함

pub.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

pub.answer_rationale: 'Eventually'는 앞 문장(오랜 번영)과 뒤 문장(쇠퇴와 해체) 사이의 시간적 전개 관계를 정확히 연결하며, 다른 연결어처럼 절 간 논리 관계를 잘못된 접속 유형(유사·예시)으로 왜곡하지 않는다.
pub.evidence_span: ______ , when nation-states began enforcing their own tariffs and navies in the sixteenth century, the loosely organized League could not compete and gradually dissolved.
pub.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에는 ", when nation-states began ..."라는 부사절과 완전한 주절이 이어지므로 빈칸에는 문장 앞에 놓이는 부사 하나만 들어가야 한다. "Eventually"가 이 조건을 만족한다. "Eventually;"와 "Eventually:"는 이어지는 쉼표와 겹쳐 문장부호가 이중이 되고 문장 경계도 잘못 만들며, "Eventually and"는 연결할 대상이 없는 접속사가 남는다. 따라서 정답은 C이다.
pub.explanation_en: After the blank come ", when nation-states began ..." and a complete main clause, so the blank must hold a single adverb that opens the sentence. "Eventually" meets that condition. "Eventually;" and "Eventually:" collide with the comma that follows, creating double punctuation and a faulty sentence boundary, and "Eventually and" leaves a conjunction with nothing to join. So the answer is C.
options: Eventually;
Eventually:
Eventually
Eventually and
pub.passage: Economic historians studying the Hanseatic League note that the alliance of merchant towns thrived for centuries without a central government, relying instead on shared trading privileges and mutual defense agreements. ______ , when nation-states began enforcing their own tariffs and navies in the sixteenth century, the loosely organized League could not compete and gradually dissolved.

difficultyReasons: 추론 단계: 시간적 전환(centuries 동안 유지되다가 16세기에 변화)이라는 단일 단계만 파악하면 됨

오답 공유 정보: 오답들이 모두 '연결어'라는 형식적 공통점만 가지고 있어 의미상 구분이 쉬움
자료 해석: 별도의 표나 수식 없이 문장 논리 관계만 파악하면 되어 해석 부담이 적음

distractors.plausibleBecause: 두 문장이 비슷한 주제(League의 상황)를 다루는 것처럼 보여 유사성을 나타내는 접속어가 적절해 보일 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 두 번째 절은 첫 번째 절과 유사한 내용이 아니라 시간이 지나 상황이 변화(쇠퇴)했음을 나타내므로 유사 관계가 아니라 시간적 전환 관계임

distractors.matches: League가 쇠퇴한 사건이 앞선 설명의 예시처럼 읽힐 수 있음
distractors.plausibleBecause: 두 번째 절이 첫 번째 절에 대한 구체적 사례처럼 보일 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: 두 번째 절은 첫 번째 절의 예시가 아니라 시간에 따른 후속 사건이며, 인과·시간적 전환을 나타내므로 예시 관계가 아님

distractors.plausibleBecause: Similarly와 마찬가지로 두 문장이 비슷한 주장을 반복하는 것처럼 보일 수 있음

pub.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

pub.answer_rationale: Text 2는 자화상 제작이라는 사실 자체는 인정하되, 그 동기를 개인주의적 자기표현이 아닌 시장 경쟁 속 기술 홍보로 재해석함으로써 Text 1의 해석에 이의를 제기한다.
pub.evidence_span: Surviving guild records indicate that self-portraits were frequently produced as demonstrations of technical skill, intended to attract future patrons by showcasing an artist's mastery of likeness and detail.
pub.evidence_target: Text 2는 Text 1이 자화상 증가를 '철학적 개인주의'의 증거로 해석하는 것에 대해, 길드 기록을 근거로 삼아 기술 홍보라는 실용적 동기를 대안으로 제시하며 반박한다.
pub.explanation: Text 1은 16세기 자화상 증가를 화가들이 자신을 독립적 주체로 인식하게 된 새로운 개인주의의 증거로 해석한다. Text 2는 길드 기록을 근거로 들어, 자화상이 실제로는 미래 후원자를 유치하기 위한 기술 시연이자 상업적 광고의 성격이 강했다고 반박하며, 이는 이전 역사가들이 강조한 철학적 개인주의와는 다른 실용적 동기라고 주장한다. 따라서 정답은 B이다. A는 개인주의라는 해석 자체는 받아들이면서 시기만 다르다고 주장하는 것으로, Text 2가 실제로는 개인주의 해석 자체를 문제 삼는다는 점에서 MISATTRIBUTED_STANCE에 해당한다. C는 자화상 제작 빈도라는 사실 관계를 뒤집어 말하는 REVERSED_RELATIONSHIP이다. D는 지문에 없는 내용(후원자가 주문을 주도했다는 주장)을 끌어들인 무관한 결합이다.
pub.explanation_en: Text 1 interprets the increase in self-portraits in the sixteenth century as evidence of a new individualism, in which painters came to see themselves as independent subjects. Text 2 cites guild records to argue back that self-portraits were actually more often a demonstration of technical skill meant to attract future patrons, a form of commercial advertising, and that this is a practical motive distinct from the philosophical individualism earlier historians emphasized. So the answer is B. A accepts the individualism interpretation itself and disputes only the timing, but Text 2 actually challenges the individualism interpretation itself, so this is a MISATTRIBUTED_STANCE. C is a REVERSED_RELATIONSHIP that flips the factual matter of how often self-portraits were produced. D brings in content that is not in the passages (the claim that patrons drove the commissions), an irrelevant combination.
options: By agreeing that self-portraits reflect individualism but arguing this individualism appeared earlier than Text 1 suggests
By arguing that guild records show self-portraits were often produced to advertise technical skill to prospective patrons rather than to express individual identity
By claiming that Northern European painters rarely produced self-portraits during the period Text 1 describes
By suggesting that patrons, rather than artists, were primarily responsible for commissioning the self-portraits under discussion
pub.passage:
Text 1
Art historians have long treated the sudden proliferation of self-portraits among Northern European painters in the sixteenth century as evidence of a new individualism, arguing that artists began to see themselves as worthy subjects independent of religious or aristocratic patronage. This shift, they contend, mirrors broader intellectual currents of the period that elevated the individual thinker and observer, and the self-portrait becomes a visual manifestation of the artist's newfound social and philosophical standing, no longer merely a craftsman serving a patron's commission.

Text 2
A more recent generation of scholars has questioned whether self-portraiture in this period should be read primarily as a statement of individual identity. Surviving guild records indicate that self-portraits were frequently produced as demonstrations of technical skill, intended to attract future patrons by showcasing an artist's mastery of likeness and detail. Rather than expressions of a painter's inner selfhood, these images may have functioned largely as advertisements circulated within a competitive commercial market for commissioned portraiture, a practical motive quite distinct from the philosophical individualism earlier historians emphasized.

difficultyReasons: 필요한 추론 단계는 1~2단계로, Text 2의 핵심 주장(길드 기록/광고 목적)을 파악하고 Text 1의 개인주의 주장과 대조하면 됨
오답 B와 C는 지문 내용과 명백히 모순되어 쉽게 제거 가능
오답 D는 부분적 어휘 일치(patron)로 약간의 함정이 있으나 핵심 주장과 무관해 큰 어려움은 아님
정답 A는 지문의 핵심 문장(길드 기록, 기술 시연, 광고)을 거의 그대로 반영해 식별이 비교적 쉬움
