pub.answer_rationale: Because the sentence already uses the coordinating conjunction "and" to join two clauses, the blank needs an adverb like "consequently" that shows the causal relationship without introducing a redundant subject or a second conjunction.
pub.evidence_span: learned to render each petal and leaf with scientific precision, and ______ she became one of the most commercially successful painters
pub.explanation: 이 문장은 "and"로 두 절을 이으므로 빈칸에는 뒤의 "she became ..." 절을 수식하는 부사가 와야 한다. "consequently"는 부사로서 "and consequently she became ..."처럼 자연스럽게 이어진다. "consequently;"와 "consequently:"는 등위접속사 "and" 바로 뒤에 세미콜론이나 콜론을 두어 절 경계를 부당하게 만들고, "consequent"는 형용사라 절을 수식하는 부사 자리에 올 수 없다. 따라서 정답은 B이다.
pub.explanation_en: This sentence joins two clauses with "and," so the blank must hold an adverb that modifies the clause "she became ..." that follows. "Consequently" is an adverb and fits as "and consequently she became ...." "Consequently;" and "consequently:" put a semicolon or colon directly after the coordinating conjunction "and," which creates an illegitimate clause boundary, and "consequent" is an adjective, so it cannot sit in a position that modifies the clause. So the answer is B.
options: consequently;
consequently
consequently:
consequent

'used'는 과거분사로 쓰일 경우 '팀이 사용되었다'는 수동의 의미가 되어 팀이 위성 추적기를 능동적으로 활용했다는 원래 의미와 어긋나는 수식 관계 오류를 만든다. 'which used'와 'they used'는 별도의 정동사를 포함한 절을 삽입해 콤마 스플라이스나 어색한 종속 구조를 만든다.
pub.explanation_en: The phrase inserted with commas should be a participial phrase modifying "Her team." The present participle "using satellite transmitters" adds the meaning that the team actively used satellite trackers, and it fits smoothly into the sentence without clashing with the main clause's verb "discovered." "Used," if taken as a past participle, would mean "the team was used," a passive meaning that creates a modification error inconsistent with the original meaning that the team actively employed satellite trackers. "Which used" and "they used" insert a clause containing a separate finite verb, creating a comma splice or an awkward subordinate structure.
options: using
which using
used
they used

pub.explanation_en: The key is to connect two ideas: Wren designed each church separately because the sites were irregular (what changed), but he always made sure the congregation could see and hear the preacher (what stayed the same). That's why B is correct. A is right that the towers were distinctive, but the towers were often designed later, and the text says the interior logic started from the spoken word, so towers weren't the main reason he adapted to the sites. C is right that Wren gave up on a standard plan, but the reason was cramped, irregular plots, not a shortage of surviving streets. D gets the column-free interiors right, but the text explains them by the need to see and hear, not by a lack of room for structural supports.
options: Wren adapted his church plans to irregular sites mainly so that each building could display a tower more distinctive than those of its neighbors.
Wren varied the layouts of his churches to suit difficult sites while consistently designing interiors so that worshippers could see and hear the sermon.
Wren abandoned the idea of a standard plan because the fire had left too few intact streets to guide the placement of entrances.
Wren designed compact interiors without columns primarily because the narrow plots left too little room for heavy structural supports.
pub.passage: After the Great Fire of 1666 destroyed most of the City of London, Christopher Wren was commissioned to rebuild more than fifty parish churches. Many of the sites he inherited were cramped, irregular plots hemmed in by surviving houses and lanes, so a single standard plan was impossible. Rather than forcing a uniform design onto each lot, Wren treated every church as a separate problem, fitting naves into odd angles and placing entrances wherever the street allowed. Yet he held firmly to one priority across these varied buildings: that the congregation should be able to see the pulpit and hear the preacher clearly. Wren argued that a Protestant church was essentially an "auditory," a room for listening, and he kept interiors compact and largely free of obstructing columns. The striking towers and steeples that rose above the rooftops, often designed years after the main structures were finished, gave each church a distinctive public face, but the logic of the interior began with the spoken word.

advisory.note: B가 지문의 두 요소, 즉 부지에 따른 설계 변화와 설교를 보고 듣게 한다는 일관된 원칙을 함께 담고 있다. A, C, D는 각각 지문의 실제 세부(독특한 탑, 표준 설계 포기, 기둥 없는 실내)를 쓰면서 이유를 잘못 연결한 오답이라 서로 비교해야 배제된다. medium 수준에 맞다. 'largely free'를 'without columns'로 바꾼 것은 오답 선택지 안의 표현이므로 문제없다.

pub.passage: Bergen had given Jens a new job and a damp apartment, and when I visited, he brought me straight to the bookbinder's workshop where he now spent his days. We argued within the hour about glue. He said the animal glue was better; I said he only liked it because the old man who owned the shop liked it. Neither of us raised the week's notice he had given me before he left, or the letters I had not answered since. He pressed a spine between two boards and turned the screw, and I watched him check the binding by letting the book fall open on the bench, gently, the way a doctor lifts a wrist. Our friendship, I thought, had become a book sewn with too few stitches. Later he showed me a ledger he had rebound for a shipping firm, its pages lying flat under the lamp, and told me the old one had looked fine on the shelf for decades and split the first time anyone needed to read it straight through. I said nothing about glue after that.

Text 2 presents the points that bold individuals linger just as long in front of any new object, not only a mirror, and that those individuals bite less because they are more experienced, showing that time in front of a mirror may reflect general boldness (and experience) rather than self-recognition. pub.passage:
Text 1
Researchers studying a population of cleaner wrasse, small reef fish that remove parasites from larger "client" fish, found that wrasse which spent more time inspecting a mirror placed in their tank later bit fewer clients during cleaning sessions. Because mirror inspection is a standard sign of self-awareness, and because biting clients is a form of cheating that damages a cleaner's reputation, the researchers concluded that self-aware wrasse are better able to manage their reputations. The effect was strongest in wrasse collected from crowded reef sections, where clients are numerous.

Text 2
A separate team observed that cleaner wrasse vary widely in general boldness, a trait measurable by how quickly an individual approaches any novel object, whether a mirror, a plastic cube, or a colored disk. Bold wrasse lingered near all such objects equally long. The same bold individuals also tended to be the most experienced cleaners, having served more clients, and experienced cleaners are known to bite less because clients that are bitten stop returning.

pub.explanation_en: Text 1 claims that congestion pricing is a powerful and fast way to change commuter behavior. Text 2 points out that in cities where public transit is already saturated during rush hour, drivers have nowhere to go, so they simply pay the fee or shift their travel patterns only slightly, dulling the policy's effect, and it holds that the policy's effectiveness depends on the condition of transit capacity. So the answer is D.
options: The author would agree without qualification, since both texts describe measurable declines in traffic volume following the introduction of congestion pricing.
The author would contend that congestion pricing never affects commuter behavior and that traffic volumes remain unchanged regardless of fees.
The author would claim that public transit investment alone, without any pricing mechanism, is sufficient to reduce downtown traffic congestion.
The author would note that the policy's effectiveness depends on whether transit systems have enough spare capacity to absorb displaced drivers.
pub.passage:
Text 1

Urban planners advocating for congestion pricing argue that charging drivers a fee to enter crowded downtown areas during peak hours is the most direct way to reduce gridlock. By attaching a real monetary cost to driving at the busiest times, cities can shift a meaningful share of commuters toward public transit, carpooling, or off-peak travel. Studies of cities that have implemented such fees show measurable declines in traffic volume and average commute times within the first year, suggesting that price signals are a powerful and relatively fast lever for changing commuter behavior.

Text 2

Congestion pricing schemes often produce impressive short-term reductions in traffic, but critics note that these gains can erode over time if the underlying public transit system cannot absorb the displaced demand. In cities where buses and trains already run at capacity during rush hour, commuters priced out of driving frequently have no viable alternative and either pay the fee anyway or shift their trips only slightly, blunting the policy's effect. Without simultaneous investment in transit capacity, congestion pricing risks becoming a revenue tool that burdens lower-income drivers more than it meaningfully reduces congestion.

pub.explanation: 빈칸 앞의 "a group"은 명사구이며, 이를 수식하며 뒤에 나열되는 목록(transportation officials, sanitation departments, property owners)을 목적어로 받으려면 능동의 현재분사 'comprising'이 필요하다. 'comprised of'는 표준 영어에서 어법상 비문으로 간주되며(수동태 오용), 'that comprised'와 'which was comprised of'는 각각 불필요하게 별도의 정동사절을 만들어 앞 문장과의 연결이 어색하거나 comprised의 태를 잘못 사용해 비문이 된다. 정답은 D.
pub.explanation_en: "A group" before the blank is a noun phrase, and to modify it and take the list that follows (transportation officials, sanitation departments, property owners) as its object, the active present participle 'comprising' is needed. 'Comprised of' is considered ungrammatical in Standard English (a misuse of the passive), while 'that comprised' and 'which was comprised of' each create an unnecessary separate finite clause, making the connection to the previous sentence awkward, or misuse the voice of comprise and produce an ungrammatical sentence. The answer is D.
options: comprised of
that comprising
which was comprised of
comprising

The resulting negotiations often delayed construction by years, even when the engineering itself posed no serious obstacles.

pub.explanation_en: The text first reports that Russian speakers distinguish blues across their two-term boundary faster, then shows that this advantage vanishes when verbal memory is occupied, concluding that language's effect depends on in-the-moment word use rather than permanent changes in vision. D connects both pieces, so it is correct. A reflects only the first paragraph and claims a lasting perceptual difference, which the second paragraph undercuts. B goes too far, since a language effect was in fact observed. C overgeneralizes: the text says only that the Russian speakers' advantage disappeared, not that everyone's color discrimination was impaired.
options: Russian speakers perceive the color blue differently from English speakers because their language divides blue into two separate basic categories.
Experiments on color discrimination have shown that the words a language provides have no measurable effect on how its speakers perceive color.
Tasks that occupy verbal memory interfere with people's ability to distinguish colors, regardless of the language they speak.
Research on color discrimination indicates that language can influence perception, but mainly through speakers' real-time use of words rather than by permanently altering vision.
pub.passage:
The idea that the words a language provides can shape how its speakers perceive the world, often associated with linguists Edward Sapir and Benjamin Lee Whorf, has been tested most rigorously in the domain of color. Russian, for example, uses two basic terms, "siniy" and "goluboy," for darker and lighter blues, whereas English uses only "blue." In a 2007 study, Jonathan Winawer and colleagues found that Russian speakers were faster than English speakers at telling apart two blues that fell on opposite sides of the siniy-goluboy boundary.

Yet the researchers also observed that this advantage disappeared when participants were asked to silently repeat a string of digits while performing the task, an activity that occupies verbal memory. Because Russian speakers' eyes did not change during the digit task, the result suggests that the language advantage depends on speakers actively drawing on their color words in the moment rather than on any permanent difference in how they see. Findings like these have led many researchers to favor a modest version of the hypothesis over the claim that language fixes the limits of perception.

advisory.note: Winawer et al. (2007, PNAS)의 결과는 정확하게 요약되어 있다. 정답 D는 두 단락의 내용을 함께 연결해야 하고, A는 첫 단락만 훑어 읽은 경우를 노린 그럴듯한 함정이다. B와 C는 각각 지나친 단정·과도한 일반화로 배제된다. 지문의 'eyes did not change'라는 표현이 다소 어색하지만 정답 판정에는 영향이 없다.

hardJudge.note: 정답 D는 두 단락(언어 이점 존재 + 언어 간섭 시 소멸)을 연결해야 도출되며, A(첫 단락만 반영·영구적 차이 암시)와 C(과잉 일반화)는 부분 근거가 있어 비교가 필요하고 B도 그럴듯한 오답으로 기능한다. Winawer et al. 2007 연구 내용(러시아어 siniy/goluboy, 언어 간섭 시 이점 소멸)은 실제와 부합한다. 다만 "Because Russian speakers' eyes did not change during the digit task"라는 문장은 논리적 연결이 어색하고 표현이 부자연스러워(눈 자체가 변하지 않는다는 진술은 자명함) 문체상 다듬을 여지가 있으나 정답 판정에는 영향이 없다.

D captures both of these points. A uses a real detail about particle chains, but the text's focus is adjustability, not greater strength, and it says the fluid becomes only close to a soft solid. options: MR dampers resist ground motion more strongly than passive dampers because their iron particles form chains that turn the fluid into a solid.

pub.passage: Engineers protecting buildings from earthquakes have long relied on passive dampers, devices filled with oil that resist motion by a fixed amount. Such dampers work well for the shaking they were designed for but cannot adjust when an earthquake proves stronger or weaker than expected. Magnetorheological (MR) dampers offer an alternative. They contain a fluid with suspended iron particles; when an electromagnetic coil inside the damper is switched on, the particles line up into chains, and the fluid thickens from a liquid with the consistency of motor oil to something close to a soft solid within milliseconds. By varying the current, sensors and a controller can tune the damper's resistance as ground motion changes. Because the coil needs only about as much power as a household light bulb, MR dampers can keep running on backup batteries even when an earthquake knocks out the electrical grid. This is an important advantage, since the stronger kinds of adjustable systems need large power supplies that may fail at exactly the moment they are needed.

B는 극성과 나이를 연결한다는 점에서 그럴듯하지만, 지문은 정상·역전 구간이 번갈아 나타난다고 할 뿐 역전 층이 더 오래되었다고 하지 않는다. D는 칼륨-아르곤 연대 측정을 언급하지만, 자철석이 기록된 방향을 잃는다는 내용은 지문에 없고 오히려 방향을 고정한다고 설명한다.
pub.explanation_en: The correct answer is C. The text says that once the flows were dated, rocks of the same age from distant continents had the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals than normal ones. A names real sampling sites from the text, but the text never mentions how fast the lava cooled. B sounds reasonable because it links polarity to age, but the text describes normal and reversed intervals alternating over time, not reversed layers being older. D mentions potassium-argon dating, but the text says magnetite locks in the field direction, not that the grains lose it over time.
options: Basalt layers from Iceland and Hawaii showed that reversed layers formed only in lava that cooled especially slowly.
Basalt layers that recorded a southward field turned out to be much older than layers that recorded a northward field.
Basalt layers of matching age from widely separated locations shared a polarity, and reversed layers were not mineralogically distinct.
Basalt layers dated by potassium-argon decay showed that magnetite grains lose their recorded direction over time.
pub.passage: When lava cools into basalt, tiny grains of magnetite inside the rock lock in the direction of Earth's magnetic field at that moment. In the mid-twentieth century, geologists sampling stacked lava flows in places such as Iceland and Hawaii noticed that some layers recorded a field pointing roughly north, as it does today, while others recorded one pointing south. At first, some researchers suspected that certain minerals simply magnetized themselves backward as they cooled, a chemical quirk unrelated to the planet's field. That explanation weakened when scientists dated the flows using the slow decay of radioactive potassium into argon. Rocks of the same age from distant continents turned out to share the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals than normal ones. By matching polarity to age across many sites, researchers assembled a timeline of alternating normal and reversed intervals—the geomagnetic polarity timescale—which later helped confirm that the seafloor spreads outward from mid-ocean ridges.

advisory.note: 정답 C는 지문의 두 근거(동일 연대·동일 극성, 광물 구성 차이 없음)를 결합해야 하는 바꿔 말하기 문항이다. 오답들은 지문 요소(지명, 연대 측정, 극성-나이 연결)를 차용해 그럴듯하다. 다만 C만 두 근거를 모두 담고 있어 비교적 쉽게 고를 수 있으나 medium 범위 안에 있다.

hardJudge.note: 정답 C는 지문의 "Rocks of the same age from distant continents turned out to share the same polarity, and reversed layers did not consistently contain a different mix of minerals"를 정확히 재진술. pub.explanation_en: The text describes a rotation task in which the two language groups used different strategies, presents the objection that their environments also differed, and then reports that studies comparing speakers in the same environment still found that language predicts strategy. That makes A the main idea. B repeats only the critics' point and conflicts with the later findings. C talks about accuracy, but the text describes different strategies, not one group doing better than the other. D goes too far: the critics question how to interpret the results, but the text never says the task can't reveal anything about mental representation.
options: Research suggests that the directional system of a language affects how its speakers solve spatial tasks, even after the influence of surroundings is taken into account.
Research suggests that differences in spatial reasoning between Guugu Yimithirr and Dutch speakers result mainly from differences in their surroundings rather than their languages.
Research suggests that speakers of languages using cardinal directions perform spatial tasks more accurately than speakers of languages using left and right.
Research suggests that the rotation task used with Guugu Yimithirr and Dutch speakers cannot reveal how people mentally represent space.
pub.passage: Speakers of Guugu Yimithirr, an Aboriginal language of northeastern Australia, describe locations almost entirely with cardinal directions, saying in effect "the cup is north of the plate" rather than "the cup is to the left of the plate." Some researchers have argued that such habits shape how speakers mentally encode space. In one well-known task, participants viewed a row of objects on a table, were turned 180 degrees to face a second table, and were asked to rebuild the row "the same way." Dutch speakers, whose language relies on left and right, usually kept the row's order relative to their own bodies, whereas Guugu Yimithirr speakers usually kept its compass orientation. Critics have noted, however, that the two groups also differed in setting: most Guugu Yimithirr participants lived in rural areas with strong outdoor landmarks, while the Dutch participants were mostly city dwellers tested indoors. Later studies that compared speakers of different languages living in the same environment have found that language still predicts which strategy people choose, although environment influences that choice too.

advisory.note: Levinson 연구를 바탕으로 새로 쓴 지문이다. 정답 A는 마지막 문장(같은 환경에서도 언어가 전략을 예측하고, 환경도 영향을 준다)과 잘 맞는다. A의 '환경을 고려한 후에도'라는 표현은 지문을 정확하게 바꿔 말한 것이다. B는 비판 단락만 훑어 읽은 사람을 노린 매력적인 오답이고, C와 D도 그럴듯하다. 중간 난이도에 맞다.

pub.answer_rationale: Text 1은 임금격차를 이전의 결정적 요인으로 지목하며 운송 여건이 갖춰지자 이전이 일어났다고 설명하지만, Text 2는 임금격차 자체는 수십 년 전부터 있었다는 시간적 반박을 제기하므로, Text 1의 논리대로라면 왜 더 일찍 이전이 일어나지 않았는지에 대한 질문에 부딪히게 된다.
pub.evidence_span: This wage gap, more than any single technological or managerial difference, explains why textile production migrated southward so rapidly once interstate transportation made the shift logistically feasible for manufacturers seeking to preserve their profit margins.
pub.evidence_target: Text 2는 임금격차가 수십 년간 존재했음에도 이전이 특정 시기에 집중된 점을 지적함으로써, Text 1이 임금격차를 이전의 결정적 요인으로 제시하는 논리에 시간적 공백이 있음을 드러낸다.
pub.explanation:
Text 2의 핵심 반박은 임금격차가 '틀렸다'는 것이 아니라, 임금격차가 수십 년간 존재했음에도 남부로의 이전이 20세기 중반에 집중되었다는 '시기(timing)' 문제를 임금격차만으로는 설명할 수 없다는 것이다. Text 1은 임금격차를 이전의 결정적 요인으로 제시하면서 운송 여건이 갖춰지자 이전이 일어났다고 설명하지만, 이는 왜 임금격차가 이미 존재하던 더 이른 시기가 아니라 하필 그 시점에 이전이 일어났는지에 답하지 못한다. 따라서 Text 1의 저자는 이 시기 문제에 직접 답하기보다, 자신의 논리 구조상 이 질문(왜 더 일찍 이전이 없었는가)에 부딪히게 될 가능성이 높다. 이는 C(정답, 인덱스 2)에 해당한다.

A(인덱스 0)는 Text 1이 운송 여건을 언급한다는 사실은 맞지만, 마치 Text 1 저자가 자신의 주장을 양보하며 장비 격차가 주된 원인이라고 인정하는 것처럼 화자의 입장을 뒤바꿔 서술하여 틀렸다.
B(인덱스 1)는 임금격차가 수십 년간 지속되었다는 사실을 인용하지만, 이를 오히려 임금격차가 '지속성' 때문에 원인이라는 인과관계로 뒤집어 사용하여 틀렸다 — 실제로는 이 지속성이 임금격차 설명에 대한 반박 근거다.
D(인덱스 3)는 Text 2의 장비 주장과 임금을 연결 지으려 하지만, 지문에 없는 '비노조 임금이 자본을 확보해 장비 도입을 가능케 했다'는 근거 없는 결합을 만들어내어 틀렸다.

따라서 정답은 C다.
pub.explanation_en:
The key rebuttal in Text 2 is not that the wage differential is "wrong," but that, because the wage differential existed for decades yet the relocation to the South was concentrated in the mid-20th century, the wage differential alone cannot explain the timing. Text 1 presents the wage differential as the decisive factor in relocation and explains that relocation occurred once transportation conditions were in place, but this does not answer why relocation happened at that time rather than in an earlier period when the wage differential already existed. So the author of Text 1 is likely to run into this question (why there was no earlier relocation) given the structure of the argument, rather than answering the timing issue directly. This corresponds to C (the answer, index 2).

A (index 0) is correct that Text 1 mentions transportation conditions, but it is wrong because it reverses the author's position, as if the author of Text 1 conceded that the equipment gap was the main cause.
B (index 1) cites the fact that the wage differential lasted for decades but is wrong because it flips this into a causal argument that the differential is a cause because of its persistence; in fact this persistence is the rebuttal to the wage-differential explanation.
D (index 3) tries to link Text 2's equipment claim with wages but is wrong because it creates an unsupported combination not in the text, that non-union wages freed up capital to allow equipment adoption.

Therefore the answer is C.
options: The author would concede that equipment differences were the primary cause but would maintain that wages made relocation logistically feasible.
The author would argue that the wage gap had existed for decades, so its persistence, rather than any change in equipment, best explains the shift.
The author would likely question why the wage gap alone did not cause relocation earlier, since Text 1 treats it as the decisive factor throughout the period.
The author would agree that newer machinery mattered but would insist that Southern mills only installed it because non-union wages freed up capital.
pub.passage:
Text 1

Economic historians examining the decline of the New England textile mills in the mid-twentieth century have generally emphasized labor costs as the decisive factor. Southern mills paid workers substantially less and operated free of the union contracts that had become standard in the Northeast, allowing them to undercut Northern producers on price even when shipping finished goods back to the same national markets. This wage gap, more than any single technological or managerial difference, explains why textile production migrated southward so rapidly once interstate transportation made the shift logistically feasible for manufacturers seeking to preserve their profit margins.

Text 2

Wage differentials alone cannot account for the timing of the textile industry's southward shift, since the gap between Northern and Southern labor costs had existed for decades before mills began relocating in large numbers. What changed in the mid-twentieth century was the introduction of newer, more efficient machinery that Southern mills, built later and free of investment in older equipment, adopted far more readily than Northern mills burdened by aging infrastructure. It was this gap in equipment, not wages, that ultimately determined which region's mills could compete profitably.

pub.explanation: 빈칸 앞 'Manchester's Free Library ... quickly attracted mill workers'는 긴 비필수 삽입절을 지나 완성된 독립절이고, 뒤의 'many of them had never ... fee'도 독립절이다. 두 독립절은 세미콜론으로 연결하고, 접속부사 indeed는 두 번째 절 앞에 두고 쉼표를 붙이는 A가 옳다. B와 D는 쉼표와 접속부사만으로 두 독립절을 이어 comma splice가 된다. C는 세미콜론 위치는 맞아 보이지만 indeed를 첫 절 끝에 붙여 의미상 '정말로 노동자들을 끌어들였다'처럼 어색해지고, 뒤 절과의 강조 관계가 사라지며 관례적인 접속부사 위치에도 어긋난다.
pub.explanation_en: The text before the blank, "Manchester's Free Library ... quickly attracted mill workers," is a complete independent clause once you skip past the long nonessential clause in the middle. What follows, "many of them had never ... fee," is also an independent clause. Two independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon, and the transition "indeed" belongs at the start of the second clause, followed by a comma, so A is correct. B and D join the two clauses with only a comma and a transition, which creates a comma splice. C does put a semicolon between the clauses, but it attaches "indeed" to the end of the first clause, so the word no longer introduces the second clause as the stronger point, and that placement breaks the usual way a transition is used.
options: workers; indeed,
workers, indeed,
workers indeed
workers, indeed

advisory.note: 독립절 판별(긴 삽입절 통과)과 접속부사 위치 판단의 두 단계가 필요함. B·D는 comma splice, C는 위치 함정으로 오답이 그럴듯함. 맨체스터 무료도서관 1852년 개관은 사실과 맞음.

hardJudge.note: 정답 A는 명확히 옳고(두 독립절 + 세미콜론 + 접속부사 indeed + 쉼표), B·D는 comma splice로 확실히 배제된다. 그러나 C는 구두점 관례상 위반이 없어(세미콜론이 두 독립절을 적법하게 연결) '관례 준수' 문항 기준으로는 방어 가능한 선택지가 되어 정답 유일성이 약하다. 표준 SAT는 이런 경우 보통 'workers indeed,'처럼 쉼표 오류를 포함시켜 배제 근거를 문법으로 만든다. 문항 자체는 긴 삽입절을 지나 독립절을 판별하는 두 단계 판단을 요구해 medium에 부합하나, C의 문법적 허용 가능성은 출제 결함으로 기록한다.

pub.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

pub.answer_rationale: A는 분사구(현재분사구) 뒤에 콤마를 두어 이어지는 독립절 "she was able to document..."과 자연스럽게 연결되는 수식어구를 만든다.
pub.evidence_span: ______ she was able to document how the organisms' light patterns shifted
pub.explanation: 빈칸 뒤에는 "she was able to document..."라는 완전한 독립절이 이어진다. 따라서 빈칸은 이 절을 수식하는 분사구(-ing로 시작하는 수식어구)여야 하고, 분사구 끝에는 콤마가 필요하다. B는 이 조건을 만족한다. A는 "cameras"와 "that" 사이에 불필요한 콤마를 넣어 제한적 관계절을 잘못 끊는다. C는 분사구 뒤에 콤마가 없어 뒤 독립절과의 경계가 불분명해진다. D는 독립절 "She used ... darkness,"와 독립절 "she was able to document ..."를 접속사 없이 콤마만으로 이어 콤마 스플라이스가 된다. 따라서 정답은 B이다.
pub.explanation_en: After the blank comes a complete independent clause, "she was able to document...". The blank must therefore be a participial phrase (beginning with -ing) that modifies this clause, and a comma is needed at the end of the phrase. B satisfies this condition. A inserts an unnecessary comma between "cameras" and "that," wrongly breaking a restrictive relative clause. C has no comma after the participial phrase, so the boundary with the independent clause that follows is unclear. D joins two independent clauses, "She used ... darkness," and "she was able to document ...," with only a comma, which is a comma splice. So the answer is B.
options: Using specialized underwater cameras, that could capture faint light in near-total darkness,
Using specialized underwater cameras that could capture faint light in near-total darkness,
Using specialized underwater cameras that could capture faint light in near-total darkness
She used specialized underwater cameras that could capture faint light in near-total darkness,

Her findings suggested that even slight warming could disrupt the predator-avoidance signals these plankton rely on to survive.

difficultyReasons: 분사구문과 콤마 사용 규칙을 정확히 알아야 함(1~2단계 추론)
오답들이 정답과 어휘·구조를 거의 동일하게 공유하여 콤마 유무, 문장 완결성 차이만으로 구분해야 함
분사구문 뒤 콤마 필요성과 관계절 앞 불필요한 콤마 구분이라는 두 가지 구두점 규칙을 동시에 적용해야 함
D 선택지는 완전한 절 구조라 분사구문 규칙이 아닌 접속사 사용의 적절성을 별도로 판단해야 하므로 사고 전환이 필요함

distractors.matches: 동일한 어휘와 구조(Using specialized underwater cameras... faint light in near-total darkness)
distractors.plausibleBecause: 거의 정답과 동일한 문구이며 관계절 앞 콤마 삽입이 미묘한 오류라 눈에 잘 띄지 않는다
distractors.whyWrong: 'that'으로 시작하는 필수적 관계절(제한적 수식어) 앞에 콤마를 찍으면 안 되는데 콤마가 삽입되어 있어 구두점 오류가 발생한다

distractors.matches: 동일한 분사구문 내용
distractors.plausibleBecause: 분사구문 뒤에 콤마가 없어도 얼핏 보면 문법적으로 문제없어 보일 수 있다
distractors.whyWrong: 분사구문(Using...) 뒤에는 주절과 구분하는 콤마가 필요한데 콤마가 빠져 있어 두 절이 붙어버리는 구두점 오류이다

distractors.matches: 주어 'She'와 동사 'used'가 원문 주어(she)와 연결되어 자연스러워 보임
distractors.plausibleBecause: 완전한 절(She used...)로 시작하여 문법적으로 완결된 문장처럼 보이고, 뒤에 and로 다음 문장과 연결하려는 시도가 그럴듯해 보인다
distractors.whyWrong: 'and'로 연결하면 이어지는 절 'she was able to document...'와 문법적으로 어색하게 결합되어 두 개의 독립절이 부적절하게 이어지거나 구조가 어긋나며, 원래 문장의 분사구문 구조(현재분사로 시작해 주절 'she was able to document'로 이어지는 구조)를 깨뜨려 문장 전체가 비문이 된다

pub.question: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

pub.answer_rationale: 황화수소 농도는 정상이고 헤모글로빈 기능도 정상인데 박테리아만 고갈되면 성장이 완전히 멈춘다는 것은, 헤모글로빈의 운반 기능이나 황화수소 자체가 아니라 박테리아의 대사(화학합성) 산물이 성장의 필수 조건임을 보여준다.
pub.evidence_span: worms transplanted to water with normal hydrogen sulfide levels but experimentally depleted bacterial populations stop growing entirely, even though their hemoglobin continues to bind oxygen and carbon dioxide normally
pub.evidence_target: Riftia의 급속한 성장과 생존은 트로포솜 내 박테리아가 화학합성으로 만들어내는 유기 화합물 공급에 전적으로 의존한다.
pub.explanation:
지문은 Riftia가 소화관 없이 빠르게 자라는 역설을 제시하고, 그 원인을 트로포솜 속 박테리아와 헤모글로빈의 협력 관계로 설명한다. 결정적 단서는 실험 결과다: 황화수소 농도가 정상이고 헤모글로빈이 산소·이산화탄소를 정상적으로 결합하는데도, 박테리아 개체수만 고갈되면 성장이 완전히 멈춘다. 이는 헤모글로빈의 운반 기능 자체가 성장의 직접 원인이 아니라, 박테리아가 이 물질들로 화학합성을 통해 만들어내는 유기 화합물(대사 산물)이 성장의 필수 요건이라는 것을 보여준다. 소화관이 전혀 없다는 사실과 결합하면 답은 A이다.
B는 포식자 감지·플룸 수축이라는 지문 속 실제 세부사항을 가져왔지만 이는 성장·영양 공급과는 무관한 지엽적 내용(IRRELEVANT_DETAIL)이다.
C는 헤모글로빈이 산소·이산화탄소를 결합하는 기능을 정확히 언급하지만, 실험 결과가 정확히 반박하듯 이 기능만으로는 성장이 유지되지 않으므로 헤모글로빈의 역할을 성장의 핵심 원인으로 과도하게 확장(OVERREACH)한 오답이다.
D는 트로포솜이 박테리아를 담고 있다는 사실은 맞지만, 트로포솜의 실제 기능은 화학합성 산물을 흡수하는 것이지 포식자로부터 박테리아를 보호하는 것이 아니므로, 트로포솜의 역할 범위를 잘못 설정한 오답(WRONG_SCOPE)이다.
pub.explanation_en:
The passage presents the paradox that Riftia grows quickly without a digestive tract and explains the cause as a cooperative relationship between the bacteria in the trophosome and hemoglobin. The decisive clue is the experimental result: even when hydrogen sulfide levels are normal and hemoglobin binds oxygen and carbon dioxide normally, growth stops completely once only the bacterial population is depleted. This shows that hemoglobin's transport function itself is not the direct cause of growth, but that the organic compounds (metabolic products) the bacteria make from these substances through chemosynthesis are essential for growth. Combined with the fact that the worm has no digestive tract at all, the answer is A.
B brings in a real detail from the passage, predator detection and plume retraction, but this is a peripheral detail unrelated to growth and nutrient supply (IRRELEVANT_DETAIL).
C correctly mentions hemoglobin's function of binding oxygen and carbon dioxide, but as the experimental result refutes, this function alone does not sustain growth, so it is a wrong answer that overextends hemoglobin's role as the key cause of growth (OVERREACH).
D is right that the trophosome houses the bacteria, but the trophosome's actual function is absorbing the products of chemosynthesis, not protecting the bacteria from predators, so it is a wrong answer that sets the scope of the trophosome's role incorrectly (WRONG_SCOPE).
options: the metabolic output of its internal bacterial symbionts, since the worm has no other means of acquiring nutrients
the plume's ability to remain extended into vent water long enough for hemoglobin to gather hydrogen sulfide, oxygen, and carbon dioxide for the bacteria to use
the hemoglobin's ability to bind oxygen and carbon dioxide even when hydrogen sulfide levels fluctuate near the vent
the trophosome tissue's ability to absorb the organic compounds that the bacteria synthesize, independent of the hemoglobin's role in supplying raw materials
pub.passage: In deep-sea hydrothermal vent ecosystems, tubeworms called Riftia pachyptila lack a mouth, gut, or anus as adults, yet they grow rapidly to lengths exceeding two meters. Biologists have found that the worms host billions of sulfur-oxidizing bacteria in a specialized internal organ called the trophosome, and that the worms possess unusually efficient hemoglobin capable of binding oxygen, hydrogen sulfide, and carbon dioxide simultaneously without the sulfide poisoning the worm's cells. This hemoglobin is concentrated in a dense plume of red tissue that the worm extends outside its protective tube into the surrounding vent water, retracting the plume instantly whenever a shadow or vibration signals a passing predator. The bacteria use the hydrogen sulfide delivered by this hemoglobin, along with oxygen and carbon dioxide, to synthesize organic compounds through chemosynthesis, and the worm absorbs these compounds directly through the trophosome tissue. Notably, worms transplanted to water with normal hydrogen sulfide levels but experimentally depleted bacterial populations stop growing entirely, even though their hemoglobin continues to bind oxygen and carbon dioxide normally. Given that Riftia has no digestive tract at all, researchers conclude that its rapid growth and survival depend entirely on ______

difficultyReasons: 정답을 고르기 위해 지문 전체(헤모글로빈, 박테리아, 트로포좀 간의 인과 사슬)를 종합해야 함
실험 결과(박테리아 제거 시 헤모글로빈 기능은 정상이나 성장 정지)를 통해 핵심 원인이 박테리아의 대사 산물임을 추론해야 함
오답 B(D)는 트로포좀의 흡수 기능이 헤모글로빈과 독립적이라는 미묘한 왜곡을 포함해 정답과 표면적으로 유사함
오답 C는 실험에서 명시된 사실(헤모글로빈 기능 정상)을 근거로 삼아 그럴듯하게 보이므로 구분이 필요함

distractors.matches: 플룸을 물속에 확장하고 그림자나 진동에 즉시 수축한다는 문장, 헤모글로빈이 세 물질을 동시에 결합한다는 문장
distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문에서 플룸이 즉시 수축하고 헤모글로빈이 세 가지 물질을 동시에 결합한다는 세부사항을 언급하므로, 플룸의 노출 지속 시간이 중요해 보일 수 있다
distractors.whyWrong: 플룸이 얼마나 오래 노출되는지는 지문에서 성장/생존의 핵심 원인으로 제시되지 않으며, 실험 결과(박테리아 제거 시 성장 정지)는 플룸 노출 시간이 아니라 박테리아의 대사 산물 부재가 원인임을 보여준다

distractors.matches: 실험에서 헤모글로빈이 산소와 이산화탄소를 계속 정상적으로 결합했다는 문장
distractors.plausibleBecause: 헤모글로빈이 실제로 산소와 이산화탄소를 정상적으로 결합한다는 문장이 실험 설명에 등장하므로 관련 있어 보인다
distractors.whyWrong: 이 능력이 정상적으로 유지되었음에도 박테리아가 없으면 성장이 멈췄다는 것이 핵심 논지이므로, 헤모글로빈의 결합 능력 자체는 성장의 원인이 아니라 오히려 원인이 아님을 보여주는 대조 정보이다

distractors.matches: 트로포좀 조직이 화합물을 직접 흡수한다는 문장
distractors.plausibleBecause: 트로포좀이 화합물을 흡수한다는 사실이 명시되어 있어 그럴듯해 보인다
distractors.whyWrong: 트로포좀의 흡수는 헤모글로빈이 공급한 원료를 박테리아가 화학합성한 산물을 흡수하는 것이므로 헤모글로빈의 역할과 독립적이라는 서술은 지문의 통합적 과정(헤모글로빈→박테리아→트로포좀)을 왜곡한다

issues: D 선택지에 대한 해설이 다소 부정확함: D의 실제 문제점은 '트로포솜이 포식자로부터 박테리아를 보호한다'는 내용이 아니라, 트로포솜의 흡수 기능을 헤모글로빈의 원료 공급 기능과 '독립적'이라고 잘못 서술한 점(실제로는 헤모글로빈이 원료를 공급해야 박테리아가 화합물을 합성하고, 트로포솜이 이를 흡수하는 연쇄적 과정이므로 독립적이지 않음)에 있음. 해설이 '포식자로부터 보호'라는, 선택지에 등장하지 않는 개념을 근거로 들어 다소 혼란을 줄 수 있음.
지문의 과학적 내용(리프티아 튜브웜의 무소화관 구조, 트로포솜 내 공생박테리아, 헤모글로빈의 다중 결합 능력)은 실제 생물학적 사실과 대체로 부합하나, '박테리아 개체수만 실험적으로 고갈시켰다'는 구체적 실험 설정은 가상의 상황으로 보이며 이는 추론 문제의 전제로 명시적으로 제시되어 있어 문제되지 않음.

pub.question: Which choice most logically completes the text?

pub.explanation: 봄이 되면서 Dario는 서류를 덜 자주 보여 주고 서류의 접힌 자국이 닳아 희미해지며, 이는 계획이 서서히 닳아 없어졌음을 보여 준다. 또 그는 아쉬워하지도 안도하지도 않고 오래전 코트를 떠올리듯 약간 놀랄 뿐이어서 의도적인 결정이 아니었음을 알 수 있다. 따라서 C가 정답이다. A는 한 번의 결정을 말해 점진성과 어긋나고, B는 직장 의무에 떠밀렸다는 근거가 없으며, D는 다시 꺼내 볼 계획이라는 단서가 없다.
pub.explanation_en: As spring arrives, Dario shows the papers less often and the folds in the papers wear faint, which shows that the plan wore away gradually. Also, he feels neither regret nor relief and is only slightly surprised, as if recalling a coat from long ago, so we can tell it was not a deliberate decision. Therefore, C is the answer. A speaks of a single decision, which conflicts with the gradual process, B has no basis for saying he was pushed aside by work obligations, and D has no clue that he would revisit the plan.
options: his plans had been abandoned in a single decision he preferred not to discuss.
his plans had been washed away by obligations he had not anticipated at work.
his former intention had worn away gradually without any deliberate choice.
his former intention had been set aside so that it could be revisited later.
pub.passage: Dario hung his uniforms on the rooftop line every morning at six, after our night shift at the bakery in Oaxaca, and I, Tendai, hung mine beside his. For months he had talked of quitting to drive a taxi with his cousin; he kept the license forms folded in his wallet and showed them to anyone who asked. That spring he showed them less often, and when he did, the creases had gone soft and gray. One morning I noticed he had begun pinning a second apron to the line, the white one the head baker gave only to those training for the ovens. He did not mention it, and neither did I. Weeks later, when I finally asked about the taxi, he shrugged and said his plans had gone out with the wash. He seemed neither sorry nor relieved, only mildly surprised, as though remembering a coat he had once owned. Below us the street vendors were unfolding their umbrellas, one stripe at a time.

pub.evidence_span: Painters in provincial workshops, far from imitating fashionable urban patrons, appear to have adopted these techniques largely because the newly available materials simply made dramatic light effects easier and cheaper to produce reliably, regardless of who was commissioning the work.
pub.evidence_target: Text 2는 Text 1이 제시한 '지방 화가의 후원자 취향 모방' 설명을 재료(안료·매체)의 보급이라는 대안적 원인으로 반박한다.
pub.explanation: Text 1은 부유한 후원자들의 취향을 모방하여 치오스쿠로가 도시에서 지방으로 확산되었다고 설명한다. Text 2는 이 시기에 안정적인 어두운 안료와 개선된 유화 매체가 더 저렴하게 보급되었다는 점을 근거로, 지방 화가들이 후원자를 모방한 것이 아니라 재료 자체가 극적인 명암 효과를 쉽고 싸게 만들었기 때문에 이 기법을 채택했다고 반박한다. 따라서 정답은 A번이다.
pub.explanation_en: Text 1 explains that chiaroscuro spread from the cities to the provinces by imitating the tastes of wealthy patrons. Text 2, citing the wider and cheaper availability in this period of stable dark pigments and improved oil mediums, argues against this: provincial painters adopted the technique not by imitating patrons but because the materials themselves made dramatic light-and-shadow effects easy and cheap to produce. Therefore, the answer is A.
options: The author would contend that provincial painters adopted dramatic light and shadow effects because newly affordable, stable pigments and mediums made the technique easier to produce, not because they were imitating urban patrons.
The author would agree that patron taste was the decisive factor, while adding that material improvements played only a minor supporting role in the process.

The author would maintain that both explanations are equally valid, since material advances and patrons' preference for the new style emerged together and reinforced one another in spreading the technique.
The author would claim that wealthy urban patrons rejected chiaroscuro and that only provincial painters embraced it independently of any material changes.
pub.passage:
Text 1

Art historians examining the sudden popularity of chiaroscuro—the dramatic use of light and shadow—in seventeenth-century European painting often attribute the technique's rise to the influence of a small circle of innovative painters whose bold canvases circulated among wealthy patrons in major cities. According to this view, once influential collectors began commissioning works featuring stark contrasts of illumination, provincial painters imitated the style to attract similarly prestigious clients, and the technique spread outward from urban centers of artistic patronage to the wider continent within a few decades.

Text 2

The patronage-driven account of chiaroscuro's spread overlooks a simpler explanation rooted in materials rather than taste. Analysis of surviving pigments and canvases shows that this same period saw the wider availability of more affordable, stable dark pigments capable of rendering deep shadow without cracking or fading, alongside improved oil-based mediums that allowed for more precise gradations of light. Painters in provincial workshops, far from imitating fashionable urban patrons, appear to have adopted these techniques largely because the newly available materials simply made dramatic light effects easier and cheaper to produce reliably, regardless of who was commissioning the work.

difficultyReasons: 두 지문의 인과관계(취향 대 재료)를 정확히 대조해야 함
Text2의 명시적 반박 어조와 대안 설명을 종합적으로 이해해야 함
선택지 C가 그럴듯한 절충안을 제시해 미묘한 구분 필요

distractors.matches: Text 2가 material improvements를 언급한다는 점
distractors.plausibleBecause: Text 2가 material factor를 언급하니 patron taste도 일부 인정한다고 오해할 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: Text 2는 patronage 설명을 'overlooks'라며 대체 설명으로 제시하지, patron taste를 결정적 요인으로 인정하지 않음

distractors.matches: 두 요인이 같은 시기에 존재했다는 점
distractors.plausibleBecause: 두 지문 모두 그럴듯한 설명을 제공하므로 학생이 절충안을 정답으로 볼 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: Text 2는 명시적으로 patronage 설명이 'overlooks a simpler explanation'이라고 하며 material 설명이 우선한다고 주장, 동등하다고 하지 않음

distractors.matches: 'regardless of who was commissioning the work'라는 문구
distractors.plausibleBecause: Text 2가 patron 관련성을 부정하는 뉘앙스가 있어 극단적으로 해석할 수 있음
distractors.whyWrong: Text 2는 patron들이 chiaroscuro를 거부했다고 말하지 않으며, 단지 patron의 취향이 원인이 아니라고 할 뿐임

pub.question: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1's explanation that chiaroscuro spread because provincial painters imitated urban patrons' tastes?

pub.answer_rationale: 학생의 목표는 개발업자가 버스보다 철도 노선 근처에 투자를 선호하는 이유를 설명하는 것이므로, 철도의 영구성이 투자를 유치한다는 정보를 담은 선택지가 목표를 정확히 달성한다.
pub.evidence_span: Fixed rail lines tend to attract more private real estate investment near stations because developers view rail infrastructure as a permanent commitment to a corridor.
pub.evidence_target: 다섯 번째 메모(고정 철도 인프라가 영구성을 신호하여 투자 유치)
pub.explanation: 학생의 목표는 개발업자가 철도 근처를 선호하는 '이유'를 설명하는 것이다. 다섯 번째 메모가 고정 철도 인프라의 영구성이 투자를 유치한다고 명시하므로 C가 정답이다. A는 버스의 유연성에 대한 내용으로 개발업자의 선호 이유와 무관하다(목표를 무시함). B는 BRT 시스템 설명으로, 개발업자의 투자 선호와 직접 관련된 정보가 아니라 다른 메모 내용을 잘못 결합한 것이다. D는 승객 수 증가에 관한 통계로, 개발업자의 투자 동기(영구성)와는 다른 메모 하나만 사용한 것이다.
pub.explanation_en: The student's goal is to explain 'why' developers prefer to invest near rail lines. The fifth note states that the permanence of fixed rail infrastructure attracts investment, so C is the answer. A is about the flexibility of buses and is unrelated to why developers prefer rail (it ignores the goal). B describes BRT systems and is a wrong answer that wrongly combines other note content rather than information directly related to developers' investment preferences. D is a statistic about ridership increases and uses a different single note rather than the developers' investment motive (permanence).
options: Because buses can be rerouted quickly in response to construction or changing demand, developers may prefer bus routes for their adaptability to shifting urban needs.
Bus rapid transit systems often lack the permanence signal of rail, which means they typically fail to attract the same level of private real estate investment as standard bus routes do.
Developers tend to favor rail infrastructure because its fixed, permanent nature signals a long-term commitment to a given corridor.
A 2015 study found that light rail systems increased ridership by 15% within five years compared to bus-only corridors.
pub.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In the 1960s, urban planners in several U.S. cities began replacing streetcar lines with bus routes, arguing that buses offered greater route flexibility.
- Streetcars require fixed tracks and overhead wires, which are expensive to install and maintain but tend to have longer operational lifespans than buses.
- A 2015 study found that cities with light rail systems, a modern successor to streetcars, saw a 15% increase in ridership within five years of construction compared to comparable bus-only corridors.
- Buses can be rerouted quickly in response to construction, accidents, or changing demand, without the need for costly infrastructure changes.
- Fixed rail lines tend to attract more private real estate investment near stations because developers view rail infrastructure as a permanent commitment to a corridor.
- Bus rapid transit (BRT) systems attempt to combine rail-like dedicated lanes with the flexibility of buses, though they often lack the permanence signal that attracts investment.

difficultyReasons: 질문의 핵심 관계(영속성 신호→투자 유치)를 노트에서 직접 찾아 매칭하는 1단계 추론
오답 A는 방향이 반대라 쉽게 제거 가능
오답 B, D는 관련 정보이지만 질문의 초점(철도 vs 버스, 투자 이유)과 어긋나 약간의 검토가 필요
전체적으로 선택지 간 정보 공유가 크지 않아 난이도는 중간 이하

distractors.matches: 버스는 공사, 사고, 수요 변화에 빠르게 재배치될 수 있다는 노트 내용과 일치
distractors.plausibleBecause: 지문에 실제로 있는 사실(버스의 신속한 노선 변경 유연성)을 언급하여 그럴듯해 보인다
distractors.whyWrong: 질문은 개발자가 왜 철도 노선 근처를 선호하는지를 묻는데, 이 선택지는 반대로 개발자가 버스 노선을 선호할 이유(유연성)를 설명하므로 질문의 목적과 반대 방향이다

distractors.matches: BRT는 영속성 신호가 부족해 투자를 끌어들이지 못한다는 노트 내용과 일치
distractors.plausibleBecause: BRT와 영속성 신호 부족이라는 노트 내용을 사용하여 관련 있어 보인다
distractors.whyWrong: BRT가 일반 버스 노선보다 투자를 덜 끌어들인다는 비교를 잘못 설정했고, 노트는 BRT를 표준 버스와 비교한 것이 아니라 철도와 비교했으며, 질문은 철도 대 버스 선호 이유를 묻는데 BRT라는 다른 범주를 끌어들여 초점을 벗어난다

distractors.matches: 2015년 연구에서 경전철이 버스 전용 노선보다 승차율이 15% 증가했다는 노트 내용과 일치
distractors.plausibleBecause: 철도 관련 통계 자료를 인용하여 관련성이 있어 보인다
distractors.whyWrong: 이 정보는 승차율(ridership) 증가에 관한 것이지 부동산 개발자의 투자 선호 이유(영속성 신호)와는 직접 관련이 없어 질문의 목적을 달성하지 못한다
